news.abstract: 100 strictly Orthodox yeshiva students, in ugly confrontation, surround group of American Reform rabbis seeking to pray at Western Wall, Jerusalem, booing loudly and hurling insults past officers from border police; clash is latest skirmish in war between Orthodox and Reform and Conservative movements, which many fundamentalists believe to be such dilution of Judaism that they are not same religion at all; photo (M)
news.title: Orthodox Confront U.S. Reform Rabbis at Western Wall

news.abstract: PARIS—  France is undertaking an active campaign to strengthen multilateral institutions as part of an effort to define the United States' potential for unilateral action as one of the world's great worries. It is, in effect, an attempt to limit American power and to convince other countries that they should work together to contain it.
news.title: So Paris Begins a Campaign to Strengthen Multilateral Institutions : Going It Alone, U.S. Upsets France

news.abstract: Hugo Chavez is inaugurated as President of Venezuela, and promises peaceful revolution to remove 'cancer' of corruption; photo; emotional two-hour address describes country 'rotting to the core' as 'social time bomb' of hunger, disease and malnutrition ticks away; reassures business leaders and foreign investors by promising to attack budget deficit, support regional currency and use military for antipoverty efforts such as road-building; calls for referendum to rewrite Constitution to remove judiciary from politics, add checks and balances and remove one-term limit for president; Fidel Castro attends, taking copious notes and embracing Chavez afterwards (S)
news.title: New Chief to Battle Venezuela's 'Cancer'

news.abstract: Edgar Bronfman Sr's reported wish to be buried amid Israel's great heroes prompts World Zionist Organization to consider whether Canadian billionaire, 69, might become first non-Israeli to be buried in Mount Herzl cemetery; Bronfman, leader in world Jewish causes, is quoted by biographer Michael Shashar as saying burial in Mount Herzl would prove he was 'real mensch'; his photo (S)
news.title: Israelis Debate Burying Bronfman Among Heroes

news.abstract: Japanese accustomed to lifetime employment are shocked by layoffs stemming from deep economic woes; Japan's 4.1 percent unemployment rate strikes blow to country's self-image and to social contract that has kept public complacent and one party in power for decades; jobless battle shame and despair, as well as challenge of finding work, and humiliation is even flaring into rare public anger; Takaharu Akimoto recalls disbelief at being asked to resign, seven years short of retirement; he is among older, higher-paid workers with particular problems finding new jobs; photo; graph; Government is going to great lengths to keep jobless figures from rising, providing generous subsidies to companies to keep workers (M)
news.title: In Japan, From a Lifetime Job to No Job at All

news.abstract: Nigeria's military, which has ruled Africa's most populous nation for many years, suffers setbacks that have unsettled many old soldiers who live in Kaduna; photos of polo club, British institution introduced in 1904; map (Kaduna Journal) (S)
news.title: Kaduna Journal; If Army Can't Play Politics, There's Always Polo

news.abstract: Newly-installed Pres Hugo Chavez Frias sends tremors through political establishment by moving to rewrite Venezuelan Constitution; process would likely replace newly elected Congress with one that has more of his allies; Chavez and his supporters see 1961 Constitution as symbol of corrupt political system that has fed popular resentment and apathy; it was written to keep Marxist groups then aligned with Cuban-backed guerrillas out of potlical process; coalition that helped elect Chavez contains Marxist and socialist groups who sorely want to replace that document (M)
news.title: New President in Venezuela Proposes to Rewrite the Constitution

news.abstract: Astronauts aboard Russian space station Mir will attempt to bounce sunlight off 82-foot mirror and direct rays toward ground, producing beams up to 10 times brighter than full moon; astronomers are protesting experiment, saying such developments threaten to produce new kinds of light pollution that could blind telescopes exploring night sky; diagrams (M)
news.title: Space-Based Mirror May Light Skies Tonight

news.abstract: British commentators are mining Shakespeare and Greek tragedies to come up with parallels for fall of Jonathan Aitken, high-born former Cabinet minister who has admitted committing perjury during libel case; his marriage and his fortune are gone, and his likely future is in prison; photo (M)
news.title: London Journal; A Right Honorable Briton? Hardly, It Turns Out

news.abstract: Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso of Brazil may face more fractious second term as raft of newly elected members of Congress switch parties just before taking office; some deputies leave ruling party to join smaller party in which they could hold more sway; they promise more critical stance twward Cardoso's proposals; several legislators have left Cardoso's party for party of Itamar Franco, Governor of their state, who is in middle of battle of nerves with Cardoso regarding his state's debt to Federal Government (M)
news.title: Legislators In Brazil Are Leaving Ruling Party

news.abstract: John S Service, first of China experts purged from State Department in McCarthy era, dies at age 89; photos (M)
news.title: John Service, a Purged 'China Hand,' Dies at 89

news.abstract: PARIS—  Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine says that he now defines the United States as a "hyperpower," a new term that he thinks best describes "a country that is dominant or predominant in all categories."
news.title: To Paris, U.S. Looks Like a 'Hyperpower'

news.abstract: Salman Rushdie is granted visa to return to India, his native land; country's banning of his novel The Satanic Verses in 1988 began chain of events that led to death threats by offended Muslims and a life in hiding; decision to allow Rushdie to return is made in highest reaches of Indian Government, but various Muslim leaders protest and make veiled threats about his safety if he does return (M)
news.title: India Gives Rushdie a Visa to Return, and Muslims Quickly Warn of Protests

news.abstract: ALOR GAJAH, Malaysia—  It has been 18 months since Haris Aziz and his family began hearing the words "economic crisis" and by now one might have expected them to be feeling the pinch.
news.title: Average Malaysians Ask:'What Crisis?'

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: PINOCHET HEARINGS END -- The House of Lords concluded 12 days of hearings to determine whether Gen. Augusto Pinochet, the former Chilean dictator, is immune from arrest and extradition to Spain on charges of torture, kidnapping and murder. Lord Browne-Wilkinson, chairman of the seven-member Law Lords, Britain's highest court, gave no clear indication of when a decision would be announced.   Alan Cowell (NYT)    RUSSIA: INQUIRY ON TYCOON WIDENS -- An investigation of the financier Boris A. Berezovsky has been widened to include Aeroflot, in which he had a stake. Those being questioned include the former Defense Minister Yevgeny Shaposhnikov; when he was head of Aeroflot, he directed the airline to channel hard-currency earnings to a Swiss company half-owned by Mr. Berezovsky, the newspaper Moskovsky Komsomolets reported.   Celestine Bohlen (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: American lawyer Edward Fagan says two Austrian banks he represents are circulating proposal that could settle Holocaust-era claims against them; banks are Bank Austria and Creditanstalt (S)
news.title: Austria Banks' Plan On Holocaust Funds

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  - The maker of BMW autos announced the departures of its two top executives Friday in a rare German boardroom revolt that analysts said was triggered by heavy losses at the company's British Rover auto-making subsidiary.
news.title: Board Ousts BMW Chief and His Heir

news.abstract: Muslim religion sanctions use of life support to keep a patient alive as long as there is some hope of revival, but once death is inevitable the faithful believe that the family should accept God's will and not keep organs functioning artificially (S)
news.title: In Islam, Brain Death Ends Life Support

news.abstract: Changing of the guard across that Arab world is heralded by the impending death of King Hussein of Jordan; most Arab rulers are aging, and several are ill, and in some places the path of succession remains uncertain (M)
news.title: News Analysis; Old Order Changes

news.abstract: Four members of an Irish Republican Army gang are sentenced in Dublin to terms of 11 to 14 years for killing Gerry McCabe, an Irish detective, during robbery of a bank van in Adare, Ireland, in 1996; outrage is voiced in many quarters over decision by prosecutors to drop charges from murder and manslaughter, which they did because crucial witnesses had been intimidated and refused to repeat in court what they had told police (M)
news.title: 4 I.R.A. Gang Members Sentenced in Killing of Irish Detective

news.abstract: Reports that Turkish Government plans a third bridge over Bosporus sets off outpouring of civic protest in Istanbul's Arnavutkoy neighborhood, which has evidently been chosen as European terminus for the bridge; some opponents of the bridge say it would not ease traffic congestion, for which they blame poor access roads, and they are pushing for a rail tunnel under the Bosporus instead; photo; map (M)
news.title: Istanbul Journal; A New Bridge? Not in My Backyard!

news.abstract: Article on countless numbers of skilled Germans caught up in broad political battle over job protection and workplace flexibility in nation with some of strictest work rules in Europe, which have helped produce one of best-paid and most productive work forces in world; map (M)
news.title: With German Craft Rules, It's Hard Just to Get to Work

news.abstract: Dutch Parliament is investigating crash of El Al cargo plane into Amsterdam housing complex that killed 43 people on ground in Oct 1992; over 1,100 rescue workers and residents say they were somehow contaminated by burning aircraft, or its mysterious cargo; El Al in Oct 1998 revealed that cargo included vats of chemicals that can be used in manufacture of deadly nerve gas Sarin; investigation is expected to hear some 70 witnesses and last months more, drawing together reports of illness and allegations of cover-up by El Al and Dutch Government that have inflamed public passions in Amsterdam; photo (M)
news.title: 6 Years After Crash, Talk of Cover-Up

news.abstract: Crown Prince Abdullah of Jordan, appointed acting monarch by Jordanian Cabinet, faces as his first test internal political challenges rather than foreign affair crises; few analysts expect major political problems in first months of rule, but say he will be forced to move in short order to replace some members of current Cabinet, including unpopular Prime Min Fayez Tarawneh (M)
news.title: New Leader's First Test Lies in Internal Politics

news.abstract: Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, cancer from which King Hussein of Jordan lies near death, comes in many forms; while prognosis varies significantly according to type, any form can act unpredictably (M)
news.title: King's Nemesis Is an Unyielding Cancer

news.abstract: The Kosovo peace conference opened to exhortations from President Jacques Chirac of France that both sides put aside their differences. The start of the talks was delayed by Serbian maneuvering and the subsequent late arrival of the ethnic Albanian delegation.
news.title: Kosovo Talks Begin With Stern Warning

news.abstract: China, easing tensions with Walt Disney Co over Disney's backing of Kundun, film sympathetic to Dalai Lama, will allow theatrical release in China of film Mulan; Disney's efforts to regain China's favor noted (M)
news.title: Easing Tensions, Disney Gains O.K. to Show 'Mulan' in China

news.abstract: Mexico City reform government probe of Nov death in Mexico City of Frederick Mc Phail Jr has led to arrest and indictment of five police officers; authorities say officers forced him to drink entire bottle of liquor after they stole his bank card and looted his account; have identified dozen other people, including three foreign tourists, allegedly victimized by same rogue officers; Mc Phail's father, Frederick Sr, stirred public outrage over slaying with newspaper advertisements; he calls case example of rampant corruption and police violence, interview; photo (M)
news.title: Murder in Mexico: Reformers Uncover Police Plot

news.abstract: Ailing Pres Boris N Yeltsin signals he is still in command with plan to lead Russian delegation to funeral of Jordan's King Hussein; trip would be less demanding than diplomatic mission, give Yelsin chance to be seen with world leaders and let him upstage Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov (M)
news.title: Ailing Yeltsin May Go to Jordan To Show He Is Still in Command

news.abstract: Jordan's King Hussein, who has ruled Hashemite Kingdom since 1952, dies of cancer at age 63; his eldest son, Abdullah, 37, is crowned King; appears on television to console grieving nation; pledges to maintain father's legacy; names half-brother Hamzeh, 18, Crown Prince in gesture that should solidify ranks within royal family; Pres Clinton and other heads of state around world pay tribute to Hussein; Clinton and wife, Hillary, former Presidents Gerald Ford, Jimmy Carter and George Bush, British Prime Min Tony Blair, host of Arab leaders, including Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat, and Israeli delegation led by Pres Ezer Weizman and also including Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu and former Prime Mins Shimon Peres and Yitzhak Shamir will attend funeral; map; photos (M)
news.title: Hussein of Jordan, Voice for Peace, Dies

news.abstract: Ireland's 40,000 nomads, formerly disparagingly called tinkers, are now politely called travelers; most have given up horsecarts and covered wagons of their ancestors for car-towed trailers; still have hard time finding regular jobs or adequate campsites; 2,000 live in illegal camps that lack normal facilities; Government has ordered local councils to provide adequate facilities within next five years; map; photo (M)
news.title: Tullamore Journal; Travelers' Tale: Irish Nomads Make Little Headway

news.abstract: AFRICA    ETHIOPIA, ERITREA: CONFLICT WIDENS -- The border conflict between the two countries on the Horn of Africa widened to a second front, as Ethiopian warplanes attacked an Eritrean position near Tsorona. It was the first time that either side had used planes in battle since they agreed to halt air strikes in June. After an eight-month cease-fire, the two nations resumed fighting over the weekend.   Ian Fisher (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Thousands of grieving Jordanians throng funeral route in Amman to pay final respects to King Hussein; break through barricades into streets; scene described; photo (M)
news.title: Jordanians Grieve Over the Passing of a King, and Worry About the Future

news.abstract: Marius Schoon, opponent of apartheid who had been fighting amnesty application by police spy who killed Schoon's wife and daughter with mail bomb, dies at age 61; photo (M)
news.title: Marius Schoon, 61, Is Dead; Foe of Apartheid Lost Family

news.abstract: Donald Dewar, Britain's Secretary for Scotland, says first order of business when new Scottish Parliament convenes in May 1999 will be to reform ancient land-holding structure, under which half of Scottish land in private hands belongs to just 350 people, and 1,500 private estates account for 80 percent of country; under plans, local communities would gain right to buy estates at market value and be able to tap National Lottery money to help raise purchase price; purchase of 13-hamlets near Lochinvar from Swedish owner by residents, who set up Assynt Crofters' Trust cooperative self-government discussed; photos; map (M)
news.title: Lochinver Journal; At Long Last, Scots Can Lord It Over the Lairds

news.abstract: Left-of-center Party of the Democratic Revolution wins gubernatorial election in Baja California Sur and powerful office of Mayor in Mexico City; victories demonstrate continuing growth of party that has capitalized on dissension in governing Institutional Revolutionary Party (M)
news.title: Leftist Opposition Party in Mexico Wins Two Governors' Races

news.abstract: The German Government said today that it had agreed in principle to establish a  compensation fund, financed by the biggest names in German industry and banking, for victims of Nazi horrors.    The proposal, announced here today by a top aide to Germany's new chancellor, Gerhard Schroder, appears to be an effort to short-circuit a wave of lawsuits in American courts against German companies that made use of slave labor and forced labor during World War II, or profited from assets seized from Jews and other victims.
news.title: Germans Approve New Plan To Pay Holocaust Victims

news.abstract: A former executive of a manufacturer of precision instruments has been arrested in Japan for reportedly flouting laws that ban the sale to Communist countries of certain types of equipment that could be used to develop nuclear weapons.     The suspect, Isao Sasaki, who retired last year as senior managing director at Ryokosha K.K., an affiliate of the electronics giant Hitachi Ltd., was arrested on Saturday and charged with responsibility for selling telecomparators to China by way of South Korea. Telecomparators are measuring devices that are accurate to less than two-thousandths of a millimeter.
news.title: Japan Holds Executive in Sale Of Sensitive Machines to China

news.abstract: The F.B.I. tried to track suspected associates of Chilean leftists in the United States in the 1970's on behalf of the Government of Gen. Augusto Pinochet, the Chilean dictator, newly declassified documents show.    The Federal Bureau of Investigation sent agents in New York and Dallas to search for two people whose names were found in the address book of a courier for an underground Marxist group in Chile. The courier was arrested in Paraguay in 1975, and the Paraguayan police passed on the information to American officials, the records show.
news.title: F.B.I. Helped Chile Search For Leftists, Files Show

news.abstract: ASIA    INDIA: STATE LEADER QUITS -- The Chief Minister of Orissa State has submitted a letter of resignation, grudgingly taking ''moral responsibility'' for a recent spate of violence, including the killing of an Australian missionary and his two sons by Hindu militants. The Minister, Jayanti Ballabh Patnaik, gave the letter to his Congress Party leader, Sonia Gandhi.   Barry Bearak (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Thousands of Jordanians from desert camps, urban shacks and sleek modern villas made their way to the royal palace today to offer sympathy to King Abdullah and prayers for his late father, King Hussein.    Queen Noor, the widow of King Hussein, and other women in the royal family prayed separately for the first time at the King's grave.
news.title: Jordanians Pay Tribute to Late King and His Heir

news.abstract: American Civil Liberties Union and other American and Mexican human rights groups complain to Organization of American States that newly erected border fences and more vigorous enforcement by Border Patrol has spurred illegal immigrants to take dangerous routes to California through mountain passes and deserts, spurring surge in deaths; say Mexican diplomats have documented deaths of 360 immigrants along California border since 1994, when United States began crackdown (M)
news.title: Tough Controls Blamed for More Deaths on Border

news.abstract: Port officials say at least 280 people are feared to have drowned when ship, Harta Rimba, sank last weekend between the Indonesian islands of Borneo and Sumatra; say 19 people were rescued (S)
news.title: Indonesia Ship Sinks; 280 Feared Drowned

news.abstract: Hosts of Kosovo peace talks, Rambouillet, France, focus on their divisions; France and United States agree to compromise under which United Nations Security Council will be asked to 'endorse,' not 'authorize' deployment of NATO peacekeepers; more practical debate is over how quickly ethnic Albanian's Kosovo Liberation Army should be required to demobilize (M)
news.title: Trickiest Divides Are Among Big Powers at Kosovo Talks

news.abstract: Hong Kong court ruling that children born in mainland China to parents who are Hong Kong residents have right to live in Hong Kong stirs tensions between China and Hong Kong; judges used case to make broad statements about independence of Hong Kong's judiciary and about Hong Kong's autonomy in general; Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's chief executive, says he will send Justice Secretary to Beijing to discuss conflict; photo (M)
news.title: Immigration Ruling by Hong Kong Court Is Generating New Tensions With Beijing

news.abstract: Judge in corruption trial of Malaysia's ousted Deputy Prime Minister, Anwar Ibrahim, bars news media from publishing Anwar's court statements about Prime Min Mahathir Mohamad and Police Chief Abdul Rahim Noor; has rejected Anwar's charges of political conspiracy (M)
news.title: Judge Gags Press at Trial of Malaysia's Former Deputy Premier

news.abstract: An escalating conflict between religious and secular Jews is expected to spill into the streets here on Sunday when a mass prayer rally against the liberal Supreme Court faces a counter-rally by nonreligious Israelis who feel that democracy is under attack.    Political leaders worked unsuccessfully today to persuade religious leaders to cancel the prayer rally, which some feared could turn violent. By police prediction, at least 100,000 demonstrators are expected, a loose coalition against ''the judicial dictatorship'' including ultra-Orthodox Jews, religious Zionists and Jewish settlers from the West Bank.
news.title: Plans for Rival Rallies on Religion Issue Stir Fears in Israel

news.abstract: Roman Catholic officials in Asia and Rome say that Pope John Paul II is considering a visit to Hong Kong later this year; such a visit could soften decades-old standoff between Vatican and China's Communist Government, which has sovereignty over Hong Kong (M)
news.title: In Bid to Court China, Pope Weighs Visit To Hong Kong

news.abstract: The newspaper Haaretz reported today that Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres held secret talks with the P.L.O. in 1988, well before the 1993 Oslo accord, when they were in the Government of Yitzhak Shamir, the rightist Prime Minister from the Likud Party.     The unattributed account, apparently leaked by a participant in the talks, in Paris, said that Mr. Rabin and Mr. Peres negotiated when they were Defense and Foreign Ministers in Mr. Shamir's unity Government, composed of the Likud and Labor Parties.
news.title: Israelis Disclose '88 P.L.O. Talks

news.abstract: Directed by Fernando Trueba. Spain.
news.title: MOVIE GUIDE : La Nina de Tus Ojos

news.abstract: Gideon Rafael, a founder of the Israeli Foreign Ministry and one of its most accomplished and longest-serving diplomats, died on Wednesday in Jerusalem. He was 85.    In a career that began before Israel was established in 1948, Mr. Rafael negotiated with the Nazis to send Jews to Palestine, served at the United Nations and in Europe and conducted secret contacts with Arab countries.
news.title: Gideon Rafael, 85, a Founder of the Israeli Foreign Ministry

news.abstract: Fall of Terni, Italy, city government forces cancellation of most of Valentine celebrations in depressed mill town whose key attraction is shrine of St Valentine; city believes its patron saint, one of 17 Roman Catholic St Valentines, could have spawned modern and highly lucrative Valentine's Day cult; map; photo (M)
news.title: Terni Journal; Politics and Heartbreak In St. Valentine's Home

news.abstract: United Nations panel created to review Iraq's disarmament record and recommend ways of persuading Pres Saddam Hussein to honor commitment to abandon unconventional weapons is dominated by arms control experts from UN Special Commission whose inspections angered Iraq; Amb Celso L N Amorim of Brazil, who heads panel and two others, on humanitarian affairs, prisoners of war and Kuwaiti property, announces members of all three; arms panel does not include Special Commission head Richard Butler, but includes his deputy, Charles Duelfer; Amorim concedes Iraq has not yet agreed to cooperate with reviews; United States Amb Peter Burleigh lauds panel, interview (M)
news.title: New Iraq Panel Has Veterans of Arms Dispute

news.abstract: Clinton Administration says State Sec Madeleine K Albright will visit Kosovo peace conference, Rambouillet, France, to push delegates to forge military accords to end fighting; says she will propose internal security arrangements, including cut in Serbian troops and police forces, dissolution of ethnic Albanian rebel army and creation of new Kosovo police force; Serbian Pres Milan Milutinovic visits Serbian delegates; warns of guerrilla war if NATO bombs Serbia; photo (M)
news.title: Albright Due at Kosovo Talks to Push Pacts on Forces

news.abstract: Punta del Este, upscale Uruguayan beach resort, is feeling impact of Brazil's economic crisis; Brazilian tourists are cancelling and Argentinians cutting back on stays; some Argentinians are switching to Brazilian beach resorts, lured by Brazilian currency devaluation; city's elite fears slump will speed shift away from dependence on long summer rentals by Argentinians; weighs bid for American tourists; map (M)
news.title: Waves From Brazilian Economic Crisis Pound a Uruguayan Beach Resort

news.abstract: ASIA    CHINA: BID TO HEAL RIFT -- Hong Kong's Secretary of Justice, Elsie Leung, arrived in Beijing to try to work out a constitutional dispute with China over a recent court decision granting mainland residents with a parent in Hong Kong the free right of immigration. She warned that a quick solution was unlikely.   Elisabeth Rosenthal (NYT)    INDIA: STATE GOVERNMENT DISMISSED -- The Government won the President's permission to dismiss the government of the state of Bihar and impose central rule. The decision was prompted by a second round of killings of low-caste, landless people in just over two weeks by a private army sponsored by landlords in Bihar.   Celia Dugger (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Politics takes a turn toward farce in Vladivostok, far eastern Russian port, which has become an object lesson in how hard it can be to raise a democratic society out of ruins of Soviet empire; a power struggle is being waged by autocratic Governor of Primoriye region, Yevgeny Nazdratenko, and Viktor Cherepkov, the highly eccentric mayor of Vladivostok until he was ousted from office in December; Cherepkov claims extrasensory perception; Nazdratenko has received a mysterious $1 million prize for leadership from World Aristocratic Academy, an organization whose only known address is a post office box in the Bahamas; photos; map (M)
news.title: On Russia's Far East Fringe, Unrealpolitik

news.abstract: Transcript of Pres Clinton's radio address on US commitment to send troops to Kosovo
news.title: Clinton on Kosovo: 'We Can Make a Difference''

news.abstract: Mayalsian Central Bank briefs foreign fund managers on nation's investment outlook, saying its decision last September to impose strict controls on foreign investment have stablilized the country and put it on the road to recovery; asserts with delight that the disaster predicted by Internatinal Monetary Fund, US Treasury Department and other critics of capital controls have not occurred; says rules have since been relaxed and Malaysia is now ready for business; map; photo (M)
news.title: Malaysia Says Its Much-Criticized Financial Strategy Has Worked

news.abstract: Ireland's coalition Government faces possible collapse after Padraig Flynn, Ireland's member of European Commission, goes on television, jokes about how hard it is maintain his three houses on $150,000 a year and brushes aside questions about the $75,000 that he allegedly received from a Dublin entrepreneur in 1989; members of Parliament from Prime Min Bertie Ahern's Fianna Fail party approve resolution demanding that Flynn explain the affair (M)
news.title: Unabashed Politician's Statements Jeopardize Irish Government

news.abstract: Pres Clinton is not scheduled to meet with any opposition figures during visit to Mexico, and they charge that he is taking sides before presidential election in 2000 (M)
news.title: Mexico Opponents See Politics in Clinton Visit

news.abstract: SUBANG JAYA, Malaysia—  If it weren't for the students wandering the halls with books under their arms, one might be forgiven for thinking Taylor's College was the headquarters of a medium-sized corporation.
news.title: For-Profit Colleges Divide Malaysians

news.abstract: Poland is seeking central role in shaping financial fund being set up by German companies to compensate those who were forced laborers during World War II and other victims of Nazi horrors; Wieslaw Walendziak, chief of staff to Prime Min Jerzy Buzek, says approximately two million Poles were deported to Germany after Nazis invaded in 1939 and subsequently worked under prison-like conditions in German companies or on farms; estimates 520,000 currently live in Poland (S)
news.title: Poland Seeks Role in Fund for Nazi Forced Laborers

news.abstract: News analysis: while Pres Clinton's proposal to send American troops to Kosovo has heartened promoters of more active American role in preventing ethnic carnage, its has also aroused fears that Administration is marching into ancient swamp without clear idea how not to get mired in it; while stopping bloodshed is worthy objective in itself, doubts focus on whether Kosovo really touches on American national interests and whether Administration really knows what it is getting into, or how to get out of region notorious for instability and complexity (M)
news.title: Doubts on Kosovo

news.abstract: LONDON—  For generations, parents have sent their children to British boarding schools for an experience often described as "toughening up." But economic times and social attitudes have changed. These days, cold dormitories and colder showers are more likely to put off, rather than attract, prospective parents — not to mention their progeny. And the schools themselves have had to learn a hard lesson: adapt or die.
news.title: In Britain, Schools Repackage Softer Image

news.abstract: Election authorities in Mexico's Guerrero State declare Rene Juarez Cisneros, candidate of governing Institutional Revolutionary Party, winner of gubernatorial election; opposition angrily contests results, alleging irregularities in vote count (M)
news.title: Ruling Party In Mexico Wins Election For Governor

news.abstract: Broad shape of agreement to end ethnic conflict in Serbian province of Kosovo emerges, with Russia playing key role at talks in Rambouillet, France, to persuade Serbs to allow NATO peacekeepers on their territory; French Pres Jacques Chirac says Russians, traditional ally of Serbs, feel ground force in Kosovo is best solution to stopping bloodshed in separatist province and that Russian soldiers are likely to be part of deployment; photo (M)
news.title: Kosovo Peace Plan Takes Shape As Russia Prods Serbs on Troops

news.abstract: Ruling by Italian high court, that woman cannot be raped while wearing jeans since tightness makes them impossible to remove without her help, reopens angry national debate about rape and about how judges view sexual assault; group of female lawmakers is on open-ended 'jeans strike,' vowing to wear jeans to Parliament until decision is changed (M)
news.title: Ruling on Tight Jeans and Rape Sets Off Anger in Italy

news.abstract: Gen Olsegun Obasanjo, who earned international esteem by becoming Nigeria's first military ruler to give up power voluntary, wins nomination of country's leading political party as its presidential candidate; move sets stage for his return to position he held 20 years ago, but as democratically elected President; he vows to make Nigeria great again; photo (M)
news.title: Nigerian Ex-Ruler Captures Lead in Race for President

news.abstract: ASIA    HONG KONG: DEPORTATIONS BLOCKED -- A Hong Kong court has blocked the deportation of 18 mainland Chinese who contend that they have the right to residency under a landmark ruling by the territory's Court of Final Appeal. The decision may further inflame relations with China, which has said the ruling is a mistake that must be ''rectified.'' A Hong Kong spokesman said Beijing and Hong Kong had ''narrowed'' their areas of disagreement.    Mark Landler (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: French Pres Jacques Chirac, at upcoming meeting with Pres Clinton in Washington, will press Clinton on France's proposal to lift oil embargo against Iraq if it allows resumption of international inspections of its weapons programs (S)
news.title: French Chief Will Press Plan on Iraq With Clinton

news.abstract: Protestors enraged by capture of Abdullah Ocalan, foremost Kurd rebel leader, storm diplomatic posts throughout Europe and elsewhere, taking hostages and setting fires; Kurds in Paris, London, Moscow, Frankfurt, Milan, Bern and more than dozen cities as far away as Sydney, Australia, stage violent protests; seize consulates; battle police; threaten mass suicides; hundreds are arrested; most of approximately two dozen hostages are freed; at least three Kurds are seriously injured after setting themselves on fire; focus of anger is against Greece, which temporarily provided Ocalan shelter, and Kenya where he was captured; both countries are believed to have betrayed him in end; Kurds demonstrate in Kurdish neighborhood in Istanbul, setting cars on fire; demonstrations of joy erupt elswhere in Turkey, where many people view Ocalan as terrorist; photos (M)
news.title: TOP KURD'S ARREST UNLEASHES RIOTING ALL ACROSS EUROPE

news.abstract: Northern Ireland Assembly approves sweeping changes in political structure in predominantly Protestant British province, aimed at giving Roman Catholics minority more power and ending sectarian violence that has killed more than 3,200 people in last 30 years; continuing dispute over disarmament of Irish Republican Army threatens to delay formation of Cabinet, which is supposed to be completed by March 10 (M)
news.title: Northern Ireland Assembly Approves Political Restructuring

news.abstract: Kurdish guerrilla leader Abdullah Ocalan, Turkey's most-wanted fugitive whose army has been fighting for Kurdish homeland, is captured in Kenya and flown back to Turkey; Ocalan, whose 14-year war has cost lives of estimated 30,000 people, has been sought by Turkish authorities for more than decade; could face execution; his semiclandestine existence since 1980 and details of his capture discussed (M)
news.title: In Snatching a Fugitive Rebel, Ankara Wins Opportunities on Several Fronts

news.abstract: Rise of Abdullah Ocalan as revolutionary leader of Kurds may have been been one of greatest modern tragedies to befall hapless group, which has been exploited and slaughtered by dozens of regimes over centuries; Ocalan, whose return to Turkey as prisoner seems to have ended his 14-year career as guerrilla leader, is by most accounts dogmatic and tyrannical; even though many Kurds have followed him, with many still considering him their leader, in eyes of world he has done as much as anyone to discredit their cause; many with whom he formed Kurdistan Workers Party in 1970's were later killed, some tortured to death on his orders; others fled to live clandestinely in Europe after he branded them as traitors for challeging him or pressing for more democracy within revolutionary movement; photo (M)
news.title: Kurds' Rebel Leader May Prove a Discredit to His Cause

news.abstract: Article profiles Qunu, South Africa, childhood hometown of Pres Nelson Mandela; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Qunu Journal; Mandela's Childhood Left a Fond Spot in His Heart

news.abstract: Fourth and final article in series, Global Contagion: A Narrative, on global financial crisis; crisis that began 19 months ago in Thailand is knocking on gates of American heartland and could be landmark crisis of post-cold-war era; while simplest challenge is for US to sustain strong growth rates, broader task will be to prevent nationalistic catacylsms in worst-off countries, like Russia and Indonesia, and to contain political and security risks of explosive frustration if crisis bites further into places like China and Latin America; while economy has demonstrated tremendous flexibility and resilience, uncertainties arise because US stock market is 64 percent higher than in December 1996 when Alan Greenspan, Federal Reserve chairman, warned against irrational exuberance; photos; chart (L)
news.title: World Ills Are Obvious, the Cures Much Less So

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and foreign diplomats welcome Indonesian Pres B J Habibie's statements favoring independence for East Timor, but fear that if break is too sudden it could lead to chaos and even civil war as Timorese factions maneuver for power; maps (M)
news.title: East Timor Seems Suddenly to Be on Verge of Independence

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: UKRAINE TREATY RATIFIED -- The Upper House of Parliament voted to ratify a treaty that effectively abandons the Kremlin's claims on Crimea on condition that Ukraine's legislature guarantee that the Russian fleet can maintain its existing fleet there. Prime Minister Yevgeny M. Primakov had sought the treaty in part to brake Ukraine's plans to join NATO.    Michael Wines (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Israel braces for reprisals after killings of three Kurdish protesters at its consulate in Berlin; Israel was already target of Kurdish rage because of its strong links with Turkey, and followers of Abdullah Ocalan have accused Israeli intelligence service Mossad of helping track down the Kurdish rebel leader (M)
news.title: Israel Denies Role but Fears Reprisal for Ties to Turkey

news.abstract: Officer-trainees in Kosovo Liberation Army are still preparing for war even as talks progress in France to reach agreement between rebels in Kosovo province and Serbian Govt; those at training school near village of Suva Rika say they will obey superiors' commands following any peace with Serbs; say core of rebel force must remain intact and armed, in order to protect ethnic Albanians when Western forces leave; over period of year, rebel army has gone from ragtag guerrilla bands to force of between 10,000 and 15,000, equipped with increasingly sophisticated weapons and bent on achieving not only autonomy for Kosovo being offered at peace talks, but independence for Kosovo's ethnic Albanian majority; photos; map (M)
news.title: Among Rebels' Officer-Trainees, No Sign Kosovo Fighting Is Over

news.abstract: Military and diplomatic pressure mounts on Pres Slobodan Milosevic to choose between tolerating NATO-led peacekeepers in Kosovo or suffering NATO air strikes for refusing them; Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright says she again warned Milosevic and that she will return to talks in Rambouillet, France; Milosevic has remained in Belgrade, and diplomats do not rule out high-level trip there before final agreement is reached; Clinton Administration and European officials expect Milosevic to conclude finally that air strikes would be more destabilizing to his rule than NATO-led ground troops keeping peace in Kosovo (M)
news.title: Pressures Mount Against Defiant Milosevic

news.abstract: King Abdullah's new regime in Jordan is gaining its financial footing, helped by strong and somewhat unexpected show of support from his neighbors; country has received promises of financial support from Saudi Arabia and Israel and pledges of continued trade ties from Syria and Iraq; this is in addition to assurance of long-term backing already provided by Clinton Administration and International Monetary Fund; Jordanians remain concerned about prospects for growth in stagnant local economy; there have been no reports of significant capital flight, and Amman's banks and stock market and currency traders opened their doors after official week of mourning for King Hussein; photo (M)
news.title: Neighbors Rally to Jordan, Easing Financial Fears

news.abstract: Former Rwandan mayor, Jean Paul Akayesu, is only man ever convicted of genocide; Akayesu wants to appeal genocide verdict handed down last fall by hiring criminal lawyer from Montreal, but his request has been quashed by administrators at United Nations tribunal in Tanzania that is trying suspects in 1994 killing of over half million Rwandans; ban, based on fact that there are already 9 Canadian defense lawyers, baffles some legal scholars; they contend policy is arbitrary and could jeopardize credibility of UN tribunal (M)
news.title: At a Genocide Trial, French Is a Handicap

news.abstract: Prime Min Costas Simitis of Greece replaces his Foreign Minister and two other Cabinet members in effort to contain growing scandal over Greece's role in capture of Kurdish rebel leader, Abdullah Ocalan; Greek Government officials give their explanation of how Greece came to secretly harbor Ocalan, and then was unable to protect him from Turkish security forces; enraged Kurdish protesters have occupied Greek diplomatic posts all over world to protest what they see as Greece's betrayal of Kurdish leader; many Greeks express skepticism about Government's explanation, suspecting that Ocalan was sold out (M)
news.title: 3 Greek Officials Removed Over Rebel Kurd's Capture

news.abstract: Hundreds of Mexican country bands sing lyrics that chronicle drug traffickers' daily lives and violent routines; extraordinary popularity of their music in Mexico and in United States underscores profound roots drug industry has sunk into North American popular culture, suggesting that millions of fans quietly admire smugglers' fabled wealth, anti-establishment bravura and bold entreprenuerial skills; photo of popular band singing in San Luis Potosi about a rooster, parrot and goat, code words for drugs; map (M)
news.title: San Luis Potosi Journal; Mexico's Troubadors Turn From Amor to Drugs

news.abstract: Excerpts from Pres Clinton's statement on Kosovo at joint news conference with French Pres Jacques Chirac, and from their answers to questions
news.title: The President Describes 'the Challenge in Kosovo'

news.abstract: Libya asks United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan to clarify assurances that he has given to try to persuade Libya to turn over suspects in bombing of Pan American flight over Scotland in 1988 (M)
news.title: Libya Asks Annan About Pan Am Trial Rules

news.abstract: Federal officials say American companies in Saipan exploit garment workers who are overwhelmingly immigrants from China; lawyers filed class-action suit in Jan accusing garment makers and major retailers of underpaying and mistreating workers; many Chinese workers say they came to Saipan voluntarily to earn about five times what they made in China; say they can save $6,000 to $10,000 in two years and return home quite well off; graph; map; photos (M)
news.title: Stretching Federal Labor Law Far Into South Pacific

news.abstract: Clinton Administration seems resigned to not having agreement by Feb 20 deadline in Kosovo peace talks; officials are hopeful that ethnic Albanian delegation will sign settlement; Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic refuses to see chief US negotiator, Christopher R Hill (M)
news.title: Serbs Yield No Ground; Envoys Seem Resigned

news.abstract: EUROPE  BRITAIN: DEBT RELIEF URGED -- Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said he would use a meeting in Germany of the Group of Seven to reinforce American and German calls for accelerated debt relief for the world's poorest nations. Mr. Brown said he would press for $50 billion worth of debt to be wiped out.    Alan Cowell (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Few in Belgrade expect NATO to bomb Serbia in dispute over Kosovo province; feel that West is being unfair to Serbia; see Pres Slobodan Milosevic finding way to avert attack (M)
news.title: In Serb Capital, More Ennui Than Anguish Over a Raid

news.abstract: Analysis of impact on Kurdish guerrilla movement in Turkey of capture and apparent taming of rebel leader Abdullah Ocalan; much will depend on whether Turkey's leaders can shift unyielding stand and allow emergence of moderate Kurdish groups; map; photo (M)l
news.title: Turks vs. Kurds: Turning Point?

news.abstract: Group of Seven industrial nations finance ministers, meeting, Bonn, agree to create modest forum of top regulators, who will meet twice a year to consult and seek ways to improve quality of financial information; reject demands by German and French leaders for broad new 'architecture' aimed at taming violent financial markets swings (M)
news.title: Major Powers Agree to Take Modest Steps On Economy

news.abstract: Olivetti SpA opens drive to acquire Telecom Italia SpA, far larger rival, for equivalent of $60.56 billion; Telecom Italia prepares to battle hostile bid (M)
news.title: Olivetti Makes $60 Billion Bid for Telecom Italia, a Major Rival

news.abstract: Interview with Nikita S Mikhalkov, director of film The Barber of Siberia, who says he will weigh running for president himself if he cannot find candidate to support; possible candidacy reflects disillusionment Russians have with choices among infirm Pres Boris N Yeltsin and slew of pretenders widely seen as power-hungry opportunists; he calls for restoration of real or idealized virtues of Czarist Russia; photo (M)
news.title: In Filmmaker's Ideal Russia, a Presidential Role?

news.abstract: RSL Communications, company headed by cosmetics heir Ronald S Lauder, signs contract with Telekom Serbia to provide long-distance telephone service to and from Yugoslavia in defiance of US policy prohibiting investment in Serbia; RSL denies doing anything improper or violating US sanctions, even though US Treasury Dept says deal was not approved and is under active review (M)
news.title: Lauder Enters Into Deal With Yugoslav Company

news.abstract: Report by General Accounting Office criticizes key part of Clinton Administration's effort to stop spread of nuclear, biological and chemical weapons by helping employ scientists from former Soviet Union on peaceful projects; study of two Energy Department programs concludes that American aid may have instead supported scientists still working in Russia on projects related to weapons of mass destruction; says some scientists or their institutes may also have provided expertise not only to weapons programs in Russia but also to those of other countries (M)
news.title: Bombs-to-Plowshares Program Criticized

news.abstract: Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee of India and Prime Min Nawaz Sharif of Pakistan hold joint news conference in Lahore and issue joint declaration pledging immediate steps to reduce risk of nuclear war and to seek solutions to half a century of raging disputes, such as conflict over Kashmir; memorandum of understanding pledges to build trust in each other through series of high-level bilateral meetings and to adopt measures to prevent any accidental launching of nuclear weaponry; pledges to continue declared moratoriums on further nuclear trials and agrees to announce in advance any testing of ballistic missiles; Vajpayee extends invitation for Sharif and wife to visit New Delhi (M)
news.title: India Promises, With Pakistan, To Seek Peace

news.abstract: Growth of Saipan Island, US Commonwealth in Northern Mariana Islands, creates some impatience with absence of street names and numbers; legislature passed bill calling for action, but job remains incomplete; many islanders say street names and numbers would be unnecessary bother and unwelcome intrusion of modern life; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Saipan Journal; Palm Trees and Sun (and Who Needs an Address?)

news.abstract: Nigeria's main party, People's Democratic Party, still clings to lead in legislative elections despite weakening of support in eastern section of country; presidential election is just one week away; among winners in legislative contests is Lola Abiola-Edewor, daughter of late opposition figure Moshood K O Abiola; photo; map (M)
news.title: Narrow Edge in Nigerian Legislative Races

news.abstract: Serbian police beat and harass cease-fire monitors in Kosovo Province as reports emerge of attacks on villages and fighting between Serbian troops and ethnic Albanian rebels; troops reportedly destroy homes of ethnic Albanians in villages near Vucitrn, 18 miles northeast of provincial capital of Pristina; 4,000 people reportedly flee; rebels reportedly attack Serbian village in area, killing one person and wounding two others; Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which provides monitors to police shaky cease-fire, lodges strong protest with Serbian Govt; map; photo (M)
news.title: Serbian Police Reportedly Beat Two Cease-Fire Monitors

news.abstract: News analysis of implications of visit by India's Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee to Pakistan, where he held summit with Prime Min Nawaz Sharif (M)
news.title: Subcontinent Sees a Light

news.abstract: Turkey and Greece trade harsh words as crisis over captured Kurdish guerrilla commander, Abdullah Ocalan, further sours already tense relations; Suleyman Demirel, Turkey's President, says Greece should be added to list of countries that support terrorism and harbor terrorists for allegedly protecting Ocalan after he fled to Kenya, where he was captured by Turkish commandos; Greece accuses Turkey of trying to use it as scapegoat for Kurdish problem, which it urges Turkey to solve quickly; photo (M)
news.title: Turkey and Greece Trade Words Over Kurd

news.abstract: Mexico's governing Institutional Revolutionary party wins decisive victories in elections for governor in states of Quintana Roo and Hidalgo; victories underscore party's resilience and point to vulnerability of divided opposition (S)
news.title: Governing Party in Mexico Wins 2 State Votes

news.abstract: Long-awaited British Govt report says London's police force is riven with pernicious and institutionalized racism and suggests that its chief officers accept that conclusion as condition of keeping their commands; makes 70 recommendatons for changes in police practices to usher in fundamental transformation of race relations in Britain (M)
news.title: British Report Finds Racism Pervades Police

news.abstract: United States and China are making crash effort to resolve issues that block China from joining World Trade Organization; Deputy Treas Sec Lawrence H Summers comments on effort after meeting with Prime Min Zhu Rongji, Beijing; United States wants accord that will lower China's tariffs and commit it to legally enforceable schedule for opening markets (M)
news.title: U.S. and China Trying Hard For Breakthrough on Trade

news.abstract: ASIA    INDIA: BIHAR TAKEOVER IN DOUBT -- The Government's decision to dismiss the state government of Bihar, scene of two recent massacres of low-caste rural laborers, and to impose central rule appears doomed in Parliament. The opposition Congress Party has decided to vote against ratification of central rule, saying the massacres are insufficient reason to dismiss an elected government.   Hari Kumar (NYT)    UZBEKISTAN: 30 HELD IN FATAL BOMBINGS -- President Islam Karimov, left, said 30 people, described as mostly radical Islamists who underwent training in Chechnya, Afghanistan and Tajikistan, had been held on charges of organizing bombings last week that he called an attempt to assassinate him. The blasts, in Tashkent, the capital, killed 16 people.   (Reuters)
news.title: World News Briefs

news.abstract: China is on move, with estimated 10 percent of population migrating, mostly in search of better jobs; rural migrants, with strong emotional ties to villages and unable to get urban residence permits needed for entirely legal life in cities, mostly seek to earn money to take home; most of migrants, now thought to number 100 million, return to hometowns every Chinese New Year, in what may be largest seasonal migration in world; their presence is transforming urban life, mixing together China's distinct regional cultures and giving rise to new rootless urban underclass; map; photos (M)
news.title: 100 Million Restless Chinese Go Far From Home for Jobs

news.abstract: Federal Judge Hector M Laffitte, reversing his earlier ruling to move trial of seven Cuban exiles charged with plotting to kill Fidel Castro to Miami, orders proceedings to continue in Puerto Rico; warns case could still be moved to Miami if prosecutors fail to establish Puerto Rico as proper venue at trial; defendants are Angel Alfonso-Aleman, Angel Hernandez Rojo, Juan Bautista Marquez, Francisco Secundino-Cordova, Jose Antonio Llama, Jose Rodriguez and Alfredo Domingo Otero (M)
news.title: In Reversal, Cuban Exiles Will Be Tried In Puerto Rico

news.abstract: Case of Algerian Farid Guendoul, 28, who bled to death fleeing neo-Nazi skinheads, Guben, has shocked Germany, spurring appeals for fight against xenophobia and renewed questions about nation's immigration policy; rise of racism in depressed area of former east German underscores resistance Chancellor Gerhard Schroder faces in trying to ease citizenship requirements; map; photo (M)
news.title: Guben Journal; Hatred, Born of a Hitlerian Mix, on March Again

news.abstract: China Southwest Airlines plane, Russian-made jet, crashes on descent to Wenzhou, killing all 61 people aboard and people on ground; crash will likely raise questions about safety of Russian planes, which have been involved in relatively high proportion of Chinese air disasters even though they make up tiny franction of commercial fleet (M)
news.title: Crash of a Chinese Jetliner Kills More Than 60

news.abstract: The Clinton Administration appears to have walked into the Kosovo peace talks without a clear idea of what to do if the ethnic Albanians failed to follow the script.    The Administration expected the Kosovo Albanians to accept NATO troops as their protectors, allowing it then to press the Serbian leader to sign an accord. But it didn't turn out that way as the Kosovo Albanians, who want independence from the Serbs, balked at a deal for autonomy.
news.title: How U.S. Hit a Snag In the Kosovo Talks

news.abstract: Former Ukraine Prime Min Pavlo Lazarenko, who was detained as he tried to enter United States, seeks political asylum; faces corruption charges in Ukraine and claims he fears persecution by Pres Leonid Kuchma's Government (S)
news.title: Ukrainian Seeks U.S. Asylum

news.abstract: ROME—  Olivetti SpA, fighting fiercely to keep alive its takeover bid for Telecom Italia SpA, was scrambling Wednesday to raise about 23 trillion to 25 trillion lire ($13.5 billion to $14.7 billion) in additional funding, financial sources in Milan said.
news.title: Olivetti Races To Add Funds For a Heftier Telecom Bid

news.abstract: Thomas A Constantine, Drug Enforcement Administration head, warns Mexican drug trafficking organizations pose unprecedented criminal threat to United States, Senate Caucus on International Narcotics Control; cites their access to large staffs, arms arsenals and best technology; sidesteps question about whether Mexico deserves to be certified as cooperating in drug-fighting efforts (M)
news.title: D.E.A. Chief Warns Senate On Traffickers In Mexico

news.abstract: Independent truth commission report concludes that United States gave money and training to Guatemalan military that committed 'acts of genocide' against Mayans during Guatemala's 36-year brutal civil war; report contradicts years of official denials of torture, kidnapping and executions of thousands of civilians in war that commission estimates killed more than 200,000 people; commission's nine-volume report lists Central Intelligence Agency training of Guatemalan officer corps in counterinsurgency techniques as key factor that had significant bearing on human rights violations during armed confrontation; staff member of commission says panel also found evidence that United States had knowledge of genocide and still supported Guatemalan military; commission was set up as part of United Nations-supervised peace accord that ended war in 1996; photo (M)
news.title: GUATEMALAN ARMY WAGED 'GENOCIDE,' NEW REPORT FINDS

news.abstract: Pres Leonid Kuchma has failed to overhaul Ukraine's Soviet-era economy, and its Parliament is swayed by current and former Communists who block land privatization and overhaul of crippling tax system; as result, Ukraine continues to teeter between East and West; it has trappings of Western democracy all in place, but bureaucracy still shows its Soviet genealogy; its basketcase economy remains lashed to its Russian past; fiscal experts say country will be hard pressed to pay its foreign debt this year; in October, Ukraine will hold its third presidential election since independence in 1991; pro-European incumbent, Kuchma, who has been unable to raise living standards, may be defeated by candidate from Socialist and Communist left, most of whom favor closer ties with Russia; photos; map; chart (L)
news.title: Struggling Ukraine Teeters Between East and West

news.abstract: PARIS—  NATO moved forces closer to Kosovo on Thursday after U.S. intelligence reported that Serbian troops, backed by scores of tanks, were massing just across the border.
news.title: Milosevic Is Warned Against Launching Offensive : NATO Troops Move Closer To Kosovo to Counter Serbs

news.abstract: Palestinian officials reportedly rebuffed Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu's quiet offer to carry out several of Israel's obligations under frozen peace agreement signed last fall; Netanyahu, through intermediary, proposed that Israel open up promised southern safe-passage route between Palestinian territories in West Bank and Gaza, and he volunteered to release some Palestinian petty criminals from Israeli jails; but Palestinians did not take initiative seriously, because Netanyahu made no offer to cede any additional territory in West Bank; Saeb Erekat, senior Palestinian peace negotiator, says he views Netanyahu's offer as domestic political gesture to help him get re-elected; photo (M)
news.title: Palestinians Reject Netanyahu Offer as Campaign Tactic

news.abstract: Clinton Administration asks Secretary General Kofi Annan to handle all communications with Libya about turnover of two suspects wanted in 1988 bombing of Pan American flight in Lockerbie, Scotland; also asks Annan to discourage efforts by envoys from Saudi Arabia and South Africa to give Libya further assurances about trial, treatment of suspects or sanctions if men are handed over; decision to narrow mediation effort reflects growing concern that Col Muammar el-Qaddafi might be receiving 'mixed messages,' in form of assurances that neither United States nor Britain would agree to (M)
news.title: U.S. Seeks to End 'Mixed Messages' Over Lockerbie Suspects

news.abstract: United States and Britain warn at United Nations Security Council that they will seek added sanctions against Libya unless it surrenders suspects in 1988 Lockerbie airplane bombing within 30 days to be tried before Scottish court in Netherlands; Sec Gen Kofi Annan backs deadline (M)
news.title: A Warning At the U.N. To Libyans

news.abstract: Olusegun Obasanjo, retired general who is frontrunner in Nigeria's Presidential race, portrays self as only safe bridge in transition to democracy; he and rival, Olu Falae, wind up short campaigns that offer no clear picture of their ideology or plans to deal with economic, political and social problems; map; photo (M)
news.title: Counting Nigerians Before They Vote

news.abstract: Guatemalan truth commission report blaming military for deaths of nearly 200,000 people in 36-year civil war surprised nearly everyone with bluntness and severity of its judgments and recommendations; weakens political standing of military high command and their civilian allies and leaves them open to prosecution; charge of genocide against groups of Mayan people is not covered by amnesty they were granted in 1996 (M)
news.title: Searing Indictment

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    IRAN: ELECTION TURNOUT IS HEAVY -- Iran's first local elections in 20 years drew a heavy turnout in a contest that could give supporters of President Mohammad Khatami the upper hand in a power struggle against hard-liners in the Islamic Government. Polling stations in some towns ran out of ballots and voting hours in larger cities had to be extended. (AP)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Hong Kong's highest court bows to intense pressure and responds to Hong Kong government's request for 'clarification' with extraordinary statement that it had not meant to challenge Chinese authority with its recent ruling granting residency to mainland children of Hong Kong parents; does not alter ruling; lawyers and democracy advocates score stand (M)
news.title: In 'Clarification' on Immigrants, Hong Kong Court Bows to China

news.abstract: A $60 billion bid by the No. 2 Italian phone company, Olivetti S.p.A., for Telecom Italia was given a green light to move forward today, when Italian stock market regulators ruled that it was legally admissible.    The ruling came two days after Telecom Italia's chairman, Franco Bernabe, won boardroom backing for what is expected to be a long and bitter corporate battle, unaccustomed for the Italian business world and reminiscent of big American hostile buyouts of the 1980's.
news.title: Regulators Give Green Light to Olivetti's Bid for Telecom Italia

news.abstract: With Serbian troops apparently disregarding a NATO ultimatum to stop fighting in Kosovo and withdraw from the southern Serbian province or face air attacks, the allies could face the gravest test of their credibility since they forced a settlement of the war in Bosnia more than three years ago.    Time and again, the allies have been insisting since last spring that they would not stand by and watch, as they did for years in Bosnia, while Serbian forces committed atrocities against civilians. Yet not even the threat of 400 bombers, including B-52's, has been able to get the Yugoslav President, Slobodan Milosevic, to agree to accept a force of 28,000 international peacekeepers for Kosovo as part of a settlement that would provide autonomy for the province.
news.title: Peacekeeping in Kosovo: Grave Test for NATO Allies

news.abstract: Within hours after youths passing by a Juarez drainage canal on a recent day discovered the body of a 13-year-old girl, the most recent victim in a long series of sexual killings here, Esther Chavez Cano was rushing to spread the dismal news.    She was on the phone to members of the feminist organization she heads. She was typing E-mail messages to congresswomen and journalists. And in news interviews, Ms. Chavez, a 65-year-old former accountant for Kraft Foods, was accusing the new Governor of Chihuahua of breaking campaign promises made last year to investigate the killings of women in Juarez more seriously than his predecessor did.
news.title: Feminist Propels Outcry at Brutal Mexico Killings

news.abstract: For Prime Minister Atal Behari Vajpayee, the euphoria of his historic peacemaking visit to Pakistan was short-lived.     The stories about high-stakes nuclear diplomacy were quickly bumped off the front pages this week by his Government's mad scramble to salvage its move to dismiss the government of the eastern state of Bihar, one of India's poorest and most populous.
news.title: New Delhi Bid To Take Over Eastern State Hits Obstacles

news.abstract: The United Nations Security Council today demanded an immediate halt to the fighting between Ethiopia and Eritrea, after Ethiopian forces apparently smashed through the defenses along its disputed 600-mile border with Eritrea and appeared to be pushing deeper into the country in the direction of the Red Sea.     At an emergency meeting here, the Council called on both sides to refrain from further hostilities and resolve their border dispute on the basis of the peace plan drawn up the Organization for African Unity.
news.title: End Fighting, U.N. Council Tells Ethiopia And Eritrea

news.abstract: Ethiopia declares total victory over Eritrea in border conflict after four-day offensive dislodged Eritrean army from remote dusty borderland in Bademe region; Eritrea says it has no plans for counteroffensive (M)
news.title: Ethiopia Wins Border War Against Eritrea

news.abstract: VANG VIENG, Laos—  With a ring of opium grease starting to bubble around the pinhole on the end of his pipe, the emaciated old man reclining on a pile of dirty white pillows nods slightly to signal the liquid will soon vaporize.
news.title: Drug Tourism / In Laos, English Menus and New Opium Dens : Westerners Flock East for an 'Asian Trip'

news.abstract: Federal agents in California arrest Yao Yi, Chinese citizen, and charge him with trying to obtain component vital to missile guidance systems; arrest sheds light on China's alleged effort to smuggle American technology to improve accuracy of its weapons (M)
news.title: U.S. Says It Caught a Chinese Smuggler Seeking Gyroscopes That Can Guide Missiles

news.abstract: Doctors in Japan, for first time, perform legal heart transplant striking at taboo on taking organs from patients whom Japanese traditionally do not consider dead; operation on man in 40's is ethical and emotional milestone in country that has long believed that death comes only after heart stops beating and body turns cold (M)
news.title: Death Taboo Weakening, Japan Sees 1st Transplant

news.abstract: Two months after its rollout into the market, the euro is well into the process of becoming a no-longer-new-currency. The long haul is setting in.
news.title: Amid Political Interference, The Euro Has Yet to Foster A Unified Monetary Policy : Initial Luster Of New Money Begins to Fade For Europe

news.abstract: Nine people die in Ambon, Indonesia, after police open fire on crowd outside mosque; shootings follow new round of clashes between Muslims and Christians in provincial capital, on island 1,400 miles east of Jakarta; photo (M)
news.title: 9 Die at Indonesian Mosque When Police Fire at Rioters

news.abstract: UN panel recommends that new international tribunal be convened to try about dozen senior Khmer Rouge officials on charges of crimes against humanity while they ruled Cambodia; under recommendation, separate Cambodian truth commission would consider all other cases; China informs Clinton Administration it will veto idea if brought before UN Security Council; Khmer Rouge relied almost exclusively on Chinese support during their rule, which led to deaths of nearly two million Cambodians between 1975 and 1979 (M)
news.title: U.N. Panel Urges Tribunal For Khmer Rouge Leaders

news.abstract: 13 foreign tourists and unknown number of Ugandans are kidnapped while tracking mountain gorillas in forest near Uganda's southwestern border; three are Americans; attackers appear to be Rwandans (S)
news.title: Tourists Kidnapped

news.abstract: Man-in-the-News profile of Gen Olusegun Obasanjo, who will become Nigeria's first elected President after 16 years of military dictatorships; he is anomaly in country's recent history, and man of contradictions; he is best known as only one to have relinquished power voluntarily, out of eight generals to rule Nigeria since independence from Britain in 1960; caused resentment for governing with strong hand before 1979, but gained respect after being jailed in 1995 as outspoken critic of military dictatorship; was released from prison eight months ago; photo (M)
news.title: Man in the News; Nigerian Question Mark: Olusegun Obasanjo

news.abstract: Anxious quiet returns to northernmost area of Israel following Israeli bombardment of guerrilla targets across border in Lebanon; residents of Kibbutz Maayan Baruch are allowed to emerge from underground shelters for first time since week of Hezbollah attacks left seven Israeli's dead and led to sharpest Isralei offensive deep inside Lebanon since 1996; photo; map (M)
news.title: Israelis on Border Are Anxious, but Area Is Quiet

news.abstract: Eight foreign tourists, including American couple, are slain in Bwindi Impenetrable Forest of Uganda by band of Hutu rebels, who are said to be remnants of ethnic Hutu militias that carried out mass killings in Rwanda in 1994; four Ugandan park employees are also slain; victims include four Britons and two New Zealanders; Robert Haubner and his wife Susan Miller, slain American couple, were executives for Intel Corp; attack on group of 31 tourists appears to be related to violence that has beset central Africa for years; survivors say as many as 150 Hutu soldiers sought out Americans and Britons among tourists; map; photos (M)
news.title: 8 Tourists Slain in Uganda, Including U.S. Couple

news.abstract: Kosovo Liberation Army political leader Adem Demaci resigns, raising hopes among diplomats that ethnic Albanian guerrilla movement will sign autonomy plan proposed at peace talks; Demaci opposes peace plan, which would grant Kosovo autonomy under protection of NATO-led military force; Yugoslav tank and mortar fire pounds southern Kosovo hillsides, striking at rebel positions and driving thousands of ethnic Albanian civilians from their homes in some of heaviest fighting since start of talks; US and NATO officials say Yugoslav military buildup in Kosovo is violation of cease-fire reached in Oct, but that NATO will probably refrain from punitive strikes to avoid undermining efforts to reach accord; map (M)
news.title: Hopes for Kosovo Deal Rise As a Guerrilla Chief Resigns

news.abstract: Ethiopian troops recently expelled Eritrean Army from Badme region, which they have been fighting over for nearly year; Eritrea says it is willing to accept cease-fire, but Ethiopia has not said whether it will end hostilities (M)
news.title: Ethiopia Is Celebrating, But Perhaps Too Soon

news.abstract: Clinton Administration officials and NATO diplomats say that US and its allies have no intention of launching punitive strikes against Yugoslav military targets at this point despite army buildup and renewed fighting in Kosovo (M)
news.title: NATO Said to Rule Out Kosovo Reaction

news.abstract: Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe report condemns Croatian Government of Pres Franjo Tudjman for violating human rights and rights of minorities and disregarding rule of law (M)
news.title: Croatia Branded as Another Balkans Pariah

news.abstract: Analysts for years have been predicting demise of Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), but its recent election victories have undermined those arguments; debate over party's past and future dominate Mexico as Pres Ernesto Zedillo and 2,000 party stalwarts prepare to celebrate its 70th anniversary on March 4; party for decades was tool of successive presidents using authoritarian methods to insure one-party rule; over last 20 years, opposition parties have chipped away at monopoly and currently control Congress and 10 of 32 state capitals; dozens of PRI leaders have defected to opposition; PRI has never lost presidency; polls suggest that party can win presidential election next year, but only if it can avoid damaging split; Zedillo says that unlike his predecessors he will not handpick his successor; photo (M)
news.title: Ruling Party, at 70, Tries Hard to Cling To Power in Mexico

news.abstract: Otumfuo Opoku Ware II, traditional King of the Asante people of Ghana, dies at age 89; photo; map (M)
news.title: Opoku Ware II, King of Asante, Is Dead at 89

news.abstract: Senior US officials say suspected terrorist Osama bin Laden and Taliban, his protectors in Afghanistan, have had violent falling-out, raising possibility that his days of refuge may be numbered; say fight broke out between bin Laden's bodyguards and Taliban officers assigned to watch over him; say bin Laden was expelled from Kandahar; say he was isolated in countryside and stripped of his satellite telephones, which allow him to plot with fellow radicals throughout world; Taliban has shown no sign that it is willing to deliver bin Laden to US; Taliban official says Afghanistan has sent emissary to US asking how to deal with him (M)
news.title: Terror Suspect Said to Anger Afghan Hosts

news.abstract: US heats up two politically contentious trade disputes with Europe, slapping 100 percent tariffs on $520 million in European products and threatening to ban Concorde from landing in US; tariffs imposed by Clinton Administration on luxury goods are part of six-year battle over trade in bananas; threat to ban Concorde is in bill passed overwhelmingly in House, in retaliation for European ruling that would ban many older American airplanes from landing in Europe; both battles are really about tensions that have erupted between US and Europe newly unified by common currency; Washington and European Union find themselves unable to resolve seemingly ordinary economic disputes, with each accusing other of defying World Trade Organization (M)
news.title: MIFFED AT EUROPE, U.S. RAISES TARIFFS FOR LUXURY GOODS

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    ISRAEL: NETANYAHU ON PULLOUT  Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he would consider ''the possibility of a unilateral withdrawal'' from Lebanon if ''accompanied by necessary security measures.'' He rejected a suggestion by Foreign Minister Ariel Sharon that May elections be postponed in order to form a unity government dedicated to a pullout. Both men's remarks followed a campaign promise by the Labor Party candidate, Ehud Barak, to withdraw troops within a year if elected Prime Minister.   Deborah Sontag (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Prime Min Zhu Rongji says China will push on with economic and social reforms despite 'grim economic picture'; says China will continue to open country wider to outside world; his sobering speech before Parliament enumerates China's many current problems--from unemployment to official corruption to flagging export market; says China will continue recent policy of massive deficit spending to bolster economy and insulate itself from worst of Asia's economic woes; predicts China will have economic growth of 'around 7 percent' in 1999, down from official 7.8 percent in 1998 (M)
news.title: China Grimly Pledges to Push On With Reforms

news.abstract: PARIS—  Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's personal efforts staved off failure at least temporarily in the Kosovo peace talks last month at Rambouillet, France, but her intensive, often improvised, diplomacy raised concerns that her entry into the talks clouded the prospects for settling the civil war between Serbs and ethnic Albanians when the two sides reconvene on March 15, according to officials in Europe and the United States.
news.title: Albright Takes Some Heat For Rambouillet 'Success'

news.abstract: Protestants and Catholics opposed to promise of peace in Northern Ireland are killing and maiming their own; members of paramilitary armies who control working-class neighborhoods are turning their violence on their own, in vicious effort to avoid being swept away in march toward peace; in grim paradox, beatings increase at times like present, when cease-fires and political negotiations drastically reduce killing between two warring religious communities and bring exhilarating promise of peace; Sam Cushnahan, director of Families Against Intimidation and Terror, nonsectarian organization, says new violence is from militias that took on enforcement role to maintain unity and discipline in their communities as sectarian conflict became more intense; says they do not want to give up this power and control; photos (M)
news.title: No End to Violence in Ulster: Each Side Now Kills Its Own

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    JORDAN: NEW CABINET SWORN IN -- King Abdullah swore in a new 23-member Cabinet, ridding the Government of officials who were loyal to Prince Hassan, the uncle once expected to become King. Abdullah, 37, installed Abdul-Raouf Rawabdeh, left, as Prime Minister, and urged him and the rest of the Cabinet to consolidate ties with Israel and to work for a more open government and a freer press.   (AP)    IRAN: DRIVE ON DISSIDENT -- A special religious court barred Iran's newspapers from even mentioning Ayatollah Hossein-Ali Montazeri, a prominent liberal dissident who regularly denounces the conservatives' hold on Iran. Mr. Montazeri, who has been under police surveillance for years, was once favored to become Iran's supreme leader.   (Agence France-Presse)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Pavlo Lazarenko, former Ukrainian Prime Minister who asserts that his nation's leaders are using corruption charges to persecute him, says he has cleared first procedural hurdle toward winning political asylum in United States; Ukraine's prosecutor general tells news service that he is confident of Lazarenko's eventual return to Ukraine for prosecution; says Ukraine has given US evidence that Lazarenko embezzled and misused millions of dollars in government funds as part of long-running corruption scheme; he has been in Federal custody in New York since Feb 19, when he arrived at Kennedy International Airport with invalid visa; photo (M)
news.title: Ukraine's Ex-Premier Says He's Closer to Gaining U.S. Asylum

news.abstract: Labor party candidate Ehud Barak injects actual issue, withdrawal of forces from Lebanon, into Israel's volatile, personality-based election campaign; polls show voters are suspicious that such promises capitalize on grief at recent deaths of seven Israelis; Barak promises to withdraw army in one year, Yitzhak Mordechai says he would act even sooner, and Ariel Sharon calls for delaying election altogether; Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu opposes such deadlines, preferring to seek Lebanese cooperation rather than dealing with Syria (S)
news.title: Issue of Troops in Lebanon Energizes Israeli Election

news.abstract: Senior Chinese officials reaffirm determination to squeeze dead wood and red ink out of bloated state-owned enterprises, vowing to make nearly all competitive and profitable by end of 1999; Zhu Rongji, reporting on first year as prime minister, says he will press ahead with overhaul and streamlining of bureaucracy despite 'grim environment at home and abroad'; implicitly acknowledges social unrest that has flared as urban unemployment grows and farmers protest taxes and corruption; projects seven percent economic growth for 1999 (S)
news.title: China Reaffirms Drive to Overhaul Bloated State Industries

news.abstract: Lord Denning, prominent British judge who often favored precepts of common sense over starchier ones of common law, dies at age 100; his handling of inquiry into 1963 Profumo scandal recalled, as well as decisions protecting individuals from bureaucrats, corporations and trade unions; photo (M)
news.title: Lord Denning, 100, a Populist Who Enlivened British Courts
