news.abstract: Italian Prime Min Massimo D'Alema, in Washington, tells Pres Clinton he is shocked by acquittal of American pilot in deaths of 20 tourists who died when ski lift cable was cut by US military plane; says, at joint news conference, that Italians and Europeans demand accountability and punishment; Clinton apologizes, says US is not trying to duck responsibility, and reviews procedural changes to prevent such incidents; visit coincides with verdict in court martial of Richard Ashby, who says Marine Corps refused to deliver crew's letter of sympathy to victims' families (S)
news.title: Italian Presses Clinton on Pilot's Acquittal

news.abstract: Sec Madeleine Albright meets with East Timorese separatist leader Xanana Gusmao, who is brought from house arrest to Indonesian Foreign Ministryfor occasion; Albright hears talks with Gusmao and Pres B J Habibie on desperately poor region's transition to independence (S)
news.title: Albright, on Visit to Indonesia, Meets Detained Timor Leader

news.abstract: Algerians have new hope of peace following savage war between country's military rulers and Islamic guerrilla groups that took at least 80,000 lives since 1992; presidential election is scheduled for Apr 15, with 11 candidates representing array of political opinions, and promise from army not to interfere, as it has in past; many Algerians conclude that faction among generals are so shocked by years of violence that they decided to begin transferring some power to elected politicians; senior Government officials say there can be no final answer until country rebuilds its economy and finds work for millions of unemployed, especially in 70 percent of population under 30, commonly described as 'standing reserve force' for guerrillas; photos; map (L)
news.title: Unforeseen, Strife Eases For Algeria

news.abstract: Emir of Bahrain, Sheik Isa bin Salman al-Khalifa, dies of heart attack at age 65 following meeting with visiting Defense Sec William S Cohen (M)
news.title: Sheik Isa, 65, Emir of Bahrain Who Built Non-Oil Economy

news.abstract: When President Clinton visits El Salvador, Nicaragua, Honduras and Guatemala over four days this week, he will find a region forged by one tragedy or another over the last several decades, and more often than not forgotten in its intervals of renewal. The trip begins tomorrow, the day after Salvadorans vote on a new President, further cementing a remarkable democratic transformation after 12 years of civil war. Compared with the clamor of the 1980's, when the region's upheavals dominated American foreign policy, that change has occurred nearly silently.  Article, page 8.
news.title: New Era for Region As Clinton Sets Visit

news.abstract: Pres Clinton will begin four-day visit to Central America, with stops in El Salvador, Nicaragua, Honduras and Guatemala, beginning Mar 8; region's upheaval dominated American foreign policy in 1980's; now, it has taken natural disaster--Hurricane Mitch--to refocus attention there; Clinton's agenda for this visit will reflect global issues of today--free trade, immigration and drug trafficking, in addition to repairing damage from Hurricane Mitch; but past interventions and traumas are likely to confront Clinton in places like Guatemala, where truth commission recently blamed country's military rulers, assisted by Washington, for acts of genocide against country's Maya population during 36-year war; photo; map (M)
news.title: Clinton to Begin Visit to Central America

news.abstract: South Africa's first multiracial party, United Democratic Movement party, was formed by Bantu Holomisa, black man, and Roelf Meyer, who is white; recent poll suggests they may already have won over as much as 9 percent of voters; that is twice goal they set when they formed party year ago; they operate on shoestring, mostly relying on volunteers, as they campaign around country; nobody expects Holomisa-Meyer team to win South Africa's second post-apartheid elections, scheduled for June 2; but they may push aside crumbling former National Party and Zulu-focused Inkatha Freedom Party to become biggest opposition party; some political analysts even wonder if they might some day challenge African National Congress party of Pres Nelson Mandela; photo (M)
news.title: Odd Twosome Takes On South Africa's Status Quo

news.abstract: United States Defense Sec William S Cohen, touring region to solidify anti-Iraqi sentiment among friendly Arab government, offers to sell Saudi Arabia sophisticated air-to-air missiles to help shore up its defenses against Iraq, meeting with Prince Sultan bin Abd al-Aziz; Iraq charges US pressures and blackmails Arabs (M)
news.title: U.S. Offers Saudi Arabia New Weapons

news.abstract: Interior Min Sergei Stepashin warns of economic, political and 'operational' moves to punish separatist Chechnya region unless Chechen kidnappers quickly free Maj Gen Gennadi Shpigun; kidnappers seized him from plane on ground in Grozny; Russian officials are evacuated by convoy from region (M)
news.title: Russia Promises to Punish Chechnya for Abduction of General

news.abstract: Canada, which contains 20 percent of world's known freshwater resources, has set temporary nationwide ban on bulk exports of fresh water; says moratorium will remain in effect until all 10 provinces can come up with way to ban exports permanently; Min Lloyd Axworthy cites concern that water could become commercial good covered by North American Free Trade Agreement, and therefore subject to continental exploitation (M)
news.title: Free Trade in Fresh Water? Canada Says No and Halts Exports

news.abstract: Prof Ronald Willetts, British authority on life in ancient Crete, dies at age 83 (S)
news.title: Ronald Willetts, 83, of Britain, Expert on Life in Ancient Crete

news.abstract: IMAGINE arriving at the airport to find that instead of the familiar airline check-in desks, there is just one long row of desks displaying the logo Star Alliance. At other airports, you might have a choice of Oneworld or Atlantic Excellence. But this is Hamburg, a Star Alliance hub.
news.title: Are Airline Alliances Passenger-Unfriendly?

news.abstract: Energy Sec Bill Richardson says Wen Ho Lee, Taiwan-born scientist at Los Alamos National Laboratory, was fired for security breaches after FBI questioned him in connection with China's suspected theft of US nuclear secrets; accuses Lee of 'stonewalling' investigation; Lee has not been charged with crime, but he has been identified by Federal officials as prime suspect in spying; China denies any such theft; Sen Fred Thompson criticizes Clinton Administration for failing to notify Congress in 1997 that China had stolen nuclear secrets when Administration certified that Beijing was no longer helping other nations build nuclear bombs (M)
news.title: U.S. Fires Scientist Suspected Of Giving China Bomb Data

news.abstract: Turkish filmmaker Reis Celik has produced film about three college dropouts who tried to set off Marxist revolution in Turkey, but who were captured and hanged in 1972; film, Goodbye Tomorrow, focuses on most prominent of three, Deniz Gezmis; since film's release, debates over Gezmis, leftist movement and death penalty have come to surface in Istanbul; photos (M)
news.title: Istanbul Journal; Film Confronts a History Few Turks Can Agree On

news.abstract: LONDON—  Correction published in the International Herald Tribune, March 11, 1999:
news.title: U.S. Can't Solve Every Crisis, He Says, Urging Quick Action : Blair Presses Case For Europe Force

news.abstract: Biographical sketch of El Salvador's newly elected Pres Francisco Flores notes that he was born in Santa Ana on Oct 17, 1959, and holds bachelor's degree in political science from Amherst College; photo (M)
news.title: Man in the News: Francisco Guillermo Flores Perez; New Salvadoran Puzzle

news.abstract: William L McGonagle, who as Navy captain won Medal of Honor for maintaining control of technical research ship Liberty although wounded when ship was attacked by Israel in 1967 Arab-Israeli war, dies at age 73; photo (M)
news.title: William McGonagle, 73, Hero Of Israel Attack on the Liberty

news.abstract: National Endowment for Arts Chmn William J Ivey cancels grant for The Story of Color after learning from reporter that bilingual children's book was written by Mexican Zapatista guerrilla Subcomandante Marcos and bears picture of him wearing ammunition belt and mask; overrules multilayered, yearlong grant approval process; expresses concern that NEA funds might aid rebels; decision stuns Texas publisher, Cinco Puntos Press, shoestring operation that laid out $15,000 to print books; Bobby Byrd, who runs company, says he made it clear in grant proposal that guerrillas would not get NEA money; photos (M)
news.title: N.E.A. Couldn't Tell a Book by Its Cover

news.abstract: Federal grand jury indicts Yao Yi, Chinese scientist, and Collin Shu on charges of conspiring to violate export control laws by attempting to ship fiberoptic gyroscopes to China; Customs Service holds shipments could have helped China improve accuracy of its missiles (S)
news.title: China Export Charges

news.abstract: Proposal by Mitsubishi Corp to build huge salt plant in partnership with Mexican Government in Laguna San Ignacio pits it against environmentalists seeking to protect gray whale's winter breeding grounds; both sides have launched sophisticated, global campaigns, with videos, Web sites, letter-writing drives and guided tours to promote its view; top scientists, recruited by both sides, are divided on issues; lagoon is part of biosphere reserve created by Mexico in 1988 as largest protected natural area in Latin America; map; photo (M)
news.title: Laguna San Ignacio Journal; Save the Whales? Mine the Salt? Mexican Standoff

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and Congressional committee are wrangling over how much to make public of committee report on China's acquisition of sensitive American military technology; bipartisan committee found China harmed national security over last 20 years by stealing nuclear secrets and acquiring other American technology; dispute is taking on more partisan tone, providing ammunition for critics of Pres Clinton's China policy in days before key United States-China talks; committee members comment (M)
news.title: Political Battle: What to Reveal On China Arms

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    ARGENTINA: A ROYAL RECONCILIATION  Prince Charles, who is making a three-day state visit, paid homage to Argentine troops who died in the 1982 Falkland Island war and shook hands with survivors, who asked him to help them visit Argentine war graves on the disputed islands. The Prince, seen left with President Carlos Saul Menem, laid a wreath at the monument to Argentina's 652 war dead, echoing a similar gesture of reconciliation by Mr. Menem in London last year.   (Reuters)    BOLIVIA: JUDGES SUSPENDED  The Government announced that it is suspending 18 judges and magistrates in several cities on suspicion that they are connected to drug dealers or have given traffickers special treatment in their courts.   Clifford Krauss (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: PARIS—  If there is a common link to the young designers working in Paris right now — Jeremy Scott, Bless, Gaspard Yurkievich, Sharon Wauchob — it is that they all belong to a school of hyper-realism.
news.title: A New Breed in Paris:Hyper-Realistic Designers

news.abstract: US envoy Richard C Holbrooke, after meeting with Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic, says he has failed to win any change in Serbian leader's opposition to peace proposal for Kosovo (M)
news.title: After 2d Day With Milosevic, Envoy Reports No Progress

news.abstract: House Speaker J Dennis Hastert, despite Clinton Administration's objections, says House will vote on whether to endorse sending US peacekeeping troops to Kosovo if settlement is reached there (M)
news.title: House to Vote on Kosovo Force Despite White House Appeals

news.abstract: Pentagon says US flight crews working temporarily at base in Aviano, Italy, are prohibited from low-level training flights like one that hit ski-gondola cable 13 months ago, killing 20 people (M)
news.title: U.S. Curbs Low-Flight Training in Italy Near '98 Ski-Lift Deaths

news.abstract: PARIS—  Jeremy Scott, who will close the latest round of international women's ready-to-wear shows Saturday night, is just one of a number of young designers, with a median age of about 25, currently shaping fashion's future. The dark, gothic aesthetic of his contemporaries, Veronique Branquinho, Olivier Theyskens and Balenciaga's Nicholas Ghesquiere, for example, has had an enormous effect on many a runway this season.
news.title: Young Designers Shaped by Dark Gothic of '80s : Minding the (Generational) Gap

news.abstract: Private charities that are buying freedom for enslaved children and young women in Sudan react angrily to recent criticism of them from Unicef, United Nations Children's Fund; John Eibner, head of Christian Solidarity International of Zurich, which since 1995 has bought and set free 5,942 Sudanese children, spending about $50 a child, declares 'It is very difficult to understand why Unicef should say our activities are intolerable'; Charles Jacobs of American Anti-Slavery Group in Boston, which helps raise money to support Christian Solidarity, holds 'What is intolerable is to leave these women and children in the hands of brutal captors' (M)
news.title: U.N. Criticism Angers Charities Buying Sudan Slaves' Release

news.abstract: Pres Clinton and a group of Central American leaders declare that they will work among themselves and with United States to reach 'humane and permanent solutions' to problems of illegal immigration; declaration is issued at one-day meeting in Antigua, Guatemala, that focuses on reconstruction after a devastating autumn hurricane, development, trade and immigration; photo of Clinton and Latin leaders (M)
news.title: Clinton and Latin Leaders Turn to Immigration

news.abstract: LONDON—  While accessory designers in London may be the unsung heroes of the city's revival as a fashion hotspot, the problem is some of them are victims of their own success.
news.title: Accessory Designers in Britain Cash In on Their Eccentricity : The Extras That Count (and the Zanier the Better)

news.abstract: ASIA    INDONESIA: EAST TIMOR BALLOT -- Indonesia and Portugal agreed to let East Timor decide through a direct ballot whether to accept Indonesia's offer of greater autonomy or seek full independence. Details of the vote remain to be worked out. The accord came after two days of talks at the U.N. among the Indonesian Foreign Minister, Ali Alatas, left, the Portuguese Foreign Minister, Jaime Gama, and Secretary General Kofi Annan. Indonesia has still has not decided how much additional autonomy to allow the former Portuguese colony. Further talks will be held next month.    Paul Lewis (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: US House votes narrowly to support Pres Clinton's plan to send American troops to Kosovo should a peace settlement be reached, after a passionate and bitter debate on United States policy in Balkans; 219-to-191 vote reflects House deeply divided over Clinton's efforts to commit troops to another peace settlement in Balkans; supporters of Clinton argue that United States has a moral obligation to stop a genocidal war that could ignite a broader conflict; opponents--including House majority leader and House Republican whip--argue that Kosovo would prove to be a quagmire, and that Europe could police any settlement (M)
news.title: In Vote Clinton Sought to Avoid, House Backs a Force for Kosovo

news.abstract: TOKYO—  When the Japanese talk about female sexuality, the one thing everyone agrees on is the allure of feet. For more than a millennium, women's feet and footwear have played a major role in defining femininity. Fifteenth-century samurai warriors picked concubines by their feet, often without bothering to inspect the rest. In 19th-century Edo (old Tokyo), presenting a woman with sandals was the prelude to any sexual relationship. And until about 30 years ago, Kyoto geishas treated favored clients with the sight of their bare feet.
news.title: There's but One Rule for Footwear Here:Display!: In Japan, the Allure of Feet

news.abstract: Algerian paramilitary police officers are riding Train 1001 between Algiers and Oran in effort to cut down on attacks by Islamic rebels as it travels through Atlas Mountains; map; photo (M)
news.title: Oran Journal; Algeria's 'Train of Death' A Bit Safer, God Willing

news.abstract: NEW DELHI—  The Himalayan mountains are a long way from the world's fashion capitols, but this remote region at the top of the world is the source of one of this season's best-selling accessories. Brilliantly colored, featherweight pashmina shawls have become a fashion sensation, combining today's essential elements of style: comfort and luxury.
news.title: Market for Cashmere Shawl Expands : The Lure of Pashmina

news.abstract: Italian Prime Minister Massimo D'Alema, in Poland to mark expansion of NATO, expresses outrage that US Marine Corps Capt Richard J Ashby was acquitted of charges connected to flying jet into ski gondola cable in northern Italy, killing 20 people; says that he expects US to find those who are responsible for disaster, and if not, Italy might have to reconsider how jurisdiction is awarded in future (M)
news.title: At NATO Event, an Italian Call for Justice

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: JEHOVAH'S WITNESS RULING -- Final judgment was deferred in a closely-watched court case against the Jehovah's Witnesses, who have been charged with violating Russia's restrictive law on religion. A judge sent the case to a panel that includes two linguists, a psychologist and two experts on religion. Rights advocates, who see the case as a test of religious tolerance, said the order was an attempt to put off a politically-charged decision.    Celestine Bohlen (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Three powerful bombs exloded in midst of markets in two towns in Kosovo, killing at least six people, including two children, and wounding dozens more; attack comes as leaders of ethnic Albanian majority leave for new round of peace talks with Serbs in Paris; two sides blame each other (M)
news.title: Bombs Kill 6 in Kosovo Markets As Leaders Depart for Paris Talks

news.abstract: Gen Charles E Wilhelm, commander of US forces in Latin America and the Caribbean, says American troops in Haiti are being put in danger by country's increasing political turbulence and should be removed; recommends periodic visits by US military personnel (M)
news.title: U.S. General Recommends Pullout From Haiti

news.abstract: NATO leaders believe that alliance's credibility is at stake in coming peace talks on Kosovo in Paris; delegation representing Albanian rebels in Kosovo have still not signed internatinal peace plan for autonomy worked out in February, and Pres Slobodan Milosevic of Yugoslavia has not budged from rejection of number of appeals by European, American and Russian officials to agree to take the peacekeepers provided under the agreement; photo (M)
news.title: In New Talks on Kosovo, NATO's Credibility Is at Stake

news.abstract: Hugo Banzer was democratically elected President of Bolivia in 1997, two decades after his military dictatorship; disappearance of 200 Bolivians during Banzer's rule from 1971 to 1978 was only minor issue in election campaign; Banzer's fortunes began to change following arrest of Gen Augusto Pinochet of Chile in London on Spanish judge's charge that he led effort to kidnap and kill leftists in five South American countries in 1970's; Banzer is being besieged by allegations from local human rights groups, press and even senior congressional members of his ruling coalition that he knowingly participated in joint operations with Chilean and Argentine military Governments as part of larger regional effort called Operation Condor that led to deaths of at least 36 people; map; photos (M)
news.title: Bolivian's Dark Past Starts to Catch Up With Him

news.abstract: NATO's gala 50th anniversary celebration in Washington may or may not include Russia, which remains uneasy about alliance, an old enemy that now includes former Soviet bloc countries of Poland, Czech Republic and Hungary; NATO has confidentially promised to limit crisis deployments to three countries, but Russian defense figure Sergei Karaganov says his country's strategy is still to have NATO as 'weak' as possible because 'we are not part of it'; Russia's longterm strategy is also to discourage NATO from trying to include Baltic states or other former Soviet-bloc nations, by making process as diplomatically painful as possible; anxiety is preoccupation of Russian elite and ranks low on average citizen's long litany of woes; polling graph (M)
news.title: Russia Remains Uneasy Over NATO's Expansion

news.abstract: Novo Selo, Serbia, one of few mixed villages left in Kosovo, is place where Serbs and ethnic Albanians live side by side in apparent harmony; they are surrounded by violence, and as conflict escalates around them, they cling to hope that peace will reach them before war does; photo; map (M)
news.title: Villagers Hope Kosovo Peace Arrives Before the War

news.abstract: Commodore William E Warwick, Cunard mariner who became first master of last great ocean liner Queen Elizabeth 2, dies at age 86; photo (M)
news.title: William E. Warwick, Commodore of QE2, Dies at 86

news.abstract: Washington questions whether China's current bare-bones arsenal of missiles and nuclear weapons will grow to become more potent arsenal that could rekindle kind of fears that shaped cold war; suspicion that China stole design of America's most advanced miniaturized warhead from Los Alamos National Laboratory 10 years ago has prompted anger in Washington, especially in Congress; despite continuing evidence of Chinese espionage abroad, most experts doubt China intends to change fundamentally its largely defensive nuclear strategy; experts outside US Government say China wants arsenal large enough to give it global status and deter potential for nuclear blackmail, but small enough so that country will not be bankrupted by its military force, as Russia was; they say China's modernization could accelerate its ability to threaten its neighbors; map (M)
news.title: Will Beijing's Nuclear Arsenal Stay Small or Will It Mushroom?

news.abstract: Pres Clinton's national security adviser, Samuel R Berger, says there is no question that China benefited from important information leaked from Los Alamos National Laboratory; Republicans and some Democrats are calling for further investigation into whether Administration delayed investigating loss after first suspicions arose in 1996 (M)
news.title: 'No Question,' U.S. Says, Leak Helped China

news.abstract: China's Parliament will amend Constitution to declare private business 'important component of the socialist market economy,' and it will further amend Constitution to incorporate rule of law; to China's fast-growing business class, change brings new sense of legitimacy and protection in country where business owners ae still likely to face significant political, economic and social discrimination; at practical level, business executives expect change to help end vast array of discriminatory practices that make it hard for them to buy land or get loans (M)
news.title: Capitalists to Be Granted Official Status in Communist China

news.abstract: Veton Surroi, leader of ethnic Albanian delegation in Paris, says it is ready to sign Kosovo peace accord; French officials say signing was delayed while mediators consulted Serbs to see whether they would accept agreement with some minor changes; Serbs have accepted most of political provisions, but have refused to consider NATO peacekeepers to enforce it (M)
news.title: Ethnic Albanians Move to Accept Kosovo Pact

news.abstract: Banks in Ecuador open for first time in over week, during which Government had kept them closed because of worsening financial crisis; strike by taxi drivers blocks roads and brings commerce and transport to near halt; taxi drivers are protesting tripling in gasoline prices, to over $3 gallon, announced by Pres Jamil Mahuad (M)
news.title: Banks in Ecuador Reopen After Week's Closing, but Taxi Strike Aggravates Tensions

news.abstract: Senior intelligence and law enforcement officials say Wen Ho Lee, Taiwan-born scientist at Los Alamos National Laboratory questioned in nuclear espionage investigation, admitted to Federal Bureau of Investigation that he had unauthorized contacts with Chinese scientists; say his admissions helped cement decision by Energy Sec Bill Richardson to fire him on March 8; say Lee's statements had not provided enough evidence to lead to his arrest (M)
news.title: Los Alamos Scientist Admits Contacts With Chinese, U.S. Says

news.abstract: Sens Jesse Helms and Ernest F Hollings, reflecting Congressional anger over Pres Clinton's response to suspicions that China stole nuclear secrets, threaten to block Administration's efforts to help China become World Trade Organization member this year; also urge suspension of some scientific exchange programs; Sen Richard C Shelby urges Clinton or Energy Sec Bill Richardson to put moratorium on visits by scientists from countries like China to US national weapons laboratories, and on reciprocal visits by US scientists to foreign installations; CIA Dir George Tenet says retired Adm David E Jeremiah will head independent panel of experts to review possible harm to national security resulting from suspected thefts that took place in 1980's and were discovered by nuclear arms experts at Los Alamos National Laboratory in 1995 (M)
news.title: LEADING SENATORS DEMAND U.S. LIMIT HELP FOR BEIJING

news.abstract: Institute of Medicine report finds that preserving last known samples of deadly smallpox virus in Russia and US may provide important scientific and medical opportunities that would be lost if virus is destroyed this year, as planned; report is likely to influence Pres Clinton's thinking about politically and scientifically contentious issue (M)
news.title: Panel Says Smallpox Stocks May Be Useful

news.abstract: PARIS—  Taking up a sought-after appointment on the European Commission in Brussels four years ago, Edith Cresson seemed to put a safe distance between herself and her image from early in the decade as a headstrong politician with a knack for insulting remarks, including slurs against Britain and Japan when she was France's first female prime minister.
news.title: Trademark Traits Bring Cresson's Career to Close

news.abstract: News analysis of abrupt resignation of entire executive leadership of 15-member European Union amid charges of fraud and gross mismanagement; resignation clearly reflects deeper malaise in which democratic accountability of organization's Brussels-based leadership has not grown, even though size and power of united Europe have expanded; underscores need for European leaders to pay greater attention to theme of democracy (M)
news.title: Mouse That Roared: European Parliament Stands Up

news.abstract: Senior Clinton Administration aide ordered late in 1996 that security measures at nation's nuclear weapons laboratories be quickly strengthened, months earlier than previously acknowledged, but orders were largely ignored or delayed; Deputy Energy Sec Charles B Curtis ordered that series of security measures be carried out on strict timetable, but measures were not taken despite warning in department's annual security review for year that department was at greater risk of becoming victim of espionage than at any time in its history; officials say lapses occurred mostly during transitional period, during which Federico Pena became Energy Sec in 1997 and Curtis left office month later (M)
news.title: Nuclear Lapses Known in '96, Aides Now Say

news.abstract: Transitions, post-Communist world's sole magazine devoted to analyzing region's own transformations, ceases publication--victim of Russian financial crisis, bad management and shifting priorities of financier George Soros, its main supporter (M)
news.title: Mitteleuropa Loses a Voice As Soros Shuts His Magazine

news.abstract: Interview with Dr Ronald J Clarke, South African anthropologist engaged in effort to extract skeleton believed to be 3.5 million years old from Sterkfontein caves near Johannesburg; his discovery, announced in December 1998, may help answer some enduring questions about human evolution; scientists have likened find to discovery of famous 'Lucy' skeleton in Ethiopia in 1974; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Sterkfontein Journal; Solving a 3.5-Million-Year-Old, 3-D Jigsaw Puzzle

news.abstract: Breitling Orbiter 3, having floated some 20,000 miles over Europe, Africa, Asia, Pacific Ocean and Central America, heads into home stretch over Atlantic Ocean in its bid to become first balloon to circle world nonstop; Dr Bertrand Piccard is pilot and Brian Jones is co-pilot; diagram (M)
news.title: Balloon Crew Has First Global Nonstop in Sight

news.abstract: It is a blustery day at Rutgers University, in New Jersey, and Walter Hewitt, a nurse at the health center, is treating his 10th cold of the day. "Open your mouth," he says to a student ... and out pops a silver tongue ring. Down the hall, when a nurse practitioner, Judith Greif, asks another student to lift his shirt for an examination, she notices his nipples are pierced.
news.title: American Topics : Tattoos Guide Campus Nurses

news.abstract: Aryeh Deri, charismatic Israeli politician, is convicted on corruption charges in verdict that outrages ultra-Orthodox Sephardic Jews who consider him champion of their community; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Politician Convicted of Corruption

news.abstract: LONDON—  One of the biggest challenges to the growth of the Internet in Europe can be summed up in a few words. Words like Yahoo!, AOL or Amazon.com.
news.title: Europeans Focus on Local Content to Spur Internet Growth

news.abstract: Families and allies of Yitzhak Rabin and Menachem Begin are raising millions of dollars to build museum-scale centers to honor late Israeli Prime Ministers (M)
news.title: 2 Late Israeli Leaders, 2 Grand Museums

news.abstract: Clinton Administration, with Kosovo talks at a dead end, and Yugoslav leaders more recalcitrant than ever, is publicly pushing threat of air strikes, but officials say they have no option but diplomacy, at least for another week; Administration's policy of using threat of air strikes to force Pres Slobodan Milosevic to sign peace agreement has failed so far; peace talks conclude in Paris with ethnic Albanians signing an agreement on autonomy, but Serbs still refusing to accept it (M)
news.title: Doubts on NATO Air Raids As the Talks on Kosovo End

news.abstract: Saudi Arabia releases an Iraqi plane it seized on Wednesday after United Nations sanctions committee failed to agree on whether such flights of religious pilgrims violate United Nations sanctions; UN officials say that plane that Saudi authorities detained at Jidda airport was carrying 111 Iraqis traveling to Mecca for the haj pilgrimage to Mohamed's birthplace required once in a lifetime of all pious Muslims who can afford it (M)
news.title: Saudis Release Iraqi Plane in Sanctions Dispute

news.abstract: Pres Clinton asks an advisory panel today to analyze security threats at Energy Department's nuclear laboratories, after suspicions surfaced that China stole nuclear-weapons designs from United States (S)
news.title: Clinton Asks Panel to Analyze and Solve Security Threats to Nuclear Labs

news.abstract: Arthur Doak Barnett, leading scholar and government adviser on China, dies at age 77; photo (M)
news.title: A. Doak Barnett Dies; China Scholar, 77

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: 'GENETIC FOOD' WARNING -- Britain ordered restaurants, cafes, delicatessens, fast-food outlets and caterers to tell their customers if their meals contain genetically modified products. Failure to comply with the regulations, which go into effect immediately, could bring fines of up to $8,750.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: International monitors are ordered to pull out of Kosovo, and Western embassies order their nonessential staff to leave country after peace talks collapse in Paris; NATO officials say no bombing will be made until all cease-fire monitors are safety out (M)
news.title: Monitors and Embassy Staff Told to Leave Yugoslavia

news.abstract: SYDNEY—  It was touted as the most advanced nonnuclear submarine in the world — a silent, potent leviathan capable of staying submerged for 70 days and patrolling over long distances.
news.title: New-Generation, but Noisy, Australian Submarines Under Attack

news.abstract: Four Irish Republican Army guerrillas convicted of terrorist crimes in Northern Ireland are sentenced to a total of 400 years in prison, but they will be freed by July 2000 under terms of peace agreement; about 300 Catholic IRA and Protestant paramilitary prisoners have already been released early under agreement (S)
news.title: '400 Years' in Irish Jail Lasts Just 16 Months

news.abstract: Jean Pierre-Bloch, French resistance figure, high-ranking member of de Gaulle's Free French movement during World War II, dies at 93; photo (M)
news.title: Jean Pierre-Bloch, 93, Is Dead; Resistance Fighter for France

news.abstract: Pres Clinton says that Serbs have crossed the threshold of acceptable behavior and that force is the answer to prevent further bloodshed in Kosovo; says that beyond human toll, conflict in Kosovo could send tens of thousands of refugees across borders and possibly draw Albania, Macedonia, Greece and Turkey into the war; makes case to Congressional leaders, but they remain skeptical about the reasons for US involvement in hostilities in former Yugoslavia; Western Governments begin removing cease-fire monitors and nonessential personnel from Yugoslavia; Pentagon dispatches additional combat aircraft to region; Clinton photo (M)
news.title: Clinton Says Force Is Needed to Halt Kosovo Bloodshed

news.abstract: Dr Bertrand Piccard and Brian Jones sail into history when their Breitling Orbiter 3 completes the first nonstop balloon trip around world; balloon, at altitude of 36,000 feet, sped past finish line at at 9 degrees 27 minutes west longitude over Mauritania; harrowing trip had taken pilots over Europe, Africa, Asia, Pacific Ocean, Central America and Atlantic Ocean; photo; map (L)
news.title: Balloon History, and in Only 20 Days

news.abstract: French prosecutor Yves Bot rules that French President Jacques Chirac cannot be prosecuted while in office on political corruption charges stemming from his years as Mayor of Paris and leader of his conservative Gaullist party (M)
news.title: Ruling Says Chirac Can't Be Prosecuted on Corruption Charge

news.abstract: Thousands of panicked refugees flee their homes and villages as Serbian forces press an offensive against ethnic Albanian rebels in Kosovo; offensive comes as foreign monitors are evacuated from Kosovo after peace talks for Serbian province collapse and liklihood of NATO air strikes grows; photo (M)
news.title: Fears Deepens as Monitors Quit Kosovo

news.abstract: Russian Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov is facing one of his greatest challenges this week when he visits United States in effort to win several billions of dollars in credits from skeptical International Monetary Fund; success would help Russia to regain modicum of respectability on world financial markets as well as to restructure its colossal foreign debt; it would also make Primakov a conquering hero at home, with greatly improved chances of succeeding President Boris Yeltsin; photo (M)
news.title: Russian With Many Faces May Get Lift in U.S. Visit

news.abstract: Wildlife advocates are pressuring Canadian Government to adopt national endangered species law to protect wildlife and its habitats; some US wildlife groups plan to institute legal action that raises threat of trade sanctions against Canada unless effective law is passed (M)
news.title: Canada Faces New Pressure To Safeguard Rare Wildlife

news.abstract: Builders of Breitling Orbiter 3 balloon, in which Dr Bertrand Piccard and Brian Jones became first to circumnavigate world in balloon, disclose some technical innovations that led to success; says experience gained from previous flights was important factor; cites use of foam insulation around helium-filled central section that kept gas from expanding and leaking out during day and from cooling and contracting too much at night; photo (M)
news.title: With Balloon's Work Done, Its Builder Reveals a Secret

news.abstract: Irish Prime Min Bertie Ahern says there will be settlement of dispute over Irish Republican Army disarmament in time for Northern Ireland peace effort to advance by Easter deadline; will meet soon with Northern Ireland political leaders; notes positive indications from Gerry Adams of Irish Republican Army and David Trimble, Protestant First Minister of Northern Ireland Assembly (M)
news.title: Irish Premier Sees Progress On Arms Issue In the North

news.abstract: Clinton Administration dispatches special envoy Richard C Holbrooke to meet with Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic in what officials say it last chance to persuade him to accept peace agreement for Kosovo and avoid bombing by NATO; Sec of State Madeleine K Albright says Milosevic will be presented with 'stark choice' of either agreeing to settlement signed in Paris or face NATO air strikes; US officials at NATO headquarters in Brussels present NATO ambassadors with stepped-up plan for bombing in move intended to strengthen Holbrooke's position with Milosevic; national security adviser Samuel R Berger says another diplomatic push by Holbrooke is justified one final time, even as Administration comes under criticism for handling of Milosevic; Serbian forces seem unintimidated; take advantage of withdrawal of more than 1,300 international monitors to continue rampage through Kosovo, burning ethnic Albanian villages in region at heart of conflict (M)
news.title: MILOSEVIC TO GET ONE 'LAST CHANCE' TO AVOID BOMBING

news.abstract: Nearly three months of US bombings against Iraq are proving irritant to ties between US and Saudi Arabia; senior Saudi officials acknowledge kingdom refuses to allow American warplanes based in Riyadh to take part in what it perceives as punitive raids; stand has forced US to rely more heavily on navy aircraft and on warplanes at other bases; while Saudi officials make clear privately that they would prefer someone other than Saddam Hussein ruling Iraq, their military position is indication of discomfort felt over American-led campaign (M)
news.title: Saudis Admit Restricting U.S. Warplanes in Iraq

news.abstract: Serbian troops burn and destroy village of Prekaz, birthplace of armed Albanian revolt against Serbia's rule of Kosovo; refugees flee region; fighting reported in nearby village of Poljance as Serb forces take advantage of withdrawal of international monitors to launch attacks; Serbian tanks and heavy concentrations of troops surround Drenica; four Serbian policemen reportedly die in hail of gunfire from passing car in capital of Pristina; police patrol reportedly ambushed near town of Suva Reka; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Serbs Burn the Birthplace Of the Albanians' Revolt

news.abstract: Special US envoy Richard C Holbrooke, under orders not to let Serbia delay NATO action while Kosovo burns, meets with Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic in Belgrade in last-ditch effort to negotiate at least cease-fire; says little was achieved in more than three hours of talks with Milosevic; says heightened military activities in Kosovo make it extremely difficult to pursue peace; senior NATO official says Serbian forces have destroyed three of Kosovo Liberation Army's seven reigonal headquarters in past three days, adding to urgency of Holbrooke mission; Serb forces burn villages and drive civilians from homes in Kosovo, whose population is predominantly ethnic Albanians; Pres Clinton warns military action could be imminent if Milosevic continues to choose agression over peace; says 30,000 more Albanians have been displaced from homes in last few days; says Milosevic will not be allowed to continue aggression with impunity since America's security interests must include Europe's freedom and security; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. ISSUES APPEAL TO SERBS TO HALT ATTACK IN KOSOVO

news.abstract: Handful of US Senators clash over American role in NATO air campaign if Belgrade refuses to sign peace accord with ethnic Albanians in Kosovo province (S)
news.title: Senators Clash Over U.S. Role In a NATO Bombing Campaign

news.abstract: UN warns US must pay at least $250 million in back dues in 1999 or lose its vote in General Assembly; figure supersedes more than $197 paid toward end of 1998 to avoid losing Assembly vote in 1999 (S)
news.title: U.N. Warns U.S. to Pay Bill or Lose Assembly Vote

news.abstract: Suleyman Selimi, general commander of Kosovo Liberation Army, calls on NATO to carry out air strikes on Serbia to put end to violence, as Yugoslav Army and police forces continue ransacking and burning villages; special Serbian police units continue setting houses and farm buildings ablaze in village of Poljance; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Top Ethnic Albanian Rebel Asks NATO to Start Strikes

news.abstract: SANDAKAN, Malaysia—  Owen Campbell returned to Borneo last week, back to the jungles where half a century ago his best mates were marched to their deaths.
news.title: Borneo Death March /Of 2,700 Prisoners, 6 Survived : An Old Soldier Remembers a Wartime Atrocity

news.abstract: Russia's chief prosecutor's office confirms that it is investigating corruption inside Kremlin, aimed at members of Pres Boris N Yeltsin's inner circle; investigators, acting on orders from general prosecutor Yuri I Skuratov, have seized documents from offices of presidential administration's powerful property management office, headed by Pavel P Borodin; Skuratov recently defied Kremlin order to resign; photo (M)
news.title: Yeltsin's Inner Circle Under Investigation for Corruption

news.abstract: Sir Michael Caine, corporate chief with love of books who was driving force behind Booker Prize for Fiction, Britain's most prestigious literary award, dies at age 71; photo (M)
news.title: Sir Michael Caine, 71, Muse Behind Britain's Booker Prize

news.abstract: Senior US official says that Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic refused 'every opportunity' to avoid onslaught of NATO air power during negotiations with US envoy Richard C Holbrooke (M)
news.title: U.S. Negotiators Depart, Frustrated by Milosevic's Hard Line

news.abstract: Senate votes, 58 to 41, to support NATO air strikes against Serbian military targets; vote approves one-sentence resolution authorizing Pres Clinton to carry out US bombing and missile attacks as part of NATO's efforts to end crisis in Kosovo (M)
news.title: A Wary Senate Gives Support For Air Strikes

news.abstract: Politically charged sex-and-corruption trial of Malaysia's former Deputy Prime Min Anwar Ibrahim comes to sudden end when Judge Anthony Paul refuses to hear demand by defense that he step down because of pro-prosecution bias; Paul says he will announce verdict in two weeks (M)
news.title: Malaysian Trial Over Sex and Graft Ends Abruptly; Verdict to Come Later

news.abstract: South African Judge John Foxcroft sentences former anti-apartheid activist Allan Boesak to six years in prison for stealing hundreds of thousands of dollars donated to help needy children and educate black voters (M)
news.title: Anti-Apartheid Cleric Sentenced to 6 Years for Embezzlement

news.abstract: Clinton Explains Decision  The President said he decided to use force because of moral revulsion at the killings in Kosovo and to serve American interests. Page A15.    Serbs Turn Back to Loyalty  Even the Serbs most bitterly opposed to President Slobodan Milosevic feel a surge of nationalism at a threat from the West. Page A14.
news.title: MORE ON THE BOMBINGS

news.abstract: Albanian-Americans in New York metropolitan area rejoice when Pres Clinton announces that NATO bombing of Serbia had begun, but their joy is mixed with fear for their relatives and US servicemen; photo (M)
news.title: After the Years of Mourning, a Time for Joy

news.abstract: Caryn James article on television coverage of NATO bombing of Serbia; says after Yugoslav authorities shut down site that Western news organizations had used to transmit their stories, viewers were tossed back to pre-satellite era of television; says reporters in Belgrade and Pristina talked on phone while television screen showed still photograph of that correspondent alongside map marked with his or her location (M)
news.title: War Minus Pictures Puts Crimp In Reports

news.abstract: EXISTING mobile phones have not allowed users to make calls in the United States, Europe and Asia using the same phone. But the next generation of mobile networks will allow them to do so and will provide better services to boot.
news.title: In 2001, I'll See You on the Phone

news.abstract: About 50 Western journalists flee after Serbian Government orders all members of news media from NATO countries to leave; some take refuge in Skopje, Macedonia; some journalists and crews are roughed up; while atmosphere in Pristina, capital of Kosovo province, is reportedly more tense than elsewhere in country, other journalists also face harassment; two American reporters are held in Belgrade police station for 11 hours (M)
news.title: Loud Knocks In the Night, And Orders To Get Out

news.abstract: Russia introduces Security Council resolution demanding immediate end to NATO's air strikes against Yugoslavia, denouncing them as 'threat to international peace' and 'flagrant violation' of both United Nations Charter and Yugoslav sovereignty (S)
news.title: Russia Takes Protest to the U.N. Council

news.abstract: China presses an all-out verbal assault on NATO air strikes against Serbian forces, issuing multiple demands that attack be halted, while flagship state newspaper called operation a 'dangerous precedent of naked aggression' (S)
news.title: China Mounts All-Out Verbal Assault on Air Raids

news.abstract: Profile of Wesley K Clark, four-star American general who as Supreme Allied Commander in Europe is in charge of powerful NATO air offensive against Serbia for its attacks against ethnic Albanians in Kosovo; an allied diplomat, not American, says he thinks that Clark, 54, is intellectually the most impressive chief alliance has ever had, but that he is fixated on idea that force is the only language Serb leadership understands (M)
news.title: The NATO General Who Is Intimately Familiar With His Adversary

news.abstract: MELBOURNE—  Bitterly cold, terrifyingly remote and frequently lashed by gale force winds and mountainous waves, the Southern Ocean seems an unlikely Eldorado for poachers.
news.title: Fight Over Fish Poaching Stirs Up Icy Southern Sea

news.abstract: Whispers about a face-saving Serbian loss to the world's most powerful military alliance began here long before NATO bombs started to fall on Yugoslavia.    The whispers -- reinforced earlier this week in interviews with well-placed officials in the regime of Slobodan Milosevic, with opposition leaders and with Belgrade residents -- all follow a similar line of Balkan logic. It goes like this:
news.title: Milosevic Might Win From the Loss of Kosovo

news.abstract: Russia's rage over NATO air strikes in Yugoslavia boiled over tonight when it canceled the upcoming visit by Monica Lewinsky.    The former White House intern had been scheduled to visit Russia in June or July to promote a Russian-language version of her book, ''Monica's Story.''
news.title: Russia Cancels Lewinsky Visit

news.abstract: Clinton Adm and Orgn for Security and Cooperation in Europe say that they have received reports from refugees fleeing Kosovo and others that estimated 15,000 to 20,000 ethnic Albanian civilians were put on forced march in central Kosovo by Serbian forces; Adm cautions that it does not have satellite imagery to confirm accounts; but State Dept says it will monitor 'unfolding events in Kosovo' and collect evidence of any war crimes, like summary executions (M)
news.title: White House Tells of Reports Of a Forced March in Kosovo

news.abstract: On a rocky hill that overlooks the village in Kosovo 20 yards across the border that he fled last week, Agim, 27, squinted through binoculars today at two Serbian armored vehicles parked in the middle of his town.     ''I've seen soldiers looting televisions and refrigerators,'' he reported. ''They chased us all away, and now they are stealing everything.''
news.title: Reports of Reprisals Rely on Refugee Accounts and Scratchy Phone Calls

news.abstract: The United States and the NATO alliance won a victory today when  the Security Council rejected, 12 to 3,  a Russian resolution demanding an immediate end to NATO's air attacks on Yugoslavia.    Voting in favor of the measure were two of its sponsors, Russia and China, and Namibia. Voting against were the five Council members who are NATO members -- the United States, Britain, France, Canada and the Netherlands -- together with Argentina, Bahrain, Brazil, Gabon, Gambia, Malaysia and Slovenia.
news.title: Russia's Move To End Strikes Loses; Margin Is a Surprise

news.abstract: United Nations Commission on Narcotic Drugs, meeting, Vienna, gives its drug control program unanimous approval to create own satellite monitoring system to find drug crops in major source nations; Pino Arlacchi, program head, says European Space Agency will provide satellites and technical expertise, phone interview; says European Commission will pay part of cost, estimated at as little as $15 million a year (M)
news.title: U.N. to Create Own Satellite Program to Find Illegal Drug Crops

news.abstract: Renault's deal to take stake in troubled Nissan Motor Co seen risky business gamble to strengthen global competitiveness of both companies; tries to balance differing needs of Japanese auto company and Western one; helps resolve Nissan's financial problems while allowing its management to save face; seeks to insulate Renault from Nissan's financial woes, while giving it access to Nissan's advanced engineering and technical skills and car making capacity in United States and Mexico; deal may raise as many challenges as it seeks to resolve; photo (M)
news.title: In Renault-Nissan Deal, Big Risks and Big Opportunities

news.abstract: United States, which considers itself bastion of human rights, comes under attack from friend and foe alike at United Nations annual meeting on global democratic rights, Geneva; Amnesty International places US for first time on its list of human rights violators; key issue is death penalty (M)
news.title: Good Friends Join Enemies To Criticize U.S. on Rights

news.abstract: Michael Aris, 53, British husband of Burmese opposition leader Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, dies of cancer in London after being barred by Myanmar authorities from visiting her; she has refused to leave Myanmar, fearing authorities would bar her return; American Embassy in Myanmar, in unusual move, phones her message of thanks to those who helped Aris to reporters abroad (M)
news.title: Myanmar Opposition Leader's Husband Dies, Denied a Last Visit

news.abstract: Baltimore Orioles are set to play exhibition game in Havana against team of Cuban all-stars during particularly chilly period in cold war relationship between Cuba and United States; Cuba is target of international condemnation over its new curbs on growing internal dissent; photo (M)
news.title: Old Enmities Puncture Baseball Detente in Cuba

news.abstract: Tens of thousands of ethnic Albanians, driven from Kosovo villages by Serbian forces, flock into neighboring Albania, threatening to overwhelm country's scant resources and hasty efforts of Western aid workers; tell harrowing tales of brutality by Serbian police and paramilitary units that appear to show deliberate effort by Serbs to apply tactics of 'ethnic cleansing' used in Bosnia; photos; map (M)
news.title: CONFLICT IN THE BALKANS: IN ALBANIA -- NATO Planes Step Up Attacks on Serb Troops; Long Lines of Refugees Hounded Into Albania

news.abstract: Countless sheep are ritually slaughtered in Cairo, Egypt, at start of Id al-Lahma, or Muslim feast of sacrifice, which is one of most important festivals on Islamic calender that commemmorates Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to God; ritual, mandatory only for pilgrims in Mecca but urged on all Muslims who can afford it, described; photos (M)
news.title: Cairo Journal; When Sheep Are Invited, Much to Their Dismay

news.abstract: Slobodan Milosevic, defiant as ever and proud of his nation's resistance to NATO's air attacks, staged an eerie celebration today -- a rock concert in the center of Belgrade to show solidarity with the soldiers facing down the allied assaults.    Few of the thousands of Serbs who attended were unaware that this was also the 10th anniversary of the day when Mr. Milosevic stripped broad autonomy from Kosovo, just after his security forces had killed some 30 ethnic Albanian protesters in Pristina, Kosovo's capital.
news.title: CONFLICT IN THE BALKANS: IN BELGRADE -- NATO Planes Step Up Attacks on Serb Troops; Support for Homeland Up as Sirens Wail and News Is Censored

news.abstract: Macedonia is only former Yugoslav republic that has peacefully retained ethnically mixed society, but war being waged at its borders in Kosovo is testing country's ability to keep itself intact; working in its favor is ambition to move toward Western-style democracy and widely shared dread of ending up like neighbors; photo (M)
news.title: Balkan Rarity: A Peaceful Mixture of Ethnic Groups, All Looking to the West

news.abstract: Although US officials consider Slobodan Milosevic largely responsible for much of warring that has ravaged Balkans for past eight years, he has not been indicted by international war crimes tribunal, publicly or secretly; American and tribunal officials say US Government and tribunal are responsible for Milosevic's avoidance of legal accountability; Clinton Administration made him partner in seeking peace in Bosnia, and neither court nor US has considered indictment priority; neither have devoted resources to amassing evidence for indictment (M)
news.title: Tactics Were Barrier To Top Serb's Indictment

news.abstract: Grupo Financiero Bancomer SA and Grupo Financiero Serfin SA, two of Mexico's biggest banks, will plead guilty to criminal charges of money laundering in move bringing swift end to most important legal cases stemming from major investigation into movement of illegal drug profits; will forfeit millions of dollars seized by Govt and pay fines of $500,000 each; outcome is triumph for group of Federal prosecutors, Justice Dept officials and US Customs Service who resisted strong pressure from both Mexican Govt and banks to have charges dropped (M)
news.title: 2 Mexican Banks to Plead Guilty in Laundering Case

news.abstract: Interview with combat crew of Lockheed EC-130E command-and-control aircraft that herds NATO warplanes flying bombing attacks over Yugoslavia; diagram (M)
news.title: Command, Control and Adrenaline, and Relief at Pilot's Rescue

news.abstract: Several current and former American commanders say if NATO ordered ground troops to Kosovo, vanguard of force of 30,000 to 40,000 troops could be assembled in days and would be sufficient to protect many refugees from further attack; say small number of troops, backed by air power, could sweep into besieged province and create havens for tens of thousands of ethnic Albanians fleeing Serbian attacks (M)
news.title: Could a Small Ground Force Carve Out Safe Havens?

news.abstract: NATO officials say Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic's goal in Kosovo is to carve out Serb-only enclave in province that he can keep after fighting ends; say campaign is under way to ethnically re-engineer Kosovo to achieve solution more acceptable to him; say Milosevic has proven adept over past eight years at creating 'facts on the ground'--territorial conquests that end in cease-fires and are presented to West for ratification through peace deal; concerns are heightened by visit of Russian Prime Min Yevgeny Primakov and Foreign and Defense Ministers to Belgrade; NATO officials fear Russians may try to broker agreement well short of allies' stated goal of autonomous Kosovo protected by NATO troops; photo; map (M)
news.title: Milosevic Goal Is Serb Enclave, NATO Declares

news.abstract: NATO warplanes hunt for Serbian troops in embattled province of Kosovo as Clinton Administration claims evidence of genocide is growing to include abhorrent and criminal action on vast scale; language is strongest yet by State Dept in denouncing Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic; reports persist of assassinations of ethnic Albanian leaders and of scorched-earth torching of Kosovo's villages by Serbian forces; tens of thousands of refugees continue fleeing in terror; pour into Albania, Macedonia and Montenegro, compounding region's profound refugee problem; military officials acknowledge hunt for Serbian forces is complicated by fact that they are operating in small and dispersed groups; new attacks are aimed at barracks, headquarters and other bases, rather than tanks, artillery pieces and small mobile infantry units deployed in field against Kosovo villages; more US warplanes are earmarked for NATO operation, including bombers carrying antitank bombs and aircraft designed to confuse enemy radar systems; Belgrade claims forces shot down second NATO warplane; claim is denied by Pentagon; officials continue withholding information on what brought down F-117 stealth fighter over Yugoslavia days ago; map; photo (M)
news.title: NATO HUNTING FOR SERB FORCES; U.S. REPORTS SIGNS OF 'GENOCIDE'

news.abstract: Ethnic Albanians in Kosovo's Has district flee toward Albania after Serbian forces order them to leave or be killed; officials estimate that about 10,800 refugees crossed border by 8 AM on March 30 and that they are coming at rate of 2,000 hour; they join 60,000 ethnic Albanians who fled into Albania day before; photo (M)
news.title: Kosovars Flee to Beat Serb Deadline of Death

news.abstract: Growing refugee crisis in Kosovo has left Clinton Administration and NATO officials wondering whether they will be able to achieve their goal of peaceful settlement between Serbs and ethnic Albanians; nearly a third of 1.8 million ethnic Albanians in Kosovo have been forced from their homes by Serbian troops; many refugees have fled to Macedonia, Albania or Montenegro; State Department spokesman James P Rubin says Administration stands by framework of Rambouillet accord, which calls for Kosovo to stay in Serbia as autonomous entity; NATO officials say Kosovo could wind up as separate entity under international protection if allies succeed in subduing Serbian military (M)
news.title: After Kosovo's 'Cleansing': Can Two Sides Ever Coexist?

news.abstract: Update on Kosovo crisis (M)
news.title: KOSOVO UPDATE

news.abstract: Panel of senior UN officials concludes that Iraq has gone from relative affluence to massive poverty since imposition of economic sanctions after Persian Gulf war in 1991 and recommends several steps to alleviate suffering of its people; does not recommend lifting of sanctions, but suggests easing them with specific modifications, which US says it might oppose (M)
news.title: U.N. Panel Seeks to Ease Suffering of Iraq's People

news.abstract: Hillary Rodham Clinton, who is in Marrakesh, Morocco, says that NATO bombing in Yugoslavia is necessary because Serbs planned 'campaign of massive and systematic destruction' against ethnic Albanians in Kosovo; photo (M)
news.title: Hillary Clinton, in Morocco, Says NATO Attack Aims at Stopping Bloodshed

news.abstract: ASIA    INDONESIA: RELIGIOUS RIOTS SPREAD -- Rioting in the remote eastern Indonesian islands of Maluku province spread from Ambon, where hundreds of Christians and Muslims have been killed in the past two months, to the nearby island of Tual. According to reports from Tual, at least two people were killed and 10 were wounded. In Jakarta, soldiers with sticks beat students during a protest, left, against the killing of four activists shortly before the downfall last year of President Suharto.   Seth Mydans (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Zambia's High Court rules that Kenneth D Kaunda, father of modern Zambia and country's President for 27 years, is stateless person; says Kaunda is not Zambian citizen under Constitution because his parents were from former British Nyasaland, now called Malawi; Kaunda has been feuding for years with Pres Frederick J T Chiluba, who replaced him after elections in 1991 (M)
news.title: Founder of Zambia Is Declared Stateless In High Court Ruling

news.abstract: Pentagon says three American infantrymen patrolling Macedonia's border with Kosovo are missing after reporting by radio that they had been surrounded and were under fire; say soldiers, whose names are not released, might have been captured by Serbian forces; CNN broadcasts videotape from Serbian television showing what Serbs identify as three Americans who were reported missing on March 31; soldiers are part of US First Infantry Division, which had about 350 members in Macedonia for years, remnant of United Nations force that is being withdrawn now that thousands of NATO troops are stationed near border; map (M)
news.title: 3 G.I.'s Missing in Macedonia After They Reported Attack

news.abstract: Man in the News sketch of NATO Sec Gen Javier Solana Madariaga notes that he is running air operation against Yugoslavia, biggest one alliance has carried out in its 50 years of existence; Solana was born in Madrid on July 14, 1942 and is former Foreign Minister of Spain; photo (M)
news.title: From Foe to NATO Chief -- Javier Solana Madariaga

news.abstract: Refugees arriving in Albania say Serbian forces are shelling villages, towns and cities in Kosovo; say Pristina, Kosovo capital, is in flames, with widespread death and destruction; Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe says shelling has driven more than 10,000 ethnic Albanians from their homes; says refugees crossed border at Morini, joining 84,600 other refugees who have fled into Albania since crossing was opened on March 27, after being sealed for 11 months; map; photos (M)
news.title: Serbs Shelling Wide Swath of Kosovo

news.abstract: Jakub Krasniqi, spokesman for Kosovo Liberation Army, says guerrillas in Kosovo are aiding NATO forces in targeting in bombing campaign; says ethnic Albanian rebels, severely outnumbered and under-armed, have not launched any offensives aganist Serbian forces since start of bombing; asks for intervention of NATO ground troops, or for West to arm rebels; remarks are aimed at boosting morale of movement, which is badly shaken by Serbian attacks and widespread flight of tens of thousands of civilians (M)
news.title: Albanian Fighters Say They Aid NATO in Spotting Serb Targets

news.abstract: Text of Pres Clinton's speech at Norfolk Naval Air Station on crisis in Kosovo, Serbia (M)
news.title: Clinton's Speech on Kosovo: 'We Also Act to Prevent a Wider War'

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  Kenneth Bacon, the Pentagon spokesman, is as somber, cautious and understated in his press briefings as almost anyone in Washington.
news.title: From NATO, Much Rhetoric and Few Details About the Air Strikes

news.abstract: Three US soldiers captured along Yugoslav-Macedonian border will appear before Yugoslav military court; US says court-martial would be violation of international law; Staff Sgt Andrew A Ramirez, Staff Sgt Christopher J Stone and Specialist Steven M Gonzales are paraded on Serbian state television, which also broadcasts unexpected meeting between Pres Slobodan Milosevic and Ibrahim Rugova, prominent leader of Kosovo's ethnic Albanians and part of delegation that signed Western-drafted peace agreement in Rambouillet, France, that Serbs rejected; both leaders sign document calling for peaceful end to Kosovo crisis through political means; spokesman for ethnic Albanian rebels calls Rugova's meeting high treason; Rugova, re-elected as leader of ethnic Albanians in April and has long advocated nonviolent political solution to problem, reportedly asks protection from Serbian police; some Western diplomats say he may be trying to shore up position and save what is left of Kosovo from catastrophe; he was originally supported by US, but his credibility sharply declined with rise in support for insurgents of Kosovo Liberation Army; Western officials fear Milosevic may reach agreement with him for Kosovo's partition or political autonomy along lines West has drawn, but without presence of NATO peacekeeping troops West has insisted on; Milosevic moves to shore up support in Yugoslav Army by dismissing commander and seven other generals based in sister republic of Montegenro; photos (M)
news.title: Military Court Will Examine Soldiers' Cases

news.abstract: Vast archeological site at Aomori, Japan, is shedding new insights into life of the Jomon people, and revealing unexpected sophistication of culture existing from 10,000 to 300 BC; scientists believe modern Japanese are product of both Jomon people and Yayoi immigrants from China and Korea; map; photo (M)
news.title: Aomori Journal; Out of the Mist Looms, Maybe, the First Japanese

news.abstract: ROME—  Prime Minister Massimo D'Alema of Italy struggled to keep his cabinet together on Friday in the face of a threat by his Communist partners to withdraw its ministers unless a truce in the war between NATO and Yugoslavia was achieved over the Easter weekend.
news.title: D'Alema Faces Communist Walkout Over Easter Bombing

news.abstract: UN aid coordinator David Morton warns that food scarcity engulfing North Korea will worsen in next two months because rations on which majority of population depends are running out, and will not be restocked until summer harvest; says people will have to rely on corn stalks, wild roots and the like; food from abroad is directed mostly to nursery schools, kindergartens and hospitals; Morton describes malnutrition that has stunted most children; photo (S)
news.title: North Korea's Food Near End, Aid Workers Say

news.abstract: Military analysis of NATO's air war over Yugoslavia; politicians and their assessments of public sensitivities have grounded just as many bombing runs as bad weather for most of campaign of past 10 days; commanders have been overruled by civilian bosses, driven by perception of political risks of losing aircraft and pilots, even though they believed military risk of flying low-level attacks was acceptable; diagrams (M)
news.title: 4 Sides in War: Serbs, NATO, Clouds, Politics

news.abstract: Senior US officials say US will have to consider accepting some of hundreds of thousands of ethnic Albanians fleeing Kosovo; State Department reports 'chilling evidence' of 200,000 people being held by Serb forces near train station in Pristina in preparation for forced evacuation; US procedures for admitting refugees explained (M)
news.title: U.S. Grapples With Issue Of Finding Refugees Homes

news.abstract: List of aid organizations taking donations to help Kosovo refugees
news.title: Helping Balkan Refugees

news.abstract: Chinese Prime Min Zhu Rongji, set to visit United States, must face wide range of issues that have soured Congress on strategy of mutual engagement; Chinese, although outraged by American-led bombing of Yugoslavia, decided against delaying trip, sign of how much China still values US ties (M)
news.title: Volatile Issues Await China's Premeir in U.S.

news.abstract: Indian Government begins program to make it easier for people of Indian descent around world to visit and invest in India; stops short of offering dual citizenship and vote (M)
news.title: India Offers Rights to Attract Its Offspring's Cash

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and NATO allies oppose proposal, pressed by growing number of American politicians, to arm Kosovo Liberation Army; are wary of ethnic Albanian rebels because of their political ideologies and questionable commitment to democracy; some in rebel movement are considered hard-line Marxists, others Islamic fundamentalists; NATO allies also fear Russia could see effort to arm rebels as further justification for it to arm Serbs; photo (M)
news.title: NATO Is Wary of Proposals To Help Arm Kosovo Rebels

news.abstract: Russians see Pres Clinton and NATO as villians in Yugoslavia and Pres Slobodan Milosevic as defiant patriot; Russian media focuses on Serbs affected by NATO bombing, while Western media focuses on atrocities against Kosovo's ethnic Albanians; Russian officials strive to steer public opinion against NATO bombing (M)a
news.title: Russians See and Read Another Slant to the War, With Milosevic as a Patriot

news.abstract: Table updates events in Kosovo crisis; map
news.title: KOSOVO UPDATE

news.abstract: Both sides in conflict in Kosovo, Serbia, are bound together in net of terror in which tangled web of history, friendships and enmities, war and routine business underlies explosion in brutality; there is confusion over what is really happening in province as tragedy unfolds and as minutiae of life and death are drowned out by clashing statements from Washington and Belgrade; killings and other atrocities in Suka Reka, among hundreds of small towns caught up in chaos and horror of conflict, described; photos (M)
news.title: Kosovo Killings Bind Both Sides In Net of Terror

news.abstract: NATO bombing of Yugoslavia, which consists of Serbia and Montenegro, opens chasm of resentment and suspicion in Montenegro between supporters of its elected Govt that wants to embrace Western Europe and supporters of Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic, who is defiantly waging war against alliance; bombing of military targets inside Montenegro has handed Milosevic's supporters resonant battle cry, while badly undermining arguments of Montenegro's moderate leadership that good things come by cozying up to West; photo (M)
news.title: Trying to Balance Friendship With the West and Loyalty to Serbia

news.abstract: Many Serb conscripts ordered to report for military duty have gone into hiding; they assert patriotism and denounce NATO while expressing dislike for regime of Pres Slobodan Milosevic (M)
news.title: SERB CONSCRIPTS DRIFT INTO HIDING

news.abstract: Tide of Kosovar refugees swells to 30,000 at camp near Macedonian border, where conditions have deteriorated alarmingly making death and disease commonplace; Macedonian soldiers and police in riot gear are preventing refugees from wandering further into Macedonia; aid agencies report deaths of 25 people over past two days, mostly among old and very young; hepatitis and pneumonia are rampant and sanitation is poor; conditions described; many refugees seem in severe shock from ordeal, and there is growing sense of desperation; many remain trapped on Serbian side of border, which Macedonian Govt has effectively sealed; photo; map; chart (M
news.title: Misery and Disease Sweep Macedonian Camp

news.abstract: Interview with Jose Isidro Rodriguez, Mayor of Zaragoza, El Salvador, who grew up in local orphanage founded by American priest after massacre of mother in 1980 and who is embodiment of country's transformation from war-ravaged state to peaceful democracy; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Zaragoza Journal; War Orphan Is Mayor, and at Peace With Himself

news.abstract: Advance crew of US soldiers prepares camp near Tirana, Albania, from which American troops will coordinate airlift of supplies to ethnic Albanian refugees driven from Kosovo, Serbia (S)
news.title: CRISIS IN THE BALKANS: THE G.I.'S; Airlift Base Takes Shape In Albania

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook column says anti-NATO and especially anti-American feeling has grown steadily among ordinary Serbs with bombing of largely civilian infrastructure targets in Serbia, and that attacks seem to have solidified support behind Pres Slobodan Milosevic; while NATO is formal enemy, Serbs seem to be reserving most of animosity for US--leader of Western alliance; photo (M)
news.title: Serbs Seem to Be Blaming U.S., Not Milosevic

news.abstract: Wang Xizhe, prominent exiled dissident who tried to return to China, is diverted to Thailand by Asiana Airlines, which received warning from Chinese Govt that it would be held responsible for his return (S)
news.title: Beijing Prompts Airline to Divert Dissident

news.abstract: Approximately one million ethnic Albanians are believed still trapped in Kosovo, Serbia, and fate of many is unknown; sporadic telephone calls to relatives in US from those in hiding paint grim picture; once lively provincial capital of Pristina has become ghost town (M)
news.title: Ordeal for Albanians Still in Kosovo

news.abstract: NATO gives military commander, Gen Wesley K Clark, authority he wanted to send 24 American Apache helicopter gunships to Albania, with surface-to-surface missiles and about 2,000 American soldiers who will use them to attack Serbian forces across border in Kosovo; obtains approval for deployment from Albanian authorities; helicopters and missile systems will be in position within week, supplementing bombing campaign allies say is just getting seriously under way as weather has cleared; allies transports fly food and medical supplies to refugee camps along Macedonian border; photos; map (M)
news.title: Anti-Tank Copters Will Go Into Action Against Serbs In Kosovo Soon, Allies Say

news.abstract: Venice Journal on uproar over city's plan to evict 250 cats from their official sanctuary on San Clemente island, which has been sold to real-estate developer; photo; map; powerful animal rights lobby is upset, as is neighborhood where haven is to be relocated; Venetians believe cats helped save city from 1348 plague and treat them with deference; city enacted Italy's first law guaranteeing cats place to live in freedom and providing money for food (M)
news.title: Venice Journal; With Claws Drawn, Italians Duel Over 250 Cats

news.abstract: Russia's chief prosecutor issues arrest warrant for Boris Berezovsky, tycoon and political mover who has taken sensational tumble from graces of Russian high finance and of Pres Boris Yeltsin; Berezovky and Nikolai Glushkov, former Aeroflot official, are charged with money-laundering and diverting foreign currency from airline to company in Geneva that they control; charges may be related to machinations of Yeltsin and prosecutor's office; Berezovsky, in Paris, greets warrant with contempt (S)
news.title: Russian Tycoon (and Yeltsin Adversary) Is Charged With Fraud

news.abstract: Macedonian Government sends Kosovo refugees abroad, some of them against their will, and stories of families being separated in crush and sent to unknown destinations further traumatize those in camps; photos; several hundred refugees go to Turkey, 91 to Norway; some 300-400 cars waiting to cross border are reportedly ordered by Serb police to return to Pristina, apparently to show press that Pres Slobodan Milosevic wants Albanians back (M)
news.title: Many Fear Where They're Going, as Well as Where They've Been

news.abstract: Ambroise Roux, prominent and influential figure in French industrial and financial worlds who was key adviser to Georges Pompidou, France's President from 1969 to 1974, dies at age 77; photo (M)
news.title: Ambroise Roux, 77, Pompidou Adviser and French Management 'Godfather'

news.abstract: NATO bombs accidentally demolish two residential areas in Serbian town of Aleksinac; photos; map; local police report seven people killed and almost 50 others wounded; explosions also damage NATO's reputation for surgical precision in strikes against Slobodan Milosevic and his policies in Kosovo Province; Air Commodore David Wilby says it is possible weapons fell short of target, Serbian army barracks 600 yards away (S)
news.title: Small Serbian Town Is Stricken By a Deadly 'Accident of War'

news.abstract: Disclosure that China may have stolen secrets about neutron bomb from United States in 1995 calls into question Clinton Administration insistence that China's nuclear spying occurred in 1980's, while Republicans held White House, and that Pres Clinton acted quickly when he learned of security breaches in February 1998; bipartisan Congressional report on China's acquisition of United States technology includes detailed, but still secret, account of Beijing's efforts to obtain neutron bomb secrets, including reports of efforts during Clinton Presidency; Clinton Administration has reportedly resisted Congressional requests to make more recent material public; Federal Bureau of Investigation, Central Intelligence Agency and Energy Dept are continuing to examine case; no suspect has been identified (M)
news.title: Intelligence Report Points To 2d China Nuclear Leak

news.abstract: New York Times/CBS News poll finds most Americans expect conflict between Serbia and Kosovo to drag on for months or years, to involve deployment of United States ground troops and to cause loss of American lives; 52 percent of Americans surveyed support Pres Clinton's policy in conflict, but fewer than third think current NATO bombing campaign will stop ethnic cleansing in Kosovo; 46 percent say they favor use of ground troops, while 48 percent are opposed; only 21 percent opt for ground troops when given other options of continuing air attacks or pulling out altogether; backing for ground troops is strongest, at 55 percent, among those who say they follow fighting most closely; but support is slowly growing in general as bombing campaign and plight of refugees are dramatized on television screens; chart (M)
news.title: Americans, in Poll, See U.S. Involvement Growing

news.abstract: Update of situation in Kosovo (M)
news.title: KOSOVO UPDATE

news.abstract: NATO allies open diplomatic offensive aimed at probing for signs that Pres Slobodan Milosevic might be ready to back down, even as they continue air attacks against military targets in Kosovo; foreign ministers of 19 NATO members will meet on Apr 12 to take stock of operation and show their determination to keep bombing until Milosevic accepts political solution; Air Commodore David Wilby claims bombers scored their first major breakthrough against Serbian armored forces attacking Albanian civilians in Kosovo; NATO officials and others wonder what prompted Milosevic to say he had ordered cease-fire, since they see no end to attacks in Kosovo by Yugoslav and Serbian forces; Defense Sec William S Cohen says he has no independent information about statement by Cyprus's Acting Pres Spyros Kyprianou, that he is near reaching deal with Belgrade to release three American soldiers captured last week; photo; map (M)
news.title: NATO BOMBERS HIT SERB FORCES; REFUGEE FLOW HALTS ABRUPTLY: DIPLOMATIC FLURRY
