news.abstract: Many Indonesians see Pres B J Habibie as vestige of despised old order who must be pushed aside before country can truly move on; he is not given credit for freeing press, bringing new respect for human rights and allowing dozens of political parties to compete on newly open electoral playing field; most Indonesians think reform was huge national movement born out of decades of frustration; some think it was former Pres Suharto himself who fostered economic development that allowed nation to mature, to learn and then to reject his paternalistic form of leadership; they feel Habibie was merely in right place at right time; photo; map (M)
news.title: Indonesia Changed, but Who Deserves the Credit?

news.abstract: Analysis of implications of Russia's surprise deployment of troops in Kosovo, as it pertains to Russian foreign policy; if troop decision was made without Pres Boris N Yeltsin's approval, then he no longer has full control of his Government; if Yeltsin did know and approve of plan, it would mean he has tossed aside obligations under international peace agreement barely week old; it would also suggest that Russia in Yeltsin's final year as President is increasingly unreliable and unstable nation driven more by domestic politics and anti-West nationalism than by any internal compass; photo (M)
news.title: Instability in Moscow: Who Is Giving Orders?

news.abstract: Kosovar Albanians in Lugagji, Kosovo, stand by roadside all day in chill rain to cheer and clap at arriving British convoy; they say this is first time they have dared venture out to main road in two and half months; road is highway between Macedonian border and Pristina; while Kosovo's Albanians see NATO peacekeeping deployment as welcome sight, Kosovo's Serbs are downcast and bitter; lead elements on move are British; they will be followed by French, Italian, German and American soldiers who will control various zones throughout Kosovo; photo (M)
news.title: Kosovars Venture Out, Finally, to Welcome NATO Troops

news.abstract: Defense Sec William S Cohen says Pres Boris N Yeltsin authorized early entry of Russian troops into Kosovo, possibly surprising even senior members of his own Government; Cohen declines to characterize presence of Russian troops in Pristina as mistake or case of crossed signals between Moscow and military commanders in Balkans; Cohen insists that Russian troops would have to come under NATO command; White House officials say Pres Clinton is scheduled to speak to Yeltsin as American and Russian diplomats and generals meet in Moscow and Macedonia to try to clarify Russia's role in peacekpeeing force; Moscow has so far balked at putting its troops under direct NATO command; photo (M)
news.title: Cohen Says Yeltsin Authorized Deployment

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II, in Warsaw, explains how Catholics should behave in newly democratic Poland; urges Poles to resist secularism; his tone is gentler, more understanding, than it was in 1991, when he scolded Poles for allowing themselves to be seduced by worst excesses of freedom; since that time, center-right Government coalition has passed laws that are far closer to church teaching, including strict restrictions on abortion; Catholic Church has lost some power it held when it was seen as country's main bastion against Communist authorities, but it remains unusually influential, by European standards; photo of Pope with bandage covering cut on forehead from fall at Vatican Embassy; map (M)
news.title: Pope, Hurt in Fall, Tells Poles to Resist Secularism

news.title: Last Serbian Troops Pull Out of Kosovo

news.abstract: Yuli Edelstein, Israel's Immigration Minister, is among new breed of Israeli politicians; they are younger, from greater diversity of ethnic backgrounds and less likely to be veterans of great Israeli wars, lifelong Zionists or even Jewish; Edelstein is former Soviet refusenik whose father is Russian Orthodox priest; is No. 2 to Natan Sharansky, who is at helm of small but powerful Russian immigrant party; photo (M)
news.title: From Siberia to Israeli Cabinet (No, He's Not Sharansky)

news.abstract: Kamal Eddin Hussein, Egyptian army officer who helped to overthrow King Farouk of Egypt in 1952 and became Vice President of Egypt, dies at age 77; photo (M)
news.title: Kamal Eddin Hussein, 77, Figure In Coup Against Farouk in 1952

news.abstract: Dozens of Serbs in civilian dress, who call themselves 'warrior citizens,' prevent ethnic Albanians for third consecutive day from entering predominantly Serbian sector of northern Kosovo industrial town of Mitrovica, jeering and threatening any who dared to enter; declare about one-third of city and predominantly Serbian towns to north 'Serbian zone' in direct challenge to NATO authority; NATO officials say present strategy is to avoid confronting Serbs in hope situation will calm over time; photo (M)
news.title: NATO's Peacekeeping Force, Defied by Both Sides, Struggles to Keep Order

news.abstract: ASIA    INDIA, PAKISTAN: MORE FIGHTING -- Indian soldiers cleared Islamic guerrillas from another Himalayan outpost yesterday, a day after driving them from the highest peak overlooking India's northern highway in Kashmir, an Indian spokesman said. India has reported steady progress in pushing back the fighters, who it says infiltrated from Pakistan in an attempt to change the 1972 cease-fire line that divides the region. Western nations have been pressing the two nuclear powers to settle the dispute peacefully. (AP)    CAMBODIA: 2 CHARGED IN TOURISTS' KILLING -- Two former Khmer Rouge guerrillas who were later commissioned in the Cambodian Army, Sam Bith, top, and Chhouk Rin, have been formally charged in the killing of three backpackers in 1994, a state prosecutor said. The two were arraigned in Phnom Penh Municipal Court two weeks after another former guerrilla, Nuon Paet, was sentenced to life in prison for ordering the killing of the three tourists, David Wilson of Australia, Mark Slater of Britain and Jean-Michel Braquet of France. The three, all in their mid-20s, were abducted from a train on July 26, 1994. (AP)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: UN Committee for Nongovernmental Organizations, led by small group of developing nations, inflicts major setbacks on human rights groups that seek to expose and combat political oppression; withdraws accreditation of Zurich-based Christian Solidarity International and refuses accreditation, amid lobbying by China, to Human Rights in China, New York organization that monitors abuses in China; reverses occur as enforcement of norms of human rights seems to be growing, following 1998 decision to establish international criminal court and tribunals to judge those responsible for genocide; group of organizations led by Human Rights Watch of New York plan new campaign to bring more exiled dictators and other leaders accused of human rights abuses to justice in their own countries or those that extend asylum (M)
news.title: U.N. Committee, Under Pressure, Limits Rights Groups

news.abstract: News analysis: will of Indonesian people may in large part be denied, regardless of outcome of vote count in recent Parliamentary election; country's complex electoral system does not guarantee victory for challengers, even those who win most votes; none of current candidates are reformers at heart even though reform has been watchword of election campaign (M)
news.title: Indonesia's Vote: Reformers May Be Disappointed

news.abstract: NATO Gen Wesley K Clark, visiting Macedonia with Pres Clinton, calls on NATO allies to move quickly to flood Kosovo with peacekeepers as acts of violence and retribution continue in province; suggests that more than 50,000 peacekeepers orginally planned might be needed; some Army forces under his own command apparently may be slow in leaving Germany for Balkans; NATO troops have become increasingly visible in Kosovo's major cities, but are seen only sporatically in smaller, remote villages racked by tensions (M)
news.title: Top General Would Speed Deployment For Kosovo

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder is due to announce Wednesday an unpopular austerity plan that political analysts view as the last chance for his shaky coalition government to revive Europe's biggest economy.
news.title: Austerity Plan to Test Schroeder's Government

news.abstract: Warren Rudman, who heads Pres Clinton's foreign intelligence advisory board, tells unusual joint hearing of four Senate committees that blame for lax security at weapons labs that enabled China to acquire nuclear weapons design secrets is widespread and bipartisan and requires independent solution; Energy Sec Bill Richardson opposes creating semi-autonomous agency within Energy Department to oversee nuclear arms programs; instead backs creation of department undersecretary to take control of programs; Richardson and Rudman later testify before House Commerce Committee (M)
news.title: In Wake of Espionage, Debate On New Nuclear Arms Agency

news.abstract: Organizers of United Nations meeting on year 2000 computer problems say disruptions are unlikely to be as widespread or serious as earlier feared; Amb Ahmad Kamal, who heads UN working group on information technology, says corrective action is under way everywhere; delegates from 173 nations attended meeting, up from 120 at first meeting in Dec; organizers say regional sessions that led up to meeting could spur international cooperation on technical issues long after year 2000 challenge has passed (M)
news.title: More Countries Studying Year 2000 Disruptions, U.N. Panel Finds

news.abstract: Pres Eduardo Frei of Chile overhauls Cabinet and sets economic stimulus package; responds to rising unemployment and increasingly tense relations with military upset over Government's inability to bring home Gen Augusto Pinochet, former dictator under house arrest in Britain; unexpected moves are aimed at boosting Government's declining credibility and aiding presidential campaign of Christian Democrat-Socialist coalition candidate, Ricardo Lagos (M)
news.title: Chile Leader Moves to Aid His Economy, And Prestige

news.abstract: HONG KONG—  As investors stampeded out of Asia in 1997, igniting a global financial crisis after Thailand floated its currency, many analysts concluded that the world had been too sanguine about foreign-exchange risk and its potential to wreak havoc on capital markets and national economies.
news.title: As Yen Weakens, Japan's Neighbors Begin to Worry

news.abstract: Planje, Kosovo, was more or less leveled in near-daily attacks by NATO planes in weeks before peace agreement was signed with Serbia; residents who are returning to village say they blame Serbia for destruction, not NATO; photo (M)
news.title: Even in Towns NATO Hit, Albanians Fault Serbs

news.abstract: Japan's $16 billion defense industry in theory has been partly opened to foreign competition, but analysts say odds are heavily stacked in favor of local companies; they say that couple of contracts can mean life or death of weapons division of Japanese company in these hard economic times (M)
news.title: In Arms Sales, Japan Coddles Its Own

news.abstract: Government officials say middle-level analyst in Central Intelligence Agency raised doubts about whether military planners were zeroing in on right building shortly before US bombs struck Chinese Embassy in Belgrade on May 7; Clinton Administration begins to brief Congress about internal investigation of bombing; briefing includes account of analyst's warning; Administration recently provided similar reconstruction to Chinese officials; strike, which killed three Chinese and wounded at least 20 others, was serious setback to relations with China (M)
news.title: C.I.A. Analyst Questioned Target Before Chinese Embassy Bombing

news.abstract: US officials say local Serbs in civilian clothes opened fire on checkpoint run by US marines in Zegra, Kosovo, provoking firefight that left one Serb dead and two others wounded; say fourth Serb was arrested after marines stormed house where Serbs had retreated; say no marines were wounded; gunfire underscores volatility of NATO's operation in Kosovo, 12 days after peacekeepers first arrived; it is second time that US troops have come under direct fire; photo (M)
news.title: Serb Is Killed In Gun Battle With Marines

news.abstract: Current and former commanders in Kosovo Libveration Army, and some Western diplomats, say that senior commanders of rebel army, which signed disarmament agreement with NATO, carried out assassinations, arrests and purges within their ranks to thwart potential rivals; say that campaign, in which as many as half dozen top rebel commanders were shot dead, was directed by Hashim Thaci and two of his lieutenants, Azem Syla and Xhavit Haliti; Thaci denies, through spokesman, that he was responsible for any such killings; photo (L)
news.title: Leaders of Kosovo Rebels Tied to Deadly Power Play

news.abstract: Fears about Hong Kong's future as an Asian trading post grow since United States Senate moved to tighten controls on exports to Hong Kong in response to a Congressional report on military espionage and China; Senate approves legislation that would impose more stringent controls on export of equipment and technology with military uses to Hong Kong and Macao unless both territories allow United States to verify that sensitive shipments end up in right hands (M)
news.title: U.S. Move Has Hong Kong Worried It Will Lose Trade

news.abstract: Some villages across Kosovo are gripped by new contortion of fear, violence and retribution, following United States marines' firefight with Serbs that kills one Serb and wounds two others; virtually every Serb in village of Zegra, Kosovo, leaves, most in single, bedraggled column of cars, trucks and trailers, some pulled by tractors, others by oxen or horses; as they leave, ignoring entreaties of their Orthodox priest to stay, smoke and flames pour from at least a dozen houses (L)
news.title: Serbs Flee While Albanians Loot, And Marines Find Peace Is Tricky

news.abstract: Update on developments in Kosovo (S)
news.title: KOSOVO UPDATE

news.abstract: Protest leaders at National Autonomous University, Mexico's biggest university, seek more power for students and oppose Mexico's shift away from welfare state; student strike began on April 21 as protest against plan by administration to make those who could afford it pay tuition; university's president, Francisco Barnes de Castro, admitted defeat and agreed to make all tuition payments voluntary after seven weeks; but student strikers were not satisfied, and strike, which closed down classrooms for 270,000 students, is now in its third month and shows no sign of moving towards resolution; photos (L)
news.title: Student Strike in Capital Jarring All of Mexico

news.abstract: Tense calm prevails along border between Israel and Lebanon after Israel's most severe bombardment of Lebanon since 1996; civilians on both sides wait for next rocket or bomb to fall; photos; map (M)
news.title: Lebanon And Israel Still Tense After Clash

news.abstract: German Parliament approves plan for building of vast memorial in heart of Berlin to six million Jewish victims of Holocaust; vote opens way for construction near Brandenburg Gate of project designed by New York architect Peter Eisenman; it will combine field of more than 2,000 stone pillars with building that is officially being called 'documentation center' but will have many of attributes of a Holocaust museum; photo of model of design (M)
news.title: Berlin Holocaust Memorial Approved

news.abstract: British Broadcasting Corp stirs passionate debate by appointing Greg Dyke, head of Pearson Television, as its next director general; Conservative opposition questions BBC's independence, and many fear a 'dumbing down' of BBC programs in view of Pearson's association with shows like Baywatch and a puppet called Roland Rat; appointment focuses attention anew on $87,000 that Dyke has donated in recent years to political campaigns of Prime Min Tony Blair and his followers (M)
news.title: BBC Chooses Ally of Blair As Director, To Tories' Ire

news.abstract: Natan Sharansky, Russian immigrant leader, will be next Interior Minister in Israel, wresting control of powerful ministry from ultra-Orthodox Shas Party, which has held it for years; Sharansky, whose party campaigned for Interior Ministry, signs agreement to join coalition Government of Prime Min-elect Ehud Barak (S)
news.title: Israel Moves To Coalition, And Changes Are in Offing

news.abstract: Russia moves step closer toward securing new $4.5 billion loan from IMF when Communist-dominated Parliament passes several laws to raise Government revenue and restructure collapsed banking sector; Russia has not done everything IMF has demanded (S)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Vast destruction by Serbs of ethnic Albanian property in Kosovo has barely begun to be tallied; costs of physical reconstruction are unknown; hopes of progress in impoverished region are set back years, if not decades; destruction, mostly confined to rural areas before Mar 24 start of NATO bombing, shifted to cities and intensified after bombing as Serbs apparently sought revenge and to drive Albanians away for good; map; photo (M)
news.title: In the Rubble That Was Kosovo, Damage Tally Has Barely Begun

news.abstract: Senior White House officials were informed that China might have stolen American nuclear secrets in 1995, nearly a year earlier than the Clinton Administration originally disclosed, officials now say.
news.title: When U.S. Learned Of China Spy Charge

news.abstract: State-controlled television that Slobodan Milosevic has used so masterfullly for last decade is now portraying a tranquil Kosovo, promoting Serbian defeat as victory and focusing on reconstruction, leaving millions of Serbs in ignorance or confused denial; but as pace of misleading information accelerates, there are indications that credibility of Milosevic's programming is beginning to slide, particularly as it becomes more difficult for government to hide both its lack of money and the flood of refugees who have fled north from Kosovo; photo (Belgrade Journal) (M)
news.title: Live, in Belgrade, the Milosevic News

news.abstract: Linda S Shenwick, administrative and budget officer at United States Mission to United Nations, is accused of 'insubordination' and threatened with immediate transfer; State Department officials say Shenwick funneled damaging information to Congressional Republicans and reporters in effort to sabotage Clinton Administration effort to pay $1 billion in back dues to UN; her lawyer, Victoria Toensing, says Shenwick is classic whistle-blower who is being punished for exposing waste and fraud (M)
news.title: U.S. Tries to Punish Aide Over U.N. Leaks

news.abstract: NATO peacekeepers reopen airport in Pristina, Kosovo, clearing way for regular flights of troops, supplies, and, eventually, civilians; first military aircraft, a Russian cargo plane, lands; photo (M)
news.title: Peacekeepers, at Last, Reopen Pristina Airport

news.abstract: Russian and American officials say blisteringly hot summer and reverberations from Russia's economic crisis are taking devastating toll on nation's crops, making it likely that Moscow will appeal for American food aid (M)
news.title: Tough Year Is Projected For Farms Of Russia

news.abstract: Hundreds of nongovernmental organizations in Indonesia, notably Urban Poor Consortium led by Wardah Hafidz, have been boldly pushing their agendas since forced resignation of Pres Suharto in 1998; goals include human rights, environmental protection, workers' protection, legal aid and political freedoms as well as rights for poor; are one building block of new civil society, part of transformation of Indonesia that is realigning patters of power; photo (M)
news.title: Activists Thrust Agendas Into Post-Suharto Void

news.abstract: King Hassan II, who has ruled Morocco despotically for past 38 years, is recasting image as author of 'Hassanian democracy,' hybrid that has widened political freedoms while retaining paramount political power of Alawite dynasty that he heads; has established elected lower house of Parliament, in which leftist parties gained largest bloc of seats in elections in 1998; has ordered cleanup of country's human rights record to include release of dozens of political prisoners and payments of $500-per-month compensation to families of prisoners who disappeared or died; has retained curbs on hard-line Islamists, who are forbidden by King to form political parties or to contest elections; while palace officials acknowledge his absence from public view is because of ill health, they deny suggestions from Western diplomats that Hassan is seriously ill; photo; map (L)
news.title: Morocco's King Loosens His Grip, and Holds On

news.abstract: David Trimble, First Minister of Northern Ireland Assembly, says stalled peace effort in Ulster can be saved by simple statement from Sinn Fein, political wing of the Irish Republican Army, that IRA is committed to disarming by May 2000; photo (M)
news.title: In Ulster, Hints of a Shift to Save Peace Effort

news.abstract: Discontent is growing in Croatia under Pres Franjo Tudjman, whose virulent nationalism and penchant for domination of ethnically pure state is exceeded in Balkans only by Slobodan Milosevic in Yugoslavia; his efforts to radiate new Croatian glory, at time when economy is near collapse, has met with public outrage; opinion polls suggest his ruling Christian Democratic Union will be trounced by opposition by margin of 2-to-1 in parliamentary elections later in 1999; map; photo (M)
news.title: Croatia's President Polishes a National Myth

news.abstract: Israel's rightist Likud Party withdraws from coalition talks with Prime Min-elect Ehud Barak, announcing that it will not join his government and is headed for opposition; move defines contours of Barak's emerging coalition as he negotiates with Shas, ultra-Orthodox party of Sephardic Jews that is third-largest faction in Parliament and likely partner in new Govt; Barak has already reached agreements with three parties and accord with Shas would give Barak 77-seat majority in 120-seat Parliament; Shas relatively dovish positions on peace talks and territorial compromise with palestinbians contrasts with Likud's harder line (M)
news.title: Likud Decides Not to Join A Coalition Led by Barak

news.abstract: Negotiations to end 11-month-old war in Congo inch forward as foreign and defense ministers of all the nations involved in conflict meet in Zambia to discuss draft text for cease-fire; talks, already days behind, break up within two hours; Congo and Zimbabwe, one of its allies, reportedly objected to parts of document, which was hammered out by lower level officials (M)
news.title: Mixed Results at Congo Cease-Fire Talks

news.abstract: World Health Organization says approximately one-third to half aid provided by corporate America and others for more than million of ethnic Albanian refugees who feld Kosovo, Serbia, is inappropriate and likely to gather dust in warehouses or be destroyed at government expense; critics from international relief agencies say problem arises because there are far too many incentives for companies to empty out warehouses, regardless of need, and for charities to ferry it along; are angered over what they regard as attitude, especially prevalent among American donors, that any gift is better than none (M)
news.title: In a Wave of Balkan Charity Comes Drug Aid of Little Use

news.abstract: Chinese Govt is worried over Falun Gong, or Buddhist Law, organization that melds Buddhism, meditation, Chinese exercise techniques and mystical ideas of exiled founder, Li Hongzhi, into wildly popular movement; has been involved in subtle battle of words and wills with group since 10,000 members unexpectedly staged illegal sit-in around Beijing's leadership compound, demanding official tolerance and recognition; claiming tens of millions of ardent folowers in China, Buddhist Law has emerged as powerful if hard-to-define force to be reckoned with; group has no obvious political agenda and claims only loose organization, but demonstration in April displayed enormous power to move its members aned ability to embarrass Communist Party if it does not get its way; photos (M)
news.title: Beijing Journal; Group's Morning Exercises Are Politically Suspect

news.abstract: International study, sponsored by Council on Foreign Relations in New York and paid for by European Commission and Govt of Norway, criticizes Yasir Arafat's concentration of executive power, while expressing compassion for Palestinian Authority; says Palestine Liberation Organization president has concentrated power so effectively that he personally approves all senior officials' vacations and their per diem expenses; says he has used Govt to ease unemployment and to reward political loyalty to such extent that public sector is bloated, inefficient and risks incurring staggering debts to pay expenses; says Palestine Legislative Council is relatively impotent, judiciary is in disarray, unregulated monopolies rule many industries and police force abuses its powers; its other findings and recommendations discussed (M)
news.title: Panel Criticizes Extent of Arafat's Power

news.abstract: MILAN—  Today's well-dressed man with money to burn can afford to look flash, but the fashion statement he prefers to project is the look of low-key luxury.
news.title: Low-Key Luxury Is In, and Italy's Fabric Maestros Can Supply It

news.abstract: Catholicos Karekin I, spiritual leader of Armenian Orthodox Christians worldwide, dies at age 66; photo (M)
news.title: Karekin I, Armenian Patriarch, Dies at 66

news.abstract: Advertising drive ordered by United States court opens to inform victims of Nazi persecution how to claim compensation from $1.25 billion fund set up by Union Bank of Switzerland and Credit Suisse; people can apply even if they or relatives never had Swiss account; World Jewish Congress and panel of lawyers oversee effort (M)
news.title: Nazi Victims Get Details on Compensation Claims

news.abstract: Scene at former Tuol Sleng prison, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, described; prison, preserved unrestored as museum since Khmer Rouge fled in 1979, was used as torture chamber by Duch (Kang Kek Ieu), who now awaits trial; photo (M)
news.title: Phnom Penh Journal; Coming Khmer Rouge Trial Rouses Jail's Ghosts

news.abstract: Armed robbers ambush officers of elite Presidential Guard near Pres Ernesto Zedillo's residence, Mexico City, Mex, stealing $50,000 military payroll, killing two soldiers and wounding two; brazen midday attack seems certain to spur view that crime, key issue in state and national elections, is out of control (M)
news.title: Robbers Hit Zedillo Presidential Guard, Kill 2 and Steal Payroll

news.abstract: National Security Council aide says Russian bombers flew close enough to Iceland and Norway last week, during Russia's largest military exercise since Soviet Union's breakup, to cause United States and Norway to scramble fighter planes as precaution; say Russians apparently did not violate Iceland's or Norway's air space in incidents reminiscent of cold war confrontations; sees incidents linked to recent tensions over Russia's role in Kosovo (M)
news.title: Russian Bombers Face Off Against American Fighters

news.abstract: United Nations General Assembly begins debating action plan first drawn up five years ago to limit world population growth, although developing countries remain deeply divided over some aspects of plan; Sec Gen Kofi Annan cites importance of stabilizing population (S)
news.title: U.N. Takes Up Plan to Limit Population

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min-elect Ehud Barak forges broad coalition Government, clinching last deal with ultra-Orthodox Shas Party; Government will consist of seven extremely different parties, mixing secular with religious, left with right and settlers with backers of Palestinian state; is widely expected to back Barak's plan to move forward on peace deals with Palestinians and Syria; Barak will be own Defense Minister; table (M)
news.title: Barak Creates Wide Coalition With 7 Parties

news.abstract: PARIS—  If you flinch every time you hear an electronic approximation of Beethoven's "Fuer Elise" on a mobile telephone, you will be grateful that few mobile-phone operators have installed widespread networks in underground metro systems around the world.
news.title: New Frontier for Mobile-Phone Operators Lies Underground

news.abstract: No incidents are reported in Turkey in wake of death sentence given to Kurdish rebel leader, Abdullah Ocalan; police remain on alert; Kurds stage demonstrations in several European cities and in Australia, but none escalate into serious violence; several arson attacks are reported on Turkish businesses in Germany (M)
news.title: Turkey Reports No Strife After Kurd's Sentence

news.abstract: Joshua Nkomo, once-fiery African nationalist and guerrilla leader who was father to Zimbabwe's struggle for independence, dies at age 62; photo (M)
news.title: Joshua Nkomo of Zimbabwe Is Dead at 62

news.abstract: LONDON—  After seasons of gray, gray and more gray, bright color is making a comeback. Menswear designers are showing a rainbow of colors on the runways of Europe for spring 2000. But the question remains: Will men buy it?
news.title: It Is Bright, but Will Men Wear It?: Color Is Back as Men Rediscover Their 'Inner Peacock'

news.abstract: Senate majority leader Trent Lott, with at least three Senators blocking final vote to confirm Richard C Holbrooke as chief American diplomat at United Nations, says that nomination 'has some problems' but that Holbrooke is still likely to be confirmed; identity of only one of Senators blocking nomination is known publicly: Sen Charles E Grassley, Iowa Republican, who has said that he will prevent vote on Holbrooke's nomination until State Dept resolves unrelated dispute with employee described as whistle-blower (S)
news.title: Lott Says That, Despite Snags, Holbrooke Is Likely to Be Confirmed

news.abstract: MILAN—  The Italian menswear season, which closes Friday, has been about romancing the male. The fashion appeal has two aspects: sex and sport. And there are twin team-leaders: Gucci and Prada.
news.title: Gucci's Glam Slam vs. Prada's Vanity Sportswear

news.abstract: Technological advances that have made personal computers as powerful as supercomputers were just a few years ago prompted President Clinton to greatly ease restrictions on exports of high-speed machines to countries like Russia and China.      Article, page A4.
news.title: P.C. Exports Eased

news.abstract: Prime Min-elect Ehud Barak of Israel, who will be sworn in on July 7, is emerging from behind scenes to take his place as country's leader; Barak telephones Yasir Arafat, Palestinian leader, for their first official conversation; two make date to meet 'soon' and to restart stagnant peace effort; Barak also reproaches Pres Clinton for his seemingly offhand remark about wanting Palestinian refugees to live wherever they want to live; ultimate disposition of Palestian refugees has been left for final status talks, which have not yet begun (M)
news.title: Next Israeli Leader Steps Out of His Silence

news.abstract: French appeals court rejects requests for further investigation into car crash in Paris that killed Princess Diana and Mohamed (Dodi) al-Fayed and their driver in 1997; investigating judges and prosecutors must now decide whether to bring charges in case (S)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Robert B Polhill, American business professor who was held hostage for 39 months in Lebanon, dies at age 65; Polhill, former heavy smoker, learned he had throat cancer four days after he was freed in April 1990 (S)
news.title: Robert Polhill, 65, Lebanon Hostage for 3 Years

news.abstract: United States and its NATO allies are blocking Russia from flying hundreds of troops into Kosovo before details of Russia's role in peacekeeping force could be worked out; Russia has been denied use of airspace over Hungary, Romania and Bulgaria to fly planeloads of peacekeepers into Pristina, after those nations consulted with American and NATO officials; Hungary is new member of NATO, and Romania and Bulgaria seek to join it; Russian military negotiators are trying to alter agreement reached in Helsinki, by having their troops in Kosovo report only to Russian officers, rather than be under formal command of NATO; Russia also wants to station forces in Italian, French, American and German sectors of Kosovo; Clinton Administration officials say they want no more surprises from Russia, given its surprise deployment of 200 troops to Pristina airport last month (M)
news.title: NATO BARS RUSSIA FROM REINFORCING TROOPS IN KOSOVO

news.abstract: Tibetans have three principal ways to return their dead to earth; in sky burial, body is dismembered and fed to vultures; in water burial, corpse is cut into small pieces and fed to fish; third way, cremation, is too expensive for poorest Tibetans; photo; map (M)
news.title: Lirong Journal; Tibetans, and Vultures, Keep Ancient Burial Rite

news.abstract: Nicholas W Leeson, the Rogue Trader who brought down Barings merchant bank in 1995, is set to fly back to Britain after almost four years in a Singapore jail for fraud and forgery; his assets are reportedly frozen, his future is unclear and his freedom flawed by reports that he bragged in prison about having stashed away millions from the days when he traded fast and loose in Singapore; photo (M)
news.title: Britain Awaits Rogue Trader With Interest In the Spoils

news.abstract: Kuwaitis are voting in what may be country's last all-male elections, after a campaign dominated by heated national discussion of whether it is time to allow women political rights; many candidates for seats in Parliament vow to block decree by the Emir, Sheik Jaber al-Ahmed al-Sabah, that would allow Kuwaiti women to vote in next election (M)
news.title: Suffrage Issue Dominating a Kuwait Election

news.abstract: Warren Hoge analysis of the deadlock that has halted progress in putting peace accord into place in Northern Ireland and the decision by Prime Ministers Tony Blair of Britain and Bertie Ahern of Ireland to issue their own solution to the impasse and demand that Ulster politicians accept it or lose their right to govern themselves (M)
news.title: Roadblock to a Peace Pact: Irish Mostly Say 'No'

news.abstract: Some Serbian Orthodox Church priests are demanding resignation of Slobodan Milosevic as Yugoslav President, but the church continues to give priests a mixed message on what they should do in toppling a President who is an indicted war criminal; church, which supported Milosevic's wars against Croatia and Bosnia, still embraces his nationalist aspirations, while rejecting the savage means he uses to achieve them; photo of Patriarch Pavle, who has called Milosevic's policies in Kosovo criminal (M)
news.title: Church of Milosevic's Rise Now Sends Mixed Message

news.abstract: Fragile efforts begun in February to build trust between India and Pakistan are thwarted by operation of Pakistani military aimed at taking craggy peaks in Indian-held Kashmir that overlook a crucial Indian supply line; sense of betrayal runs deep on Indian side; experts believe that the likeliest explanation is that the push for the Kargil operation came from Pakistan's military and that Prime Min Nawaz Sharif went along, enthusiastically or not, believing Pakistan could plausibly deny authorship (M)
news.title: Kashmir Thwarts India-Pakistan Attempt at Trust

news.abstract: Serbian women in unprecedented numbers are deciding not to have children, primiarly because of anxiety about the war in Kosovo, fear of civil war in Serbia and unwillingness to raise children in a nation whose standard of living has declined every year for the past decade; abortion rate appears to be rising sharply and increasing numbers of young women are telling doctors they do not want to give birth; photo; map (M)
news.title: Stresses of Milosevic's Rule Blamed for Decline in Births

news.abstract: Zoran Djindjic, Serbian opposition figure who fled country during war with NATO, returns and dares Pres Slobodan Milosevic to arrest him; faces up to 20 years in prison for avoiding military service during Kosovo war, as well as daunting political problems inside fractured opposition movement; photo (M)
news.title: Key Foe, Back From Exile, Dares Milosevic to Jail Him

news.abstract: Nicholas W Leeson, arriving in Britain after four years in a Singapore jail, says he is sorry for the wild securities trading he engaged in that brought down Barings Bank; Barings liquidators allow him access to $7,900 a month of his money; Barings' creditors want to know about his financial gains from 1996 memoir (M)
news.title: Trader Who Broke Barings Is Back in Britain From Asian Jail

news.abstract: Surprise trip to Russia by Pres Hafez al-Assad of Syria is seen as first step in an expected flurry of Middle East diplomacy as Arab and Israeli leaders jockey for position in peace effort that is suddenly showing signs of life for the first time in three years (M)
news.title: Syrian President Due in Russia Today as Mideast Diplomacy Starts to Revive

news.abstract: Pres Clinton and Prime Min Nawaz Sharif of Pakistan meet for three hours, after which Administration officials say they expect Pakistani-backed forced to soon withdraw from their mountain redoubt on Indians side of cease-fire line in Kashmir; officials are uncertain whether Sharif will be able to guarantee a withdrawal of forces because people of Pakistan and its military leaders are likely to resist backing down and because Sharif does not have full control over the mountain fighters or even his own military command, which has run the Government overtly or from the shadows for much of its history; photo (M)
news.title: U.S.  IS  EXPECTING KASHMIR PULLBACK BY PAKISTANI SIDE

news.abstract: Bodies of 64 ethnic Albanians, slain by Serbs in village of Bela Crkva hours after NATO bombing began on March 25, are reburied following exhumation from mass graves for collection of evidence by war crimes investigators from Scotland Yard; emotional scene described; Scotland Yard's chief investigator John T Bunn says 60 victims were shot in individual groups, in deliberate fashion, along riverbank; photos (M)
news.title: After Scotland Yard Inquiry, A Village in Kosovo Buries 64

news.abstract: Dire predictions of Nostradamus that apocalypse will descend across swath of northern Europe on August 11 speeds exodus of French residents on annual five-week vacations; many are heeding advice of well-known designer Paco Rabanne in best-selling book, 1999: Fire From the Heavens, to stay at least 60 kilometers from Paris; photo (M)
news.title: Paris Journal; An Old Prediction Speeds France's Annual Exodus

news.abstract: News analysis: Pakistan's Prime Min Nawaz Sharif is likely to find it difficult to deliver on pledge to US following White House meeting with Pres Clinton to withdraw Pakistani-backed forces from Indian side of cease-fire line in disputed territory of Kashmir; few Pakistanis see Sharif's sudden decision to visit Clinton, and pledge to take concrete steps to restore cease-fire line, as breakthrough that could end limited, undeclared war with India; most see it either as sell-out of Kashmir cause or another ill-fated move in diplomatic game of chess; photo (M)
news.title: Pakistani's Pullout Vow: A Very Hard Sell at Home

news.abstract: Interview with J Brian Atwood, outgoing administrator of Agency for International Development, who issues unusually harsh assessment of Clinton Administration and Congress, faulting them for aid budget he says is dangerously inadequate; accuses Administration of allowing itself to be pushed around by Congress, and warns legislative cuts in foreign aid have created crisis for US; photo (M)
news.title: Departing Foreign Aid Chief Says Cuts Are Dangerous

news.abstract: EUROPE    NORTHERN IRELAND: BLAIR CLARIFICATION -- Seeking to shore up wavering Protestant support for his blueprint for setting up the new Northern Ireland government this month, Prime Minister Tony Blair told the House of Commons that Sinn Fein would have to give up its cabinet positions if its I.R.A. allies did not disarm on schedule. Mr. Blair issued the clarification in a speech arguing that the plan, negotiated in Belfast last week, was the best opportunity for peace this generation of Britons would ever have.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Ehud Barak is sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel, and he pledges in his inaugural speech that pursuit of true, lasting peace will be his foremost concern; reaches out to all his domestic constituencies; speaks of pain and death on both sides of Israeli-Palestinian conflict and suggests that both sides stop focusing on settling of historical wrongs; says he will move forward on both peace tracks at once in effort to allay fears of Palestinians that negotiations with Syria will take precedence; repeats campaign promise to withdraw Israeli troops from southern Lebanon within a year; his words are received by Palestinians in Gaza as welcome break from perceived hostility of his predecessor, Benjamin Netanyahu, and Palestinian leaders express cautious optimism; photos (M)
news.title: VOWING TO PURSUE PEACE WITH ARABS, BARAK TAKES OVER

news.abstract: Forty younger members of German Green Party issue manifesto scoring 'moralizing know-it-alls' from founding generation of 1960's; are demanding resignation of top leader, Jurgen Trittin, who is also German Environment Minister (M)
news.title: Old Greens In Germany Challenged By Upstarts

news.abstract: United Nations and India struggle to resolve dispute over closing of airport in Indian city of Srinagar that India closed to international civilian traffic when fighting erupted in Kashmir in May; dispute ostensibly involves UN use of airport, which lies south of line that divides hostile Indian and Pakistani forces in Kashmir; also reflects far broader tensions between UN and India, which has refused since 1972 to recognize UN involvement in fate of disputed Himalayan territory; map (M)
news.title: India and U.N. Working On Kashmir Plane Rules

news.abstract: Clinton Administration moves quietly to expand contacts between US and Cuba, pressing modest opening that largely sidesteps Government of Pres Fidel Castro; is seeking mainly to ease hardships of Cuban people and allow certain Americans to visit Cuba, open offices there and send money, food and medicine more freely; will lift more restrictions on money transfers and travel and announce start of direct charter flights between Havana and New York and Los Angeles--in addition to those that operate from Miami; moves follow agreement between US and Cuba to begin working more closely to combat sharp rise in drug trafficking in and around island and to take other steps to foster more cooperation; fall well within limits on American policy set in 1992 and 1996 by laws that stiffened 37-year-old embargo on island (M)
news.title: U.S., Avoiding Castro, Relaxes Rules on Cuba

news.abstract: More than 10,000 people in Uzice, Serbia, hold demonstration against Pres Slobodan Milosevic, defying police who declared the rally illegal; Zoran Djindjic, opposition leader, tells crowd that he fled country during Kosovo war because of death threats from Serbian paramilitary; says there will be daily demonstrations in cities across Serbia; says he expects Serbian Orthodox Church, which recently demanded Milosevic's resignation, to join opposition in calling for nationwide general strike; photo; map (M)
news.title: In Provincial Serbian Town, 10,000 Say 'No' to Milosevic

news.abstract: United Nations official Kevin M Kennedy say at least six people have died and 15,000 to 20,000 have fled homes in ethnic conflict on Guadalcanal, Solomon Islands, interview; says UN will back mediation effort and help aid refugees; refugees say small bands of lightly armed militants belonging to Gwale majority have driven most of minority population of Malaitan villagers from countryside to capital, Honiara, whose population is mainly from island of Malaita; UN sent mission in response to appeal from Prime Min Bartholomew Ulufa'alu, Malaitan, who asked Commonweath to mediate; Sitiveni Rabuka, Fiji's former Prime Minister, has been trying to negotiate end to violence; map (M)
news.title: 6 Are Killed in Ethnic Strife in Solomon Islands

news.abstract: Brazilian Congress adjourns for midwinter recess after session marked by squabbling among four parties that supposedly back Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso; infighting sapped his personal prestige and stalled progress on bills needed to keep International Monetary Fund economic rescue package on track; Cardoso has shown himself reluctant to exert authority when nominal allies misbehave or fail to keep promises; photo (M)
news.title: Brazil's Leader Undercut By His Quarreling Allies

news.abstract: Grigory Pasko, military journalist and Russian Navy captain jailed after documenting Navy's practice of dumping nuclear waste at sea, chronicles dismal life in overcrowded and disease-infested prison on popular political news site on Internet; verdict in his long-running trial is expected this month; photo (M)
news.title: Imprisoned Russian Writer Puts the Gulag on Line

news.abstract: PARIS—  People around the world who want to buy books in English know about Amazon.com and its arch-competitor, barnesandnoble.com. Both of those on-line booksellers do substantial mail-order business outside the United States. The Web has made available millions of books that were previously hard to come by outside English-speaking countries.
news.title: For Books, It Pays To Surf Around

news.abstract: North Korea's news media is going all out to hail 5th anniversary of Pres Kim Il Sung's death and pass mantle of authority to his son, Kim Jong Il; claim flowers are blossoming out of season to mark anniversary (M)
news.title: All Nature Mourns Late Leader, North Korea Says

news.abstract: EUROPE    NORTHERN IRELAND: DUBLIN PLEA TO I.R.A. -- Prime Minister Bertie Ahern of Ireland urged the I.R.A. to make a ''clear, unambiguous statement'' that it intends to disarm under the terms of the Northern Ireland peace accord. This, he said, could ease the entry of members of the I.R.A.'s political wing, Sinn Fein, into a new Protestant-Catholic cabinet by next Thursday's deadline for establishment of the new body. The I.R.A., which has observed a cease-fire for two years, has repeatedly said it has no plans to disarm.   James F. Clarity (NYT)    BRITAIN: PINOCHET'S COST TO TAXPAYERS -- The Law Lords, England's highest court, ruled that Gen. Augusto Pinochet would have to pay little of the costs stemming from the legal actions since his arrest in London last October on a Spanish request to extradite him to Madrid to face charges of crimes against humanity. The seven-judge panel did not speak of money amounts, but its breakdown of the 83-year-old former Chilean dictator's responsibility for legal fees meant that most of the estimated $10 million the case has cost so far would be borne by British taxpayers.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Protesters against Pres Slobodan Milosevic gather in main square of small Serbian southern town of Prokuplje, and Government fails to stage a planned rally of its own in response; Alliance for Change, collection of pro-democracy parties, draws 3,000 to 4,000 people to its rally; photo (M)
news.title: 3,000 Rally Against Milosevic, to Only a Feeble Response

news.abstract: United Nations defends a mine-clearing expert who is expelled by Iraq; expresses concern about Baghdad's continuing attempts to bar employees of certain nationalities or groups from working in Iraq (M)
news.title: U.N. Backs Mine Expert Expelled by Iraq

news.abstract: Shafik al-Wazzan, Prime Minister of Lebanon during tumultuous 1980's, dies at age 74; photo (M)
news.title: Shafik al-Wazzan, 74, Leader Of Lebanon in Tumultuous 80's

news.abstract: Government of Kazakhstan bars Russia from carrying out scheduled launching from Baikonur Cosmodrome; action comes three days after Russian rocket disintegrates over a grain-growing region (S)
news.title: Kazakhstan Blocks a Launching by Russia

news.abstract: Prime Min Ehud Barak promises that Israel with 'turn every stone' in quest for a broader Middle East peace, but cautions that it will be a few weeks before he will be ready to make his first moves; meets with Pres Hosni Mubarak of Egypt in Alexandria, who praises Barak as a friend and man of his word; photo (M)
news.title: Barak's Quest Starts With Boost by Egypt

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: MAD COW BAN ENDING -- Officials expect the European Union's ban on Britain's worldwide beef exports stemming from a 1996 outbreak of mad cow disease to be lifted next week. The ban was imposed after the disease swept through British cattle herds and was linked to Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, which attacks the human brain. More than four million animals have been destroyed in an effort to stamp out the disease, which has accounted for 40 deaths.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Clinton Administration is alarmed by the visit that Saudi Arabia's Defense Minister, Prince Sultan bin Abdelaziz al-Saud, made to Pakistani nuclear and missile facilities; officials say Saudis 'obfuscated' when asked about visit (M)
news.title: Saudi's Visit To Arms Site In Pakistan Worries U.S.

news.abstract: Romano Prodi, president of European Union's Executive Commission, announces appointment of 19 commissioners and promises new era of change after the forced resignation of the entire previous commission amid accusations of corruption; among the new commissioners is Chris Patten of Britain, who will direct European Union's relations with foreign countries (M)
news.title: European Union's Commission Is Revamped After a Scandal; a 'New Era' Is Promised

news.abstract: LONDON—  A key figure in the media campaign waged by NATO governments during the conflict in Kosovo criticized Western journalists on Friday for devoting as much coverage to alliance blunders and Serb civilian casualties as to the atrocities committed by Serb forces against ethnic Albanians.
news.title: Blair Spokesman Defends Alliance Briefings : A Key Adviser to NATO Assails Kosovo Coverage

news.abstract: Nearly 5,000 Gypsies of Kosovo have sought shelter in schoolhouse in Kosovo Polje, fleeing vengeance of returning Albanians who accuse them of collaborating with Serbs in last months of violence and ethnic purges; photo (M)
news.title: Kosovo Gypsies Now Among Vengeful Neighbors

news.abstract: United Nations is preparing to send large peacekeeping force to help stabilize Congo once cease-fire is signed, despite reservations by Clinton Administration (S)
news.title: U.N. Plans Force in Congo After Cease-Fire

news.abstract: Nearly decade and half of democracy has erased abuses of military rule from memory of most Brazilians, but two cases dating from unpleasant 21-year period have suddenly been thrust into national spotlight, creating embarrassment for Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso's Government (M)
news.title: Past Military Rule's Abuse Is Haunting Brazil Today

news.abstract: Pino Arlacchi, director of United Nations International Drug Control Program who has proposed eliminating opium poppy and coca leaf cultivation in 10 years, says his timetable for eradicating raw ingredients for heroin and cocaine around world is running ahead of schedule in some countries, but he acknowledges difficulties in others (M)
news.title: U.N. Says It Is Getting Farmers To Replace Their Drug Crops

news.abstract: Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee of India says military has chased out or killed most of Pakistani soldiers who have occupied strategic mountain tops on Indian side of Kashmir; Prime Min Nawaz Sharif of Pakistan continues efforts to convince men he insists are Islamic freedom fighters, not Pakistani soldiers, to withdraw voluntarily; Indian officials say that recently seized North Korean cargo ship was carrying makings of tactical surface-to-surface missiles destined for Pakistan (M)
news.title: India Says Its Has Evicted Most Pakistani Fighters in Kashmir

news.abstract: India and Pakistan say rival forces battling for past two months over Indian state of Kashmir, will begin phased withdrawal, heralding an end to latest confrontation between two countries; move toward peace comes week after Pakistan's Prime Min Nawaz Sharif visited with Pres Clinton in Washington and promised to take concrete steps to end crisis; both nations have fought two wars over Kashmir since winning independence from Britain in 1947; map; photo (M)
news.title: FOES REPORT PLAN TO BEGIN PULLOUT IN KASHMIR REGION

news.abstract: Analysis of political ramifications of failure of rebels in Congo to sign peace agreement aimed at ending civil war; photo; map (M)
news.title: Not Quite a Triumph in Congo

news.abstract: New Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak meets with Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat in Gaza in first Israeli-Palestinian summit in seven months; both say new era of peacemaking lies ahead, in which they will be partners; Barak, meeting with Arafat just five days after taking office, expresses determination to overcome all obstacles; allays anxiety of Palestinians by promising to move quickly to carry out terms of Wye River peace agreement; does not discuss major Palestinian concern over recent expansion of Jewish settlements in West Bank; reiterates that there will be no new settlements and no demolition of existing ones; meeting signals radical shift in tense, hostile relations that marked tenure of Benjamin Netanyahu, Barak's successor; photo (M)
news.title: At Border, Arafat and Barak Meet to Build Road to Peace

news.abstract: Republican Sen Chrles Grassley, who is blocking final Senate vote on Richard C Holbrooke's nomination to be chief American diplomat at UN, says Sec of State Madeleine K Albright is directly responsible for delay because of her treatment of State Dept employee Linda S Shenwick, who is described as whistle-blower (M)
news.title: Senator Blocking Holbrooke Calls Albright the Real Villain

news.abstract: Several thousand Kosovo Albanians march through Orahovac, Kosovo, on fourth day of peaceful protests against plans to station Russian troops among NATO peacekeepers; Albanians say Russian mercenaries fought as members of nationalist Serb militias that carried out campaign of killling, looting and burning across southwest corner of Kosovo and that Russians would be overly solicitous of handful of remaining Serbs; map (M)
news.title: For Fourth Day, Kosovo Albanians March to Protest a Plan for Russian Peacekeepers

news.abstract: Britain pushes legislation aimed at obtaining Protestant support for new Northern Ireland government, that would require Irish Republican Army to follow enforceable disarmament timetable, as deadline approaches to reach agreement on new government for Ulster; issue of when and how largely Catholic IRA will disarm has been main objection raised by Protestants to carrying out Northern Ireland peace settlement, agreed to 14 months ago and implemented haltingly since then (M)
news.title: British Putting More Pressure On the I.R.A. To Disarm

news.abstract: Federal prosecutors say fingerprints of two Egyptian associates of exiled Saudi terrorist Osama bin Laden were found on statements that took responsibility for bomb attacks against American embassies in Kenya and Tanzania in August 1998; both men, Ibrahim Hussein Eidarous and Abdel Mohammed Abdul Bari, were arrested in London on July 11 (M)
news.title: U.S. Says It Has Fingerprints Of Embassy Bombing Suspects

news.abstract: India announces suspension of six-week military campaign against Pakistan-based fighters who occupied Himalayan peaks in disputed state of Kashmir; pledges not to attack fighters as long as they complete withdrawal by July 16; Indian and Pakistan officials say military commanders have agreed to terms and timetable of pullout of fighters, who Pakistanis say are Islamic militants and India maintains are mostly Pakistani soldiers (M)
news.title: India Holds Fire in Kashmir As Enemy Forces Pull Out

news.abstract: Most widespread and sustained protests since Iran's Islamic revolution two decades ago spreads throughout country; security police and vigilante supporters move to crush pro-democracy student demonstrators outside Teheran University; demonstrations reported in 18 cities and towns, including major cosmopolitan cities of Tabriz, Shiraz and Isfahan, and more traditional cities like Meshed and Yazd; reflect deep struggle over course of Islamic revolution; students are impatient with slow pace of reforms promised by Pres Mohammad Khatami; are not calling for change in Islamic system of government, but for quickening of movement toward democracy and rule of law; diehard Islamic revolutionaries, some in positions of power, believe country's moves toward democracy are betrayal of revolutionary purism; demonstrations follow passage by Parliament of tough new press law and closure of Salam, popular left-leaning Islamic newspaper; map; photos (M)
news.title: Iran Protests Spread to 18 Cities; Police Crack Down at University

news.abstract: Taiwan abandons political formula that has long helped avert war with China, declaring it will no longer adhere to 'One China' principle that Chinese mainland and Taiwan are two parts of same country; Beijing voices outrage; accuses Pres Lee Teng-hui of taking extremely dangerous steps and warns of possible use of force; surprising and sudden shift risks badly souring Taiwan's relations with China and strains already troubled US-China relationship; represents step away from conceptual umbrella of inevitable reunification between China and Taiwan--which has been basic condition of all talks between them (M)
news.title: TAIWAN PRESIDENT IMPLIES HIS ISLAND IS SOVEREIGN STATE

news.abstract: News analysis of Taiwan Pres Lee Teng-hui's surprise statement that his Government no longer stands by premise that Taiwan and mainland are parts of same country; photo; even hint that Taiwan is moving toward formal declaration of independence rings loud alarm bells in Beijing, and shift inevitably complicates US-China relations, as well as election politics in Taiwan; Lee is expected to step down next spring after 12 years in office and apparently wants to cement his legacy as father of modern Taiwan separate from mainland (S)
news.title: 'What Is China?' Taiwan's New Answer Is Puzzling

news.abstract: Serbs living in Pancevo fear effects of toxic chemicals released from petrochemical and fertilizer factories that were bombed during NATO air campaign over Kosovo; photo; map; residents report blistering rashes from touching soil and stomach ailments from eating river fish and vegetables or drinking tap water; children, many of whom were sent to Slovakia by Red Cross to escape noxious gases, still suffer headaches and dizziness, and doctors report twice as many miscarriages as last year; authorities admit testing equipment is outdated; UN sets up investigation under Finnish environmental official Pakka Haavisto; he says biggest danger now is that ground water and Danube River are directly polluted; air strikes against industrial complex in April unleashed tons of chemicals as NATO tried to cut off Milosevic Government's resources; Pancevo has 130,000 residents, many of Hungarian and Croatian descent, and has been center of opposition to Slobodan Milosevic (M)
news.title: Serbian Town Bombed by NATO Fears Effects of Toxic Chemicals

news.abstract: Serb opposition leader Vuk Draskovic now says he will call supporters into streets to topple Pres Slobodan Milosevic (S)
news.title: Serb Opposition Leader Now Plans Protests

news.abstract: US asks Taiwan to explain its sudden declaration that it no longer stands by 'one China' policy; envoy Darryl Johnson will tell Pres Lee Teng-hui that his startling announcement is unhelpful (S)
news.title: U.S. Asking Taiwan to Explain Its Policy After Uproar

news.abstract: Swiss police authorities report sharp increase in number of reports of suspected money laundering under new law mandating stricter accountability by banks (S)
news.title: Swiss Step Up Their Scrutiny On Transfers Of Big Money

news.abstract: Argentine and British Governments agree to reinstate commercial flights between Argentina and Falkland Islands for first time since war over archipelago in 1982; agreement is hailed by Argentine officials as major diplomatic victory; Britain says agreement does not resolve dispute over which country has right to islands, which have been occupied by British citizens for more than century; Argentina says it opens way to improved ties between both two former enemies, which only restored diplomatic relations in 1990; Pres Carlos Saul Menem says final objective is to regain sovereignty over islands, which Argentina calls Malvinas (M)
news.title: Britain and Argentina to Allow Commercial Falkland Flights

news.abstract: Indian officials say withdrawal of Pakistani-backed forces from Indian-controlled area of Kashmir is on schedule to be finished by July 16 deadline; accuse Pakistan of sponsoring guerrilla attack on paramilitary camp near Srinigar on July 13; map (M)
news.title: Pakistan-Backed Force Leaves Indian Kashmir

news.abstract: White House and State Dept struggle to adjust schedules during upcoming visit of new Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak that fit not only into Pres Clinton's calendar but that of Hillary Rodham Clinton, who is playing unprecedented dual roles of First Lady and likely Senate candidate in New York; situation underscores growing challenge facing White House over next 15 months--of harmonizing not only political and policy messages of President, Vice Pres and First Lady, but also managing complex scheduling and logistics involved in Presidency and campaigns of Mrs Clinton and Al Gore (M)
news.title: On Barak Visit, Is It First Lady Hillary Clinton, or Candidate Hillary Clinton?

news.abstract: China says it has successfully developed design technology to make neutron bombs and miniaturized nuclear weapons on its own, first time it has made such assertions publicly; announcement seems timed as pointed reminder of its military capabilities, coming just days after Taiwan shifted stance toward China; rebuts Cox Committee report issued by Congressional committee in May, which accuses China of systematically stealing American nuclear technology--such as information on designs for neutron bomb and for W-88, most advanced miniaturized warhead; China says report is misleading, full of lies and racist (M)
news.title: China Proclaims It Designed Its Own Neutron Bomb

news.abstract: Mexico's social democrats, represented by Democratic Revolutionary Party, is on binge of self-destruction at time when it stands fighting chance of both winning Presidential election in 2000 and actually taking office; has been hamstrung by infighting among top party leaders, party's inability to organize clean election of its own and falling popularity of Mexico City Mayor Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, party's co-founder and its likely Presidential nominee; photo (M)
news.title: At a Hopeful Moment, Feud Tears at Mexico's Left

news.abstract: Comment on misunderstanding that arises over Pres Clinton's statement that he is 'eager as a kid with a new toy' to meet with Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak (S)
news.title: 'Kid With a New Toy' (and a Red Face)

news.abstract: Town of Islamshahr, Iran, scene of antigovernment riots in April of 1995, is subdued this time around, with people reluctant to discuss unrest in nation; in their own way, young men of Islamshahr are just as disaffected from conservative Islamic religious Government as students in Teheran; they share same desires for personal freedoms; their priorities are different, however; men of Islamshahr want jobs; map (M)
news.title: Town Hushed in '95 Crackdown Sees No Reason to Join Iran Riots

news.abstract: Clinton Administration, seeking to contain growing crisis in Asia, tries to play down timing and significance of China's declaration that it had developed on its own the ability to make neutron bombs and miniature atomic weapons; but Congressional Republicans say Beijing's assertion actually validates Congressional inquiry that accused China of stealing American nuclear secrets and was timed precisely to intimidate Taiwan (M)
news.title: U.S. Tries to Play Down China's Announcement on Bomb

news.abstract: BRUSSELS—  The death of a top prosecutor, apparently as the result of suicide, threw doubts Thursday over Belgium's two most prominent criminal investigations and forced Belgians to revisit some of the darker moments of their country's recent history.
news.title: Prosecutor in Pedophile Case Kills Himself : Belgian Official's Death Puts Top Cases On Hold

news.abstract: What is supposed to have been most important day in evolving Northern Ireland peace agreement becomes scene of chaos, farce and recrimination; new Northern Ireland Assembly is shut down indefinitely; British Govt announces that whole peace agreement is on hold; David Trimble, head of main Protestant party, and his 28 Ulster Unionist colleagues boycott Assembly session, which was scheduled to nominate cabinet ministers; Trimble says his party could not share power with Sinn Fein unless IRA begins to disarm; Deputy First Min Seamus Mallon of moderate Catholic Social Democratic and Labor Party reacts with fury, announcing he is resigning; photo (M)
news.title: One Agreement in Ulster: Assembly Session Is a Farce

news.abstract: Fear of military confrontation with China sweeps Taiwan's financial markets, causing steep stock price plunge; jitters spread across region, with stock markets dropping in Japan, Hong Kong and Singapore; domestic politics deepen instability, with James Soong announcing that he will break away from governing party and run for president as independent; some analysts fear prolonged instability could derail economy (M)
news.title: Fears of Military Confrontation With China Shake Taiwan Financial Markets

news.abstract: EUROPE    FRANCE: LIBYA PAYS FOR BOMBING PLANE -- Libya has transferred $31 million to France to compensate families of the 171 people killed when a French airliner was blown up over the African desert in 1989, officials said. A French court that convicted six high-ranking Libyan officials in absentia this year ordered Libya to pay compensation for the bombing, which occurred at a time of tension between the two countries over Chad. The French Foreign Ministry said the payment was acknowledgment by Libya that its officials were responsible for the deaths.   Craig R. Whitney (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Official Iranian view of United States is contradictory, with US presented both as evil mastermind behind every misfortune and as inept superpower unable to destroy Islamic Republic; third view, espoused by reformists newspapers that back Pres Mohammad Khatami, is that Iran can no longer play role of victim and must solve own problems; photo (M)
news.title: Iran's View of U.S.: Evil, Bumbling or Unimportant

news.abstract: Breakdown of Northern Ireland peace accord may be more loss of momentum than abandonment of purpose; has disclosed both political vacuum feared as opportunity for violence and reassuring new stability; paramilitary groups have maintained their cease-fires and economic development continues (M)
news.title: Irish Need Comply

news.abstract: Pres Clinton describes his Camp David meeting with Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak, phone interview; hails Barak's commitment to peace and his awareness of risks of peace process (M)
news.title: Clinton and Barak Drawn Together by the Politics of Peace

global_music.artist: Will Smith featuring Dru Hill & Kool Moe Dee
global_music.title: Wild Wild West

news.abstract: Tabare Vazquez, who is one of Uruguay's leading oncologists, and former mayor of capital, Montevideo, is waging busy campaign for President, leading leftist coalition of former Tupamaro guerrillas, Communists, Socialists and Trotskyites; political leaders of Uruguay's two traditional centrist parties, including Pres Julio Maria Sanguinetti, contend Vazquez is really a Marxist wolf in disguise who would destroy Uruguayan economy; polls indicate that Vazquez stands head-to-head with Jorge Batlle of center-left Colorado Party with three months remaining before first-round vote; former Pres Luis Alberto Lacalle of center-right Blanco Party is falling well behind; Vazquez photo; map (M)
news.title: With Kinder Face, the Left Is Blossoming in Uruguay

news.abstract: Vuk Draskovic, a leading opposition politician, appears for first time at rally calling for resignation of Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic, and formation of transitional government leading to new electoins; Draskovic urges festive crowd of about 20,000 people not to seek revenge or pursue a violent path that could lead to 'civil war' (M)
news.title: Key Opposition Leader Joins Rally Asking Milosevic to Resign

news.abstract: At least 10,000 people believed to be slaughtered by Serbian forces during three-month campaign to drive Albanians from Kosovo; war crimes investigators, NATO peacekeeping troops and aid agencies struggle to keep up with fresh reports each day of newly discovered bodies and graves; State Dept had estimated death toll to be 4,600 people in May, before international war crimes tribunal in The Hague indicted Pres Slobodan Milosevic and four top aides on charges of crimes against humanity; war crimes investigators say true toll may never be known, because some villagers have buried their dead without informing Western officials, and because many deaths went unrecorded in chaotic press of events when peacekeepers and United Nations relief workers first arrived; some bodies may have been burned or carried off by Serbs in effort to destroy evidence; photos; map (M)
news.title: INQUIRY ESTIMATES SERB DRIVE KILLED 10,000 IN KOSOVO

news.abstract: Talks between striking students and authorities from Mexico's largest university aimed at settling 88-day-old shutdown have collapsed, making possibility of police action to open campus more real (S)
news.title: Talks Fail to End Mexico University Strike

news.abstract: News analysis of first round of meetings in Washington between Pres Clinton and new Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak; officials familiar with their conversations note that how to reach an agreement with Syria, one of last Arab countries still at war with Israel, dominated their discussions; Clinton Adm officials believe that a deal with Syrian Pres Hafez al-Assad is doable but that it will require involvement of highest-level American officials (M)
news.title: Israeli's Talk With Clinton: Syria Accord Back in View

global_music.artist: Will Smith featuring Dru Hill & Kool Moe Dee
global_music.title: Wild Wild West

news.abstract: Vuk Draskovic, leading Serbian opposition politician, says best way to get Pres Slobodan Milosevic out of power is to seduce him to resign by promising immunity from arrest or extradition for war crimes; says he will soon name shadow Yugoslav government of experts led by prime minister selected by Milo Djukanovic, democratic leader of Montenegro; will press Milosevic through public rallies to accept government and to call new elections in three to six months while opposition works to attract disaffected Milosevic supporters; others in opposition feel time is right to confront and oust Milosevic, not to encourage him; senior opposition figures remain intensely competitive, and their lack of unity makes it more likely that if Milosevic falls it will be through chaotic outpouring of discontent; map; photo (M)
news.title: Foe Suggests Giving Milosevic Immunity To Get Him to Quit

news.abstract: Grisly details of more than 100 instances of torture and killings by Eugene de Kock, South Africa's most notorious apartheid-era henchman, are contained in amnesty application pending before Truth and Reconciliation Commission; many South Africans believe de Kock has still not told entire truth and may be holding back details in effort to make himself look more like soldier than monster, even though confession runs for more than 4,000 pages and is by far largest ever received by commission; de Kock, who headed counterterrorism unit from 1985 to 1993, is serving two life terms plus 212 years for range of charges; has written book on his life, lashing out at generals who he says abandoned him after he finished their dirty work (M)
news.title: South Africa Confronts Brutalities Of One Man

news.abstract: Israel confirms plans to add at least 50 more F-16's to already formidable jet fighter fleet; deal signals determination to maintain decisive regional air power superiority even as Israel pursues peace deals with its Middle Eastern neighbors; Prime Min Ehud Barak tells American officials that Israel wishes to but 50 new planes, a $2.5 billion order, with option to purchase 60 more for additional $2 billion; Israel already has 250 F-16's--largest fleet outside US (M)
news.title: Israel Will Buy 50 F-16's In Its Biggest Arms Deal Ever

news.abstract: Fighting continues in Congo a week after signing of cease-fire; rebels report capturing more territory, and countries embroiled in year-old conflict trade accusations over violations; map (M)
news.title: War in Congo Rattles On Despite Accord

news.abstract: Frances Mayes and her husband, Ed, gain cult following as result of Under the Tuscan Sun and Bella Tuscany, her two best-selling books describing their restoration of an 18th-century villa in Cortona, Italy; 30 to 40 travelers from US and other countries stop at gates the villa each day during high travel season to look and to seek autographs; American fixation with crumbling villas and recipes for toasted bread delights and bewilders people of Cortona; photo; map (M)
news.title: Cortona Journal; Act 2: Quest for Tuscan Pasta and Great Plastering

global_music.artist: Will Smith featuring Dru Hill & Kool Moe Dee
global_music.title: Wild Wild West

news.abstract: A Canadian auditor presented a report today about the Mexican Government's rescue of its banks concluding that about $7.7 billion of the loans absorbed by the bailout were highly irregular or plainly illegal.     Michael Mackey, the accountant hired by the Mexican Congress to  review the bailout, found that bank executives made billion-dollar loans to themselves that they never repaid; that banks lent millions of dollars to investors to buy shares in the same banks, and that top bankers made large loans to friends and family without as much as a credit study.
news.title: Bailout Audit in Mexico Cites $7.7 Billion in Dubious Loans

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: CUTTING BACK ON ROYALTY -- Britain plans to cut security for some members of the royal family as a way of reducing costs. Queen Elizabeth has asked the Government to review ways of lowering the $47 million annual bill for protection. Steps being considered include the removal of motorcycle outriders that escort royal limousines around London and the replacement of policemen patrolling homes with civilian guards.   Warren Hoge (NYT)    RUSSIA: BATTLES WITH CHECHENS -- Chechen fighters attacked Russian police posts and patrols, killing two commanding officers, wounding seven other policemen and provoking strikes by Russian artillery and helicopter gunships, Russian news outlets reported. The fighting along Chechnya's borders followed a weekend of skirmishes in which Chechen rebels killed four policemen and four civilians.   (AP)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Corruption has long been something of a national pastime in South Korea. With few laws and little Government effort to prosecute offenders, many Koreans have come to regard bribes, payoffs and kickbacks as part of political life.    But that was all supposed to change with the election of Kim Dae Jung as President in December 1997. Mr. Kim, a former political dissident, campaigned on a platform of stamping out corruption and reforming South Korea's faltering economy.
news.title: Graft Cases Remind South Koreans of Bad Old Days

news.abstract: Indonesia is preparing to relinquish control of East Timor after 23 years of occupation, and it believes that independence advocates are highly likely to win a referendum next month, says a supposedly authentic internal Government report that has been made available to reporters by advocates of independence.    The report predicted violence if independence forces won and anticipated that non-Timorese who control many businesses would leave.
news.title: Jakarta Reportedly Predicts East Timor Will Vote to Split Off

news.abstract: The wild mutton-chop sideburns are gone. The televised cheek-to-cheek tangos with marquee entertainers  are a thing of the past. And when President Carlos Saul Menem does take the occasional spin in a hot sports car these days, his bodyguards no longer need to make death-defying weaves through traffic to chase after him.    At age 69 and in his final five months in office, Mr. Menem still makes good copy -- but now the press attention is focused on the presidential psyche. Argentine magazines, quoting anonymous sources, report that Mr. Menem is depressed, lonely and bitter because many of his closest allies, including his hand-picked Vice President, have abandoned him.
news.title: Soon to Bow Out, Argentine Brushes Off the Boos

global_music.title: Wild Wild West

news.abstract: European Court of Human Rights, Strasbourg, France, which serves 41-nation Council of Europe, is raising its visibility with high-profile cases; Luzius Wildhaber, court president, comments (M)
news.title: Europe's Rights Court Taking On Increasingly Sensitive Cases

news.abstract: PARIS—  The Phantom Menace has struck high fashion with designers at this week's couture shows divided between attention-grabbing futurism and clothes for the terrestrial world.
news.title: But Couture Outfits Grab Public's Attention : Wild, and Unwearable

news.abstract: Yugoslav Government plans to authorize back pay for reservists, pensioners and teachers in bid to assuage popular grievances and stop wave of protests by army reservists unpaid for months spent in Kosovo; new payments are likely to spur inflation in damaged economy; map; photo (M)
news.title: Belgrade Officials Plan Back Pay for Protesting Reservists

news.abstract: Hugh Fish, British environmentalist whose love of pristine rivers helped clean up Thames, dies at age 76 (S)
news.title: Hugh Fish, 76, Who Made Thames So Clean the Salmon Came Back

news.abstract: Hong Kong-based human rights group charges that China has detained at least 70 Buddhist Law spiritual movement leaders in 14 cities; says police searched leaders' homes, confiscating books about rapidly growing movement and addresses of people who attended meetings; group, known in Chinese as Falun Gong, could be potent force in nation facing dislocating social and economic changes; was able to mobilize thousands of followers without warning for April protest; several hundred members stage protests in Dalian and two smaller cities; map (M)
news.title: Beijing Detains Leaders of Sect, Watchdog Says

global_music.artist: Will Smith featuring Dru Hill & Kool Moe Dee
