news.abstract: Many Russians are using particularly Russian talent of adapting to seemingly any hardship to cling to vestiges of life before current economic crisis; some enterprises have even prospered, with weakened ruble protecting them from competition from foreign-produced goods, but crisis has made cynical public even more distrustful of Govt and its seemingly endless promises of economic reform; strange mixture of self-reliance, humor and weary resignation have kept nation famous for revolutions from falling apart; photo (M)
news.title: Hardened by Their History of Hardships, Russians Simply Stretch the Rubles Further

news.abstract: Destruction caused by earthquake in Yalova, Turkey, as well as search for possible survivors and retrieval of dead, described; many residents express frustration with recovery effort (S)
news.title: Hands Dig. A Shout, and Then Despair.

news.abstract: British farmers who have offered some of their land to the Government for the test-planting of genetically modified seed crops have become the target of bitter protests.
news.title: Genetic Crop Testing Angers Many Britons

news.abstract: Residents of densely populated Istanbul, Turkey, doubt Govt will plan ahead for next earthquake, which geologists predict will likely be even more deadly, despite overwhelming earthquake on August 17 that killed tens of thousands in area east of city; few believe catastrophe will compel officials to replan city, knock down shoddily constructed buildings and force builders to abide by strict anti-earthquake requirements; geologists predict next earthquake is likely to erupt further west along Anatolian fault, most probably in Istanbul or Sea of Marmara south of Bosporus; map (M)
news.title: Looking Ahead, People of Istanbul Worry That in Next Quake, They're on Their Own

news.abstract: Career profiles of Natasha Gurfinkel Kagalovsky and Ludmilla (Lucy) Edwards, Bank of New York executives suspended as central figures in money-laundering scheme involving Russian organized crime; scheme, in which billions of dollars may have been channeled through accounts at bank by Russian organized crime and by embezzlement from Russian companies, may be one of biggest money laundering schemes in history (M)
news.title: Career Singed in Global Bank Fires

news.abstract: Approximately 200 relatives of people killed in bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over, Lockerbie, Scotland, nearly 11 years ago are assured by Scottish officials that two Libyan suspects will be prosecuted vigorously and without regard to political considerations; assurances by Lord Hardie, Scotland's senior law officer, comes at meeting arranged by US Justice Dept to brief relatives on case; trial of suspects Abdel Basset Ali al-Megrahi and Lamen Khalifa Fhimah will begin in February 2000 and will take place in Netherlands under Scottish law (M)
news.title: Prosecutor Tells Lockerbie Relatives He'll Keep Trial Nonpolitical

news.abstract: Public health experts say thousands of unburied bodies in Turkey's earthquake zone may be traumatic for survivors but do not pose any danger of an epidemic of infectious diseases; say there is no evidence of increased disease since earthquake struck; say natural disasters do not import diseases that are not already present in affected area (S)
news.title: Bodies Pose No Danger Of Disease, Doctors Say

news.abstract: Aviation experts ask hard questions about China Airlines, Taiwan's flagship carrier following crash-landing at Hong Kong International Airport on August 22 that killed two people and injured 212; question why plane, with 315 passengers and crew, tried to land in howling typhoon and why carrier has had four major accidents in six years--worst safety record in Asia; photo (M)
news.title: Hong Kong Crash Raises Question About Pilots

news.abstract: Clinton Adm presses China for immediate release of American reported suffering serious spinal injuries during jump or fall from window of building in confrontation with Chinese police; China says 29-year-old Daja Meston, Tibetan linguist from Newton, Mass, was injured while trying to escape police in remote area of Qinghai province where Govt is carrying out population resettlement program opposed by human rights groups and environmentalists (S)
news.title: China Urged to Free American Hurt Fleeing Police

news.abstract: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder takes up residence in Berlin after moving office from Bonn, inaugurating first Berlin-based Govt to rule country since Hitler's collapsed at end of World War II; ceremonies are kept low-key out of fear that historical symbolism remains too charged for broad public celebration; Schroeder says arrival of Govt represents 'historic moment'--completion of decade-long transition during which Germany has undergone peaceful and successful revolution; photo (M)
news.title: Schroder Moves, and So Does Germany's Center of Gravity

news.abstract: Pentagon says Iraq's own antiaircraft artillery, not US fighter jets, killed two people in clash in northern Iraq; says reconnaissance photos show Iraq put missile launchers in residential areas of Mosul; unusually detailed accounts aim to undercut sympathy for Iraq abroad (S)
news.title: U.S. Says Iraqis Were Killed By Their Own Artillery Fire

news.abstract: Nigerian writer Chinua Achebe, 69, returns to his country, which he left in 1990 for medical treatment of injuries from car accident; arrival is seen as positive development, three months into new civilian Government (S)
news.title: Nigerian Writer Returns After a 9-Year Absence

news.abstract: Negotiations between peacekeeping commanders and local Kosovo Albanians fail to end blockade around town of Orahovac that is preventing Russian peacekeepers from moving into area; photo (S)
news.title: Kosovo Albanians Barring Russians From City Stand Firm

news.abstract: BANGKOK—  After decades of debate, delay and broken promises, Bangkok will soon offer commuters an alternative to its traffic-clogged streets. Beginning in November, Sky Train — a privately funded mass-transit railway — begins whisking travelers along 23.5 kilometers (14.5 miles) of track high above the congestion and its syrupy brown pollution.
news.title: Private Funding Propels Bangkok's New Sky Train

news.abstract: A passenger cruise liner and a cargo ship collided in the English Channel early Tuesday, slightly injuring several people on the liner, touching off a fire on the cargo ship and raising fundamental questions about shipping and safety in one of the world's busiest areas of the sea.
news.title: Cruise Liner and Cargo Vessel Collide in Channel

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  Indonesian investigators have concluded that "unlawful interference" may have caused the mysterious crash of a Singapore jet in December 1997 that killed all 104 people on board, the Singapore government said Wednesday.
news.title: 'Unlawful Interference' Cited in 1997 Accident : Report on SilkAir Crash Alludes to Pilot Suicide

news.abstract: Women are fighting side by side with men in Eritrea in 15-month war against Ethiopia; many follow lead of their mothers, who fought in 30-year war for independence from Ethiopia, won in 1991; women soldiers see their service helping to improve role of women in still-traditional Eritrea; photos (M)
news.title: Like Mother, Like Daughter, Eritrean Women Wage War

news.abstract: Spanish officials say French-speaking man hijacked Royal Air Maroc airliner with 88 people aboard after it left Casablanca, Morocco, but surrendered in Barcelona, where he diverted plane; say no one was injured (M)
news.title: Hijacking of Moroccan Jet Ends in Spain With Passengers Unhurt

news.abstract: Defense Department and Clinton Administration officials say Pres Clinton plans to withdraw last American troops from Haiti, under pressure from Pentagon and Congressional Republicans, by end of year even though peace there remains tenuous; say Pentagon, in future, will send small contingents of reservists and National Guard members on short temporary assignments; only 480 regular troops remain in Haiti, down from force of 20,000 that occupied nation in 1994, but are seen as psychologically important; smaller United Nations force of about 400 peacekeepers acting as advisers to police will not be affected (M)
news.title: Full-Time U.S. Force in Haiti To Leave an Unstable Nation

news.abstract: Rep Tony P Hall, passing through Japan on way to unofficial visit to North Korea, scores Japan for cutting off food aid to famine-stricken North Korea for political reasons while it has millions of tons of surplus rice; Japan says it will not resume aid, halted last Aug after North Korea fired missile over Japan (M)
news.title: U.S. Lawmaker Faults Japan for Halting Food to North Korea

news.abstract: ESTADO, East Timor—  Beneath the shade of the forest, the steep hillsides are quilted with the dark green leaves of the coffee trees. Mist curls through the canopies, and a fine rain soaks the undergrowth.
news.title: East Timorese Vote /Militias Interfere With a Cash Crop : Coffee Industry Embroiled in a Tug of War

news.abstract: BANGKOK—  Sales of the first biography written by a foreigner about King Bhumibol Adulyadej of Thailand with extensive cooperation of the monarch himself are being "strongly discouraged" by Thai authorities who say the book will likely soon be banned.
news.title: Bangkok May Ban King's Biography

news.abstract: Belated and confusing confirmation by NATO forces in Kosovo that at least 15 bodies were found in mass grave site last month, prompts Yugoslav Government to blame NATO for what it calls mass killing of Serbs and to demand that Security Council review situation in Kosovo; map (M)
news.title: Belgrade Sees Grave Site as Proof NATO Fails to Protect Serbs

news.abstract: Pavel P Borodin, top Kremlin official, denies corruption charges made in Italian newspaper against members of Pres Boris N Yeltsin's family and inner circle; newspaper, Corriere della Sera, says that $1 million in 'pocket money' for Yeltsin entourage had been funneled in 1994 through Swiss bank account; allegations follow months of public inquiry into Borodin's relationship with Mabetex, Swiss construction company that has had several large contracts to work on Government buildings in Moscow; photo (M)
news.title: Yeltsin Aide Denies Report Of Secret Cash In Swiss Bank

news.abstract: Turkey's secular Government is determined to bar Muslim groups from joining earthquake relief effort; senior military and civilian leaders fear that if such groups win public confidence with their relief work, they will also win new converts to cause of political Islam; photos (M)
news.title: Turkey Blocking Muslim Aid to Quake Victims

news.abstract: Washington Memo column on Sec Madeline Albright and new UN Amb Richard C Holbrooke, who have promised each other to be on best behavior and not to make their famous rivalry the stuff of American foreignpolicy for next 18 months (S)
news.title: Washington Memo; Appointment Heats Up A Diplomatic Rivalry

news.abstract: Pres Clinton warns Indonesian Pres B J Habibie that relations with US will be seriously harmed if there is mass violence during referendum on self-rule in East Timor; photo of relatives mourning victim of violence there (S)
news.title: U.S. Warns Indonesia Over Political Violence

news.abstract: Money-laundering scandal involving Bank of New York has made Moscow celebrity out of high-flying Russian businessman Konstantin Kagalovsky; he gives newspaper interview in which he speaks tenderly of his wife, Natasha, bank executive suspended in case, and discusses how allegations have complicated their life; photo (S)
news.title: Russians See Politics in Bank Scandal

news.abstract: Ugandans breathe sigh of relief now that their bachelor king, Ronald Muwenda Mutebi, has finally, at age 43, taken a bride, although his choice, Sylvia Nagginda Luswata, raises some eyebrows; bride is 35, has lived mostly in US and belongs to Edible Rat clan, which traditionally cleans washrooms; photo; map (Kampala Journal) (S)
news.title: Kampala Journal; A Sigh of Relief for a Royal Walk Down the Aisle

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    ISRAEL: SABBATH CRISIS AVERTED -- A political crisis was defused over the transport of a huge electrical turbine on the Jewish Sabbath. Ultra-Orthodox parties, which had threatened to quit Prime Minister Ehud Barak's coalition, were temporarily assuaged by a compromise agreement: The electrical company's turbine, which was to be transported on the Sabbath because it will move only at three miles per hour, was loaded before sundown, will be unloaded after sundown and will be driven by a non-Jewish truck driver.     Deborah Sontag (NYT)    EUROPE    SPAIN: BASQUE REBELS HALT TALKS -- The Basque separatist group E.T.A. suspended peace talks with the Government, accusing it of seeking political gain from the only negotiations last May. But the rebels stopped short of halting their unilateral cease-fire observed since Sept. 16. Their latest statement to the Basque news media, on Thursday, came a day after Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar blamed the rebels for stalling and charged that they are ''afraid of peace.''   Al Goodman (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Republican Presidential front-runner, Gov George W Bush, whose father was accused by candidate Bill Clinton of 'coddling' dictators in Beijing, is struggling to decide how hard a line to take toward China; issue of China is sticky one for Republican candidate, who is caught between hawkish conservatives on one side of his party and pro-business interests on the other; shadow of his father, who during his presidency claimed China as a special area of expertise, compounds problem (M)
news.title: Bush Carries Some Baggage In Developing China Stance

news.abstract: East Timor, after 24 years of bloodshed and fear, reaches its moment of truth, referendum on Aug 30 that could lead it into new era of freedom and reconciliation or one of even fiercer civil war; referendum offers choice between independence or an autonomous relationship with Indonesia, which invaded former Portuguese colony in 1975 and has fought against separatist rebels ever since; but as vote has drawn near, what should been an election campaign in tiny, remote territory has been instead a campaign of terror by brutal, ragtag militias that oppose independence; militias, backed and organized by Indonesian military, have largely ignored appeals for calm from United Nations, which deployed in East Timor in May to organize referendum; Sec Gen Kofi Annan says he is 'appalled' by continuing attacks and demands that Indonesian security forcess fulfill their obligation to maintain order; map (L)
news.title: Fearful of Militias, East Timor to Vote on Its Future

news.abstract: Peruvian Indians and peasants who for years have resisted Shining Path because of Maoist rebels' violent tactics and bizarre ideas are gaining new sense of confidence; Ayacucho Province, land of soaring Andean peaks, aromatic eucalyptus forests, ancient Indian ruins and desperate poverty that was long ignored by Government, was cradle and epicenter of Shining Path uprising; but social and political changes the rebels tried to impose backfired; as villagers organized to drive them out, a different kind of revolution took place; women, who took lead in protecting their sons from being drafted by rebels, are becoming more assertive; villagers are emboldened to demand services from central Government, and in the process village governments are becoming more democratic; once isolated Indian villages are developing local banks and building roads and bridges to become more fully integrated into national economy; photos; map (L)
news.title: A Revolution Peru's Rebels Didn't Intend

news.abstract: Iran slowly discovers it has drug problem:
news.title: Iran Confronts a Long-Hidden Problem: Drugs

news.abstract: Growing number of people in Vancouver, British Columbia, are growing concerned that Canada's liberal immigration policies are being abused; two ships that left 254 illegal Chinese immigrants on Vancouver beaches this summer causes furor, and exposes latent fear among Canadians taht, because of their famous generosity and courteousness, they are bcoming nation of doormats; ethnic Chinese people account for 20 percent of greater Vancouver's population, and Asians account for half of this fall's freshman class at University of British Columbia; Reform Party this fall plans to introduce legislation to tighten Canada's immigration laws; photo; map (M)
news.title: Vancouver Is Astir Over Chinese Abuse of Immigration Law

news.abstract: France's Green Party, emboldened by good showing in recent elections for European Parliament, threatens to pull out of Govt if Prime Min Lionel Jospin approves new generation of nuclear power stations to replace old ones; Greens, who joined Jospin's Govt in 1997, have always insisted that nuclear energy is at center of their policy concerns; even though party leader Dominique Voynet serves as Environment Minister, party says it is being ignored on vital questions inside governing coalition; country's 57 nuclear reactors provide 78 percent of country's energy (M)
news.title: Greens Say They'll Quit French Government if It Plans New A-Plants

news.abstract: Four Roman Catholic teenagers from Northern Ireland are forced into hiding to escape death threats by Irish Republican Army; development provokes new calls from Protestant officials for expulsion of Sinn Fein from peace talks due to resume in week; Protestant politicians say threats are result of leniency of Britain's Northern Ireland Sec, Mo Mowlam, who earlier ruled that organization's killings and gun-running did not constitute abandonment of two-year-old cease-fire; four identified as Martin and Gerard Groogan and Barry and Paul McDonald (M)
news.title: Four Youths Threatened By the I.R.A. Flee Ulster

news.abstract: Political pressures on Brazilian Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso continue mounting as strikes and protests spread and support for Govt slips in polls and Congress; protestors from myriad groups, emboldened by Govt's giving in to demands of striking truckers who blocked roads after Government threatened to use armed force to clear them, descend on capital to demand relief; surge in protests and Govt's uncertain response to them have contributed to renewed weaknesses of Brazilian currency, and Cardoso's popularity has suffered similar decline (M)
news.title: As Brazil's Chief Wavers, He's Deluged With Labor Protests

news.abstract: People of East Timor vote on independence; results, which will not be known for week, will determine whether territory of 800,000 people will enter new autonomous relationship within Indonesia or will become newest sovereign state; voting is mostly peaceful, despite sporadic attacks in pro-independence areas by irregular militias recruited and armed by military; UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan urges Indonesian Govt to honor results; pledges UN will aid any transition period toward any new East Timorese administration, whether independent state or autonomous Indonesian region; maps; photo (M)
news.title: With More Broken Promises of Peace, East Timor Votes

news.abstract: Helder Pessoa Camara, Brazil's Archbishop, dies at age 90; photo (M)
news.title: No Headline

news.abstract: Dispute over plans by Mexican Govt to open road into San Cristobal de las Casas in Chiapas state, main stronghold of Zapatista rebels, ignites clash between both sides possibly dashing efforts by Pres Ernesto Zedillo over past five years to bring peace to Indian region; has led to first direct skirmishes between two sides in more than year; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Road Dispute Revives Zapatista Fight

news.abstract: Samantha Smith, Panama's intelligence chief who was dismissed after American allegations that she was selling visas to Chinese seeking to enter US illegally, implicates Pres Ernesto Perez Balladares, who she says authorized their sale; says she specifically approved visas requested by Balladares; says she warned President on several occasions of serious doubts about visas, which were clearly being used by poor rural Chinese to get to Panama en route to US; Balladares denies allegations; charges Smith with making politically motivated accusations that could be seized upon by American critics of handover of Panama Canal, set for December 31 (M)
news.title: Ex-Official Accuses Panama's Leader in Visa-Selling Scheme

news.abstract: LONDON—  Two years after her death, the only monument to Diana, Princess of Wales, is the one the people have adopted, the Flame of Liberty above the Paris tunnel where she died in an automobile accident on Aug. 31, 1997.
news.title: Focus Is Shifting to Her Elder Son, the Heir to the Dynastic Flame : 2 Years On, Britons Give Diana a Shrug

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    JORDAN: HAMAS OFFICES CLOSED -- Security forces closed the Amman offices of the militant Islamic group Hamas, Government officials said, adding that they had not been registered to be used for political activities. Israel has repeatedly asked Jordan to close down the offices of Hamas, which has been held responsible for killing scores of Israelis in suicide bombings. An official said arrest warrants had also been issued but refused to say if Hamas officials were among those being sought.   (Reuters)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Georgi Chuglazov, Russian investigator, says he has proof to back up published accounts of bribes to Kremlin officials by Swiss construction company Mabetek; company is at center of inquiry into kickbacks allegedly received by top Govt officials (S)
news.title: Russian Says He Has Proof Bribes Were Paid to Kremlin

news.abstract: Divided rebels in Congo sign cease-fire accord signed by Rwanda, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Angola, Namibia and Congo month ago, Lusaka, Zambia; continue to squabble about how to carry out accord (M)
news.title: Congo Rebels Finally Sign an Accord but Real Peace Is Still Distant

news.abstract: Strong tremor and aftershock hit already earthquake-devastated towns in northwestern Turkey, bringing down several buildings and causing at least one death; 166 people are admitted to hospitals and clinics in Izmit after being hit by debris; tremor is felt in some parts of Istanbul, where main effect is psychological; prosecutors in Duzce seek arrest of 33 contractors, engineers and building owners in connection with fatal building collapses; maps; photo (M)
news.title: New Tremor Shakes Quake-Devastated Area of Turkey

news.abstract: Ukrainian ex-Prime Min Pavlo Lazarenko, detained by United States for possible extradition to Ukraine or Switzerland on charges of embezzling state funds and money laundering, bought lavish $6.75 million Marin County, Calif, estate for cash last Sept; US authorities say he made money buying and selling natural gas contracts when he was energy minister; his attorney holds charges are politically motivated; photos (M)
news.title: A Palace Fit for a Fugitive And Ukraine's Ex-Premier

news.abstract: LAPA flight carrying some 106 people crashes on takeoff from Buenos Aires, Argentina, and catches fire; as many as 80 people are killed and at least 23 hurt, including people on ground; map (M)
news.title: Argentine Jet Crashes on Takeoff; as Many as 80 Feared Dead

news.abstract: Anti-independence thugs who have terrorized East Timor for months reassert selves after extraordinarily peaceful referendum on region's future in which 98.6 percent of voters reportedly cast ballots; thugs, mobilized by Indonesian military into irregular militias, set up roadblocks in Dili and on rural roads; Eurico Guterres, militia leader, says his men will bar what he calls East Timorese elite from leaving; some promoters of independence go into hiding after reportedly getting death threats; photo (M)
news.title: Militias Raise Tensions After Timor Votes

news.abstract: Germany marks 60th anniversary of its invasion of Poland and start of World War II by declaring Poland should have place in European Union as soon as possible; Pres Johannes Rau visits Gdansk; most major German newspapers ignore anniversary; Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder's position, acknowledgment and awareness of past allied to determination to look beyond it, reflects that of large majority of Germans (M)
news.title: Remembering Their War, Germans Embrace the First Victims

news.abstract: Clinton Administration officials say United States wants assurances that international financial aid to Russia has not been lost to corruption or moved surreptitiously out of nation; stop short of calling for halt in future International Monetary Fund loans; respond to reported money laundering through Bank of New York (M)
news.title: U.S. Seeks Details on Russia's Use of Aid

news.abstract: Talks between Israelis and Palestinians stalled again early today and it seemed unlikely that new agreements would be reached before Secretary of State Madeleine Albright arrives later today.     State Department officials have said Ms. Albright would be reluctant to mediate the fine print, a key aspect of which involves the release of Arab prisoners by Israel.
news.title: Brinkmanship, Still, In the Mideast Talks

news.abstract: United States officials say privately that while Panamanian officials probably are selling Panamanian visas to Chinese immigrants using Panama as back door to sneak into United States, Justice Department cannot open probe without indications that Panamanians also help Chinese to enter US; say consular officials acted properly in revoking visa of Samantha Smith, former head of Panamanian intelligence, who says she approved suspect visas at request of then-Pres Ernesto Perez Balladares; she claimed he sold visas to supplement budget; revocation drew anger of Justice officials, who say move tipped off smuggling ring; officials say Amb Simon Ferro kept all necessary agencies informed about actions; Sen Jesse Helms asks State and Justice Departments about supposed probe (M)
news.title: Justice Dept. Inquiry Into Sales Of Visas in Panama Is Denied

news.abstract: Kursumlija, Serbia, is struggling to absorb 7,000 displaced Serbs from Kosovo as Serbia deals with some 173,000 Kosovo refugees; most Kosovo Serbs get 60 percent of their regular salaries from state suffering severe cash shortage; many are crowded in with host families that cannot afford added burden; Serbia is no longer pressing them to return to Kosovo, but encourages them to live near province and discourages them from trying to settle in Belgrade, where they would be more visible; photo (M)
news.title: Serbs Driven From Kosovo Live Crowded and in Want

news.abstract: Israelis and Palestinians fail to deliver agreement for signing ceremony in Egypt that Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright had hoped to preside over; Albright meets with Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat in Egypt, then arrives in Israel to meet with Prime Min Ehud Barak, but talks break up without a deal; at issue is Israel's refusal to release 50 Palestinian prisoners now held in Israel; negotiating atmosphere between Israelis and Palestinians was supposed to have substantially improved with new Israeli leader, Barak; it is not clear whether dispute over prisoners constitutes real crisis or matter of brinkmanship, with each side seeking to show its constituency that it is reaching for best possible bargain on emotional issue; photo (M)
news.title: MIDEAST STANDOFF REMAINS UNSOLVED AS ALBRIGHT VISITS

news.abstract: NATO and United Nations officials agree to allow part of Kosovo Liberation Army to survive as lightly armed civilian emergency force; under Kosovo peace accord, rebel army is being dismantled this month under UN supervision; its successor, called Kosovo Corps, is to be civilian force, set up for coping with emergencies like earthquakes and fires; officials say its 3,000 members will have military structure formed from core commanders and brigades of present KLA; sorting out duties of new force remains extremely delicate, because of implications for Kosovo Albanians' aspiration for independence and for Yugoslavia's sovereignty over province; while NATO sees Kosovo Corps as civilian force, along lines of National Guard in US, rebel officers see it as potential core of national army, and are selling it to their followers as such (M)
news.title: NATO and U.N. in Kosovo Agree On K.L.A. Role in Civilian Force

news.abstract: Thousands of people who have lived in prosperous parts of Turkey are likely to return to poorer regions in wake of earthquake that devastated country's booming industrial region; reverse migration could have profound social and political effects; many of those returning to undeveloped areas will bring urban attitudes with them, along with new-found cynicism about their political system stemming from Government's failures in earthquake relief effort; if enough of these people fan out through rural Turkey, they may emerge as new force for social and political change; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Turkey's Bereft Carry Cynicism Back to Villages

news.abstract: Bank of New York says it has dismissed second employee involved in its investigation into possible money laundering at bank; employee, Svetlana Kudryavtsev, reportedly failed to cooperate with bank's internal probe of matter; bank earlier discharged Lucy Edwards for failing to cooperate with investigators and not revealing to bank that she was married to Peter Berlin, whose accounts at bank were allegedly used to channel billions of dollars from Russia; investigators are also looking at another bank officer, Natasha Gurfinkel Kagalovsky, who worked closely with Edwards and is married to prominent Russian businessman (M)
news.title: Bank of New York Dismisses Second Employee in Laundering Case

news.abstract: Ariel Sharon captures leadership of opposition Likud Party in Israel, succeding Benjamin Netanyahu, who quit after losing bid to be re-elected Prime Minister in May; Sharon, 71, is veteran of many Israeli military and political battles; says he will serve only as steward of party, with goal of holding new primaries in two years to select next Likud candidate for Prime Minister; photo (M)
news.title: Ariel Sharon, Resilient Hawk, Captures Likud Leadership

news.abstract: State election in Saarland represents identity crisis for Germany's Social Democrat as Chancellor Gerhard Schroder's tries to reduce party's role as champion of workers' rights and make it promote a new entrepreneurial spirit; Schroder warily supports re-election of Saarland Governor, Reinhard Klimmt, who is a more traditional Social Democratic and faces fierce challenge from Christian Deemocatic candidate, Peter Muller, who has declared that Saarland coal industry, which employs 11,000 people, must be closed; photo; map (M)
news.title: State Election a Test for Germany's Governing Left

news.abstract: Swiss prosecutors investigating suspected money laundering by officials at high levels of Russian Government order Swiss banks to provide information on two dozen Russians who may have accounts in Switzerland; freeze at least 59 bank accounts; Russians under investigation include Pavel P Borodin, his wife, daughter and son-in-law, and Oleg Soskovets; Swiss investigation was opened in response to requests made in spring by Russia's chief prosecutor, Yuri I Skuratov, who was subsequently fired by Pres Boris Yeltsin but remains technically in office because Russian Parliament has twice rejected his dismissal; photo (M)
news.title: Swiss Freeze 59 Bank Accounts For Russian Corruption Inquiry

news.abstract: SAARBRUECKEN, Germany—  Out here in what's left of blue-collarland, Gerhard Schroeder, the Brioni chancellor, comes to town to plead he's not really one of the guys in sharp suits who closed the mines and the mills, but a friend whose heart still thumps with Social Democratic compassion.
news.title: At Stake Is His Ability to Maintain Authority and Push Reform : Schroeder Facing Nasty Months

news.abstract: Leaders from 52 countries with French-speaking populations gather in Moncton, New Brunswick, traditional capital of Acadia, and Canada's English press makes much of the fact that a good number of these leaders are among the world's worst human rights violators; Prime Min Jean Chretien addresses summit, called La Francophonie, and says it should give itself the power to purge the undemocratic; photo (M)
news.title: A Meeting of Francophones, With Insults in Plain English

news.abstract: Aramaic, the language of Jesus, survives as language of daily life of Malula, Syrian town of 5,000, and two nearby villages; successive conquerors never bothered to force their languages on this remote community in Qalamum Mountains; scholars visit Malula to study language; photos; map (M)
news.title: Malula Journal; Passing On History by Word of Mouth

news.abstract: argentine chief's tepid sta
news.title: Argentine Chief's Tepid Stand Hobbles His Party's Candidate

news.abstract: news an
news.title: In Mideast, Wariness Mixed With New Hope

news.abstract: State Sec Madeleine K Albright meets in Syria with Pres Hafez al-Assad; Clinton Administration aide says meeting will not lead to immediate resumption of Israeli-Syrian peace talks, but lays groundwork for new talks; says Assad sticks to demand that Israel recognize 1967 border before talks resume; Albright visits Beirut, Lebanon, in effort to show that time is right to widen peace effort to include Syria and Lebanon and that Lebanese Government makes strides in normalizing daily life; meets with Prime Min Selim Hoss and calls for resumption of Israeli-Lebanese talks; photo (M)
news.title: Assad Stands Firm on Conditions for Restarting Talks

news.abstract: Venezuelans have largely hailed moves by Constitutional Assembly loyal to Pres Hugo Chavez to strip opposition-controlled Congress of all its powers and take control of judicial system; Chavez's popularity has risen as result of his drive to eradicate establish order, drive deplored abroad as threat to democracy; sentiment has been building for at least decade against Congress and other state institutions seen as remote and unresponsive; photo (M)
news.title: Venezuelans Applaud Leader's Assault on System

news.abstract: Russian television channel controlled by Boris A Berezovsky, ally of Pres Boris N Yeltsin, plans weekly news program whose host, Sergei Dorenko, is known for attacks on political opponents; program will be aired at same time as long-running weekly program hosted by Yevgeny Kiselyov on channel controlled by Vladimir Gusinsky, who has recently broken with Yeltsin's dwindling team; head-to-head competition is latest skirmish in media war linked to political power struggle; Dorenko recalls both channels scheduled their news programs to avoid competition when both backed Yeltsin, interview; photo (M)
news.title: In Russia, a Power Play Acted Out on Television

news.abstract: Chinese Government announces sweeping increases in salaries, pensions and welfare payments for 84 million people, describing move as a birthday gift as the country prepares to celebrate 50th anniversary of founding of People's Republic; officials clearly hope raises will help their as yet futile attacks on stubborn deflation that has plagued China in its current economic slump (M)
news.title: China Puts More Power in Pockets of the People

news.abstract: Chancellor Gerhard Schroder of Germany suffers rebuff in state elections in Saarland and Brandenburg; in Saarland, Christian Democrats edge out Social Democrats, who have been in power for 15 years, and Peter Muller will take over state premiership from Reinhard Klimmt; far right Deutsche Volksunion takes 5.3 percent of vote and will qualify for parliamentary representation; in Brandenburg, Christian Democrats and Party of Democratic Socialism, which is the former East German Communist Party, each benefit from collapse of Social Democrats; photos; map (M)
news.title: Schroder's Party Is Set Back Painfully in 2 State Elections

news.abstract: Pres Jacques Chirac of France visits Memramcook, New Brunswick, and pledges to renew French support for Acadian people of province; Canada has made Moncton, New Brunswick, site of conference of leaders from 49 foreign nations with French-speaking populations and paints province as a place where French-speakers do not dream of secession but live happily inside federation; Acadians bask in their modern day cultural and economic renaissance; photo; map (M)
news.title: Canada's Other French-Speakers Cope

news.abstract: Islamic militants mount ferocious assault in Russian republic of Dagestan, and a powerful bomb demolishes an apartment building housing Russian officers and their families in Buinaksk, republic's second-largest city; at least 30 people are killed and about 110 wounded in explosion; renewed fighting is unwelcome political test for Vladimir V Putin, Russia's new Prime Minister; photo; map (M)
news.title: Rebels Attack Caucasus Area; Bomb Kills 30

news.abstract: Less than 24 hours after a new Israeli-Palestinian agreement was signed, two cars packed with explosives blew up almost simultaneously in two northern Israeli cities today.    In Tiberias and Haifa, the cars' occupants, presumed to be the unsuccessful bombers, were killed and several passers-by were wounded, one seriously.
news.title: 2 Cars Packed With Explosives Blow Up In Israel, Killing 3 Suspected Terrorists

news.abstract: Center for Popular Promotion and Development, private Peruvian group, is using money from Peruvian Govt and two Dutch foundations in pilot project to relieve pain of children in Ayacucho Province who have been traumatized by Shining Patch guerrilla insurgency; social workers in Vicus and other villages are encouraging children to express joys and fears in friendly classroom setting, where they play mock war games that include guerrilla attacks on villages and successful village militia attacks and army counterattacks; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Vicus Journal; Children at Play Exorcise a Brutal War's Demons

news.abstract: Former US Sen George J Mitchell, who helped broker 1998 Ulster accords, returns to Belfast, Northern Ireland, in effort to break stalemated peace talks between Protestant leaders and Irish Republican Army; says ending impasse is up to feuding political leaders, but that stalemate can be broken; urges political leaders to seize 'best' political opportunity in many years to set province on path to enduring peace and political stability; says he will not renegotiate original settlement, but will focus tightly on disarmament methods and timing and on creating executive Cabinet with members from rival parties to run new Northern Ireland Assembly, power-sharing institution at heart of agreement; impasse centers on disarming Irish Republican Army before assembly begins functioning (M)
news.title: Mitchell Says It's Up to Ulster Political Leaders to Settle Their Feud

news.abstract: Israeli police hold five people in connection with car bombings in Tiberias and Haifa on September 5; indicate suspects were Israeli Arabs; three would-be bombers were killed in blasts; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Arabs Suspected In Car Blasts, Police Hint

news.abstract: Militias backed by Indonesian military, in apparently planned campaign of savagery, continue attacks on people of East Timor who overhwelmingly voted for independence; burn homes, killing residents and forcing many thousand to flee for safety; burn home of Roman Catholic Archbishop Carlos Belo in Dili, evicting 6,000 people taking refuge there and forcing Belo to flee; fire on Australian Consulate; major operation appears under way to force many thousands of people to flee into West Timor, which is part of Indonesia; Indonesian Pres B J Habibie declares martial law in East Timor; Govt releases Jose Alexandre Gusmao, rebel leader arrested seven years ago and is regarded as potential leader of new East Timorese nation; he is turned over to UN officials in Jakarta; says he will do everything in his power to bring peace to East Timor; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Thousands in East Timor Fleeing as Militias Attack

news.abstract: Russian peacekeeping troops fatally shoot three armed Serbs in eastern Kosovo; come under fire after surprising Serbs who had ambushed car killing passenger; Serbs were also beating two wounded Albanians; NATO Sec Gen Javier Solana praises 3,000 Russian peacekeepers in Kosovo; says incident is proof of their professionalism, and that they deserve NATO support (M)
news.title: Russians Kill 3 Serbs in Kosovo Skirmish; Win Praise From NATO

news.abstract: News analysis of political turmoil in East Timor; crisis comes against backdrop of broader crisis of leadership in Indonesia, in which central Govt is weak and fragmented as politicians fight over presidential succession and once-powerful military has become hestiant, angry and divided; while it is clear that irregular militias backed by military are carrying out campaign of terror, less clear is what campaign is meant to achieve and what degree of control Govt in Jakarta has over people waging it; photo (M)
news.title: The Timor Enigma

news.abstract: Pres Boris Yeltsin derides Russian military's handling of Islamic rebellion in Dagestan as inexcusably careless, joining chorus of critics who say nation's commanders appear to have learned nothing from humiliating defeat by rebels in Chechnya three years ago (M)
news.title: Yeltsin Derides His Military For Dagestan 'Carelessness'

news.abstract: Spokesman for UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan reports quarter of East Timor's population has been driven from homes in past four days by militias opposed to independence; says many displaced people who sought refuge in churches and aid agencies are being rounded up and forcibly moved across border to Indonesian West Timor; says thousands of others have fled into hills and forests; UN officials in East Timor say they face emergency with potential catastrophic consequences; most foreigners have been evacuated; remaining 335 UN staff members are trapped in compound in capital of Dili; virtually all relief aid has ended; almost no food is available for emergency distribution and fate of many refugees remains unknown; Security Council gives Indonesian Pres B J Habibie and military commander Gen Wiranto at least 24 more hours to end reign of terror seemingly orchestrated by units of military; East Timor's Roman Catholic Archbishop Carlos Ximenes Belo seeks refuge in Darwin, Australia; was driven from country by armed militias (M)
news.title: U.N. Says a Quarter of East Timorese Have Fled

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and International Monetary Fund separately warn Indonesia that financial aid that has kept country economically afloat for last two years could be suspended if violence in East Timor is not brought under control (M)
news.title: Indonesia Is Warned It Could Lose Western Aid

news.abstract: Deaths of three Israeli Arabs in two car bomb explosions in Hafia and Tiberias on September 5 send shock waves through Israeli Arab communities; perhaps first suicide car-bombing attempt by Israeli Arabs has horrified many Arabs in small community of Mashad, who fear they may all be tarred with same brush as Palestinian militants from West Bank and Gaza; photos; map (M)
news.title: Of Bombs and Israeli Arabs, and Years of Loyalty

news.abstract: United States, seeking to preserve its relationship with Indonesia, is resisting direct threats of economic or military sanctions as Clinton Administration protests chaos in East Timor; Defense Department, which has longstanding ties with Indonesian military, is taking lead in dealing with crisis; Joint Chiefs of Staff chairman, Gen Henry H Shelton, has discussed by phone with Gen Wiranto plan to remove troops from East Timor that have allied selves with anti-independence militias and replace them with soldiers loyal to central Government (M)
news.title: With Other Goals in Indonesia, U.S. Moves Gently on East Timor

news.abstract: Felipe Turover, who worked for Swiss Banca del Gottardo as debt collector in Russia, says he saw credit card bills and photocopies of credit cards bearing signatures of Pres Boris N Yeltsin and his daughters that were provided by Swiss construction company Mabetex Project Engineering, interview; says bank officials described to him Kremlin meeting at which Pavel Borodin and other senior Russian officials accepted money and gifts from Mabetex, which did $1.5 billion worth of work for Kremlin; scores Yeltsin for giving Russia over to corruption and decline; is key figure in Swiss probe; photo (M)
news.title: Accusations of Bribery In the Kremlin Mount Up

news.abstract: Determined clique of Bengali intellectuals is pressing for change in official English spelling of Calcutta to Kolkata, as West Bengal city's name is pronounced in Bengali language; changing of municipal names has become matter of post-colonial pride in India; new names are slowly overtaking old in common usage; map (M)
news.title: Calcutta Journal; Intellectuals' Pursuit: Putting English in Its Place

news.abstract: EUROPE    NETHERLANDS: KEY JUDGE QUITS WAR PANEL -- One of the most senior judges of the Yugoslav war crimes tribunal, Antonio Cassese, will resign next February, the third key figure to quit the United Nations court in recent months. Judge Cassese, an Italian, who has served on the court since its creation in 1993, said he would go back to being a law professor at Florence University, nearly two years before the end of his term. Gabrielle Kirk McDonald, the tribunal president, will leave in November and Louise Arbour, the chief prosecutor, steps down on Sept. 15.   Marlise Simons (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan and Security Council back away from confrontation with Indonesia after Pres B J Habibie and Gen Wiranto beg for more time to quell East Timor violence; Annan suspends for day plan to evacuate UN mission; Security Council, meeting privately, rejects Portugal's plea for open debate; Wiranto, who replaces his commander in East Timor, reportedly has little control in area, which is controlled by officers linked to ex-Pres Suharto's son-in-law, Lt Gen Prabowo Subianto (M)
news.title: As Support for Intervention Grows, Indonesia Persuades U.N. to Delay Evacuation of Mission

news.abstract: United States State Dept report finds that while number of freely elected governments continues to grow throughout world, there are still many countries in which people face harassment, imprisonment or even death for practicing their religion; dept's first annual Report on International Religious Freedom cites Afghanistan, China, Iran, Iraq, Saudi Arabia and Sudan as among most repressive countries (M)
news.title: U.S. Report Details World's Religious Persecution

news.abstract: N Chandrababu Naidu, cyber-savvy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh and India's most dynamic economic reformer, wages his campaign for Parliament not by talking about economic growth, but by speaking traditional language of social programs: marriage halls for Muslims, irrigation canals for farmers, free hand tools for artisans, matching grants to poor women who save money; politicians across India are watching to see whether Naidu's aggressive blend of old-style politicking and new-wave economics gives his party a victory when votes for parliamentary elections are counted on Oct 6; as India's states become more increasingly important in drive for economic growth that is needed to pull hundreds of millions of Indians out of poverty, state leaders like Naidu are at vanguard of efforts to modernize local economies and integrate them into global marketplace; photo; map (L)
news.title: Indian Courts World's Riches and Poor's Vote

news.abstract: Excerpts from Pres Clinton's statement on East Timor; photo (M)
news.title: In Clinton's Words: East Timor, Waco, Clemency Offer, and Other Issues

news.abstract: AUCKLAND, New Zealand—  A meeting of 20 nations on the crisis in East Timor urged Indonesia on Thursday to end the violence in the disputed territory, but stopped short of taking any concrete action.
news.title: APEC Countries Defer to UN on East Timor

news.abstract: Gen Henry H Shelton, Chmn of Joint Chiefs of Staff, discloses that British general in charge of NATO forces in Kosovo, Gen Sir Michael Jackson, refused to obey an order from NATO's supreme commander, Gen Wesley K Clark, an American, to evict Russian troops after their surprise takeover of main airfield there in June; dispute between two commanders was resolved quickly by British and Ameican military leaders in favor of Jackson; Jackson had rejected order from his superior by saying 'No, I'm not going to do that. It's not worth starting World War III'; dispute raises doubts about NATO's chain of command (M)
news.title: U.S. General Was Overruled in Kosovo

news.abstract: United Nations report claims Afghanistan has more than doubled its production of opium in past year and now accounts for three-quarters of world opium crop; jump in production alarms head of United Nations Office for Drug Control and Crime Prevention, Pino Arlacchi; Arlacchi says he told Secretary Gen Kofi Annan that Afghan opium production is spinning out of control; fears Afghan output could flood Western Europe, primary market for heroin refined from Afghan opium (M)
news.title: Afghanistan Opium Record Raises U.N. Fears

news.abstract: A growing number of countries have made it a crime to drive while speaking on a cellular phone, citing evidence that the distraction can pose a serious risk. But in the United States such bans are still limited to one small suburb of Cleveland, Ohio.
news.title: xxx: Crusading Cleveland Suburb Bars Cell-Phoning Drivers

news.abstract: Pres Clinton accuses Indonesian military of direct involvement in savagery that has swept across East Timor and says international peacekeeping force must be allowed to restore order; Pentagon has insisted that there are no plans to send American ground troops to join Australian-led peacekeeping force in East Timor, but now Clinton's security adviser, Samuel R Berger, says nothing has been ruled out; Berger appears to acknowledge that Indonesia's military has muscled aside Pres B J Habibie, who seems unable to control developments in East Timor (M)
news.title: Indonesia Assisting Militias, U.S. Says

news.abstract: Foreign Min Igor S Ivanov of Russia says team of Russian law enforcement officials is going to Washington in effort to prove Moscow's eagerness to cooperate with American inquiries into money laundering; aide to Secretary of State Madeline K Albright says Russian corruption and its effect on international financial system was high on agenda during her recent meeting with Ivanov (S)
news.title: Russian Promises Help From Police

news.abstract: Roger Russell, former miner who is on 2,800-mile walk around South Africa to call attention to nation's notorious crime rate, is himself mugged; this underscores fact that crime has become one of biggest problems in South Africa and issue new Government of Pres Thabo Mbeki is eager to make a priority; Russell decided on his walk against crime after seeing videotape of South African police officers beating up suspect; his walk has two aims: as general protest against crime and to support police officers who are not engaged in brutality; photo; map (M)
news.title: Grabouw Journal; Reality Check for Anti-crime Trekker

news.abstract: Pres Clinton and China Pres Jiang Zemin, in Auckland, New Zealand, for Asian economic summit conference, declare end to months of frozen relations following bombing of Chinese Embassy in Belgrade, and their trade ministers begin meeting in hopes of closing deal that will get China into World Trade Organization this year; Chinese officials are pleased that Clinton has been critical of Taiwan Pres Lee Teng Hui for his statements describing island as separate state (M)
news.title: CLINTON AND JIANG HEAL RIFT AND SET NEW TRADE COURSE

news.abstract: Kazakhstan Pres Nursultan A Nazarbayev, with strategic ties to US at risk over sale of MIG jet fighters to North Korea, orders series of arrests, reforms government's arms export system and dismisses his closest adviser,, Nurtai Abukayev (M)
news.title: To Appease U.S., Kazakh Acts on MIG Sales

news.abstract: Nigeria has ended nearly 16 years of military rule, and its politicians have plunged into new democratic system with typical Nigerian spirit; new lawmakers say they are learning about democracy, and how to build it in diverse country of 110 million people; note that executive branch is headed by Pres Olusegun Obasanjo, military ruler in late 1970's; say creation of Senate and House of Representatives are areas where real progress toward democratization has been made; map; photos of Suleiman Isyaku, one of 360 members of Nigeria's new House (M)
news.title: Nigeria at Dawn of a Democracy Finds Making Laws Is No Picnic

news.abstract: Growing number of Japanese cities are driving out followers of Aum Shinrikyo religious sect by using public money to buy up property owned by doomsday cult (M)
news.title: To Get Cult To Leave, Japan Cities Buy It Out

news.abstract: Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, marking break with caution of German foreign policy since World War II, has laid out new vision of his country's international role, describing Germany as 'great power in Europe' that will not hestitate to pursue its national interests; new definition of German foreign policy appears to signal formal end of Germany's self-imposed reserve even as it underscores country's irreversible attachment to NATO and European Union; Schroder photo (M)
news.title: A New German Assertiveness On Its Foreign Policy Stance

news.abstract: KUALA LUMPUR—  A Canadian journalist has been sentenced by Malaysia's Court of Appeal to six weeks in prison for contempt of court.
news.title: Malaysian Court Jails Foreign Journalist for Contempt

news.abstract: Mcwayizeni Ka Dinizulu, most senior Prince of Zulu people of South Africa, dies at age 67 after long illness (S)
news.title: M. Ka Dinizulu, Zulu Leader, Dies at 67

news.abstract: Mexico's National Action Party, pro-business opposition party, selects Vicente Fox Quesada as its presidential candidate in nationwide primary; outcome makes him candidate for governing Institutional Revolutionary Party to beat in 2000 election; polls show he is most popular challenger to governing party (S)
news.title: With Vote, Mexican Right Gives a Hand To Candidate

news.abstract: American officials say North Korea has tentatively agreed to end its testing of long-range ballistic missiles in exchange for commitment from US and Japan to move forward with economic assistance (S)
news.title: North Korea Said to Agree to End Missile Tests

news.abstract: Momcilo Djujic, Serbian warrior-priest who fought as Chetnik commander in epic World War II battles in Yugoslavia, dies at age 92 (M)
news.title: Momcilo Djujic, Serbian Priest and Warrior, Dies at 92

news.abstract: At least seven people die and hundreds are injured in severe tremor in region of Turkey where more than 15,000 people died in huge earthquake on August 17; tremor was felt in Istanbul, Ankara and Izmir; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Aftershock Hits Turkish Cities Struck by Quake in August

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, in move to reward North Korea for tentatively agreeing to stop testing its new long-range missile, prepares to lift some trade sanctions that have barred commerce between both countries for close to 50 years; gesture revives question raised by Congressional critics of Administration's negotiations with North, of whether President is rewarding hard-line Communist Government for defusing crisis it created (M)
news.title: Clinton Is Ready to Scrap Some North Korea Sanctions

news.abstract: Gen Wesley K Clark, NATO's Supreme Commander, says groups of Serbian paramilitaries are infiltrating back into Kosovo from Serbia, apparently bent on causing trouble three months after Serbian forces withdrew from province (M)
news.title: NATO Commander Says Armed Serbs Are Slipping Back to Kosovo

news.abstract: US, which is seeking to force new weapons inspection program on Iraq, reports new evidence that Pres Saddam Hussein has spent money to build 'sprawling amusement park' to entertain his political followers instead of feeding hungry populace; State Dept releases declassified aerial photographs showing complex near Baghdad; photogrqaphs also substantiate reports that Hussein recently bulldozed villages where anti-Govt protests took place (S)
news.title: As Iraqis Starve, U.S. Asserts, Their Leaders Live in Luxury

news.abstract: KUALA LUMPUR—  President Bill Clinton said Monday that he was "deeply concerned" about the jailing of a Canadian journalist in Malaysia.
news.title: He Criticizes Malaysia for Jailing of Canadian : Clinton Backs Journalist

news.abstract: Presidential advisory panel led by former Defense SecWilliam J Perry has urged Pres Clinton to significantly step up diplomatic and trade ties with North Korea in bid to end North Korean efforts to develop nuclear arms; officials say Clinton has tentatively accepted findings; panel also recommended United States maintain its troop strength in South Korea and remain vigilant to new provocations (M)
news.title: Panel Urges Stepped-Up Attention to Ties With North Korea

news.abstract: Moscow's thousands of dark-complexioned natives of Caucasus Mountains, Muslim or Christian, have become suspects and potential scapegoats in Russia's reaction to suspected terrorist bombings of two apartment buildings; many are staying at home to avoid bullying by police and neighbors; many Moscow residents fear bombings mean conflict in north Caucasus region of Dagestan, where insurgents seek to create Islamic state, has been extended to city; police begin enforcing Mayor Yuri M Luzhkov's requirement that visitors to city re-register, move aimed at people from Caucasus, many of whom live in city without residency permits; photos (M)
news.title: Caught in a Backlash to Moscow's Bombings

news.abstract: China's Communist Party lists 50 approved slogans for celebration marking People's Republic's 50th birthday; slogans are only messages allowed on posters, banners and lips of celebrants (M)
news.title: China to Let 50 Slogans Bloom (a Bit, And Just 50)

news.abstract: Some former American prisoners of war from World War II have filed class-action suit against five major Japanese corporations, holding they were beaten, starved and forced to work in Japanese factories, mines and shipyards; hold they continue to suffer physical and mental problems; Eli J Warach, lawyer for plaintiffs, says suit names Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Mitsubishi International Corp, Mitsui & Co, Nippon Steel and Showa Denko KK; notes many other Japanese companies used prisoners of war as workers (M)
news.title: Ex-P.O.W.'s Sue 5 Big Japanese Companies Over Forced Labor

news.abstract: French Prime Min Lionel Jospin lauds Jose Bove, farmers' union official jailed for leading July demonstration that wrecked McDonald's restaurant building site, television interview; fast-food chain is target of protests over American tariffs on French farm exports imposed because France refuses to import American hormone-treated beef (M)
news.title: Protesters Just Say No To 'McDo'; Jospin Glad

news.abstract: Domingo Cavallo's third-party presidential race could shake up two parties that have dominated Argentina's politics; former Economy Minister, standing at 9 percent in polls, is poised to win bloc of Congressional seats for his new conservative party, making him swing negotiator in Congress and key player in economic policy; he comments, interview (M)
news.title: Respected Economist Struggles to Find Votes in Argentina

news.abstract: Tentative calm prevails in Dili, East Timor's capital, after Security Council vote approving deployment of force of up to 8,000 soldiers and equipment offered by more than dozen countries; United Nations emergency expert able to travel out of capital for first time visits largest concentration of refugees remaining in territory; finds them struggling to survive on rice handouts from military (M)
news.title: U.N. Prepares Peacekeepers As Timorese Fight to Survive

news.abstract: Analysis of German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder's deepening political crisis; central issue is that Germany is running out of money, and proposed deep spending cuts that will affect most Germans are very unpopular; Schroder is trying to change conservative country deeply attached to its habits; his proposed budget, designed to open way for sharp cuts in corporate and personal tax rates, is intended to jolt Germans into rethinking their lives; Schroder is charting course of less state, more personal responsibility, less enveloping social protection, more entrepreneurship; recent election results show public reaction to his plan has been violent; photo (M)
news.title: How Schroder's 'Dip' Is Deepening

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook vignettes from Pres Clinton's trip to New Zealand; notes New Zealanders cheered Clinton in spite of his harsh trade restrictions on New Zealand lamb, while China's President Jiang Zemin, also on visit, was booed because of China's policy on Tibet (M)
news.title: Reporter's Notebook; The Lambasting of Clinton That Didn't Last Long

news.abstract: Clinton Administration discusses which American forces would take part in peacekeeping mission to East Timor; White House says Gen Joseph W Ralston of Joint Chiefs of Staff has met with Indonesian counterpart seeking to insure full cooperation of Indonesian military (M)
news.title: U.S. and Indonesian Generals Discuss Safety of Troops in Timor

news.abstract: In a last attack on the political system he once served, a former Mexican justice official who apparently killed himself on Wednesday rather than face money-laundering charges in the United States blamed Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo for both his own death and the 1994 murder of his brother.    In a suicide note made public by his widow, Mario Ruiz Massieu charged that Mr. Zedillo had never forgiven his criticism of party officials after his brother, a party leader, was killed. He said the evidence against him was fabricated.
news.title: Suicide Note Blames President of Mexico

news.abstract: Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright criticizes Russia's leaders for failing to combat corruption, but defends Clinton Administration policy of supporting aid to Russia; Albright makes some of Administration's sharpest remarks since international investigation of money-laundering allegations surfaced; but her remarks do little to calm criticism in Congress because, for time being, she stops short of threatening to withdraw support for loans from International Monetary Fund; furor in Congress over Russian scandal makes it clear Republicans intend to make it campaign issue in 2000 (M)
news.title: Albright Warns the Russians to Battle Corruption, or Else

news.abstract: ASIA    MYANMAR: 2D BRITON JAILED -- A court sentenced a British democracy activist, Rachel Goldwyn, to seven years in prison at labor for protesting against Myanmar's military Government. Ms. Goldwyn, 28, of London, looked saddened by the sentence, the maximum possible. She was arrested after chaining herself to a lamppost in Yangon on Sept. 7 and shouting pro-democracy slogans. Another Briton, James Mawdsley, who was jailed for 17 years for anti-Government protests on Sept. 2, was allowed his first visit by a British consular official.   (AP, Agence France-Presse)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Venezuela's most unusual radio show is Hello, President, featuring Pres Hugo Chavez taking calls every Sunday morning for two hours from any Venezuelan with a problem, a complaint or a suggestion; Chavez also makes point of discussing his official agenda for coming week, often announcing major policy initiatives on the show; program exemplifies Chavez's notions of what constitutes democracy; he has repeatedly attacked Venezuela's National Congress and state legislatures as unrepresentative bodies out of touch with citizenry; photo (M)
news.title: Caracas Journal; It's Sunday, and Venezuelans Have the Leader's Ear

news.abstract: Foreign troops, ships and planes converge in Darwin, Australia, as international peacekeeping mission prepares to depart for East Timor; soldiers from Britain, Thailand and nine other countries, including small contingent of Americans, will join 4,500 Australian troops (M)
news.title: Timor Peacekeeping Force Gathers in Australia

news.abstract: Geishas, dying breed in Japan, are being replaced by kimono-clad hostesses called furisode-san; photo (M)
news.title: Tokyo Journal; Still Smiling, New Geishas Pour Sake and Charm

news.abstract: Police Chief Alejandro Gertz Manero notes that crime in Mexico City has risen to record levels but bank robberies have fallen (M)
news.title: Mexico City's Bank Robbers Feel Police Chief's Iron Hand

news.abstract: Pres Clinton orders easing of economic sanctions against North Korea in what officials say is first step in long-term plan to induce North to abandon its missile and nuclear programs; announcement--most extensive relaxation of sanctions against North since Korean War--comes four days after North Korea agreed to temporary halt in its tests of long-range missiles; photo (M)
news.title: TRADE SANCTIONS ON NORTH KOREA ARE EASED BY U.S.

news.abstract: Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat sneaks into Israel to meet with Prime Min Ehud Barak and discuss negotiations for permanent peace (M)
news.title: Arafat Slips Across Border For Secret Talks With Barak

news.abstract: Hashim Thaci, political leader of Kosovo Liberation Army, says that Kosovo Albanians want to be represented at United Nations; photo (M)û
news.title: Kosovo Rebels' Political Chief Calls for U.N. Representation

news.abstract: a small flotilla sets sail for mission in east
news.title: A Small Flotilla Sets Sail For Mission in East Timor

news.abstract: United Nations says its relief workers, once protected by their status as neutral do-gooders, have increasingly become targets of violence in troubled lands; says 180 UN workers have been killed on duty since 1992, including at least 141 locally recruited staff members; attacks on UN workers are now used to attract media attention and send political messages (M)l
news.title: U.N.'s Workers Become Targets In Angry Lands

news.abstract: a bully pulpi
news.title: A Bully Pulpit to Restore Lost African Icons

news.abstract: Rachel Goldwyn is sentenced to seven years at hard labor in Myanmar for staging one-person protest against military Government; is second young Briton in two weeks to be harshly sentenced, drawing concern of family members and diplomats and further attention to political repression in former Burma; map (M)
news.title: Burmese Pain In Spotlight As 2 Britons Sent to Prison

news.abstract: Pres Ali Abdullah Saleh has begun drive to stamp out use of khat, mild narcotic leaf chewed by some 80 percent of Yemeni men and 60 percent of women; urges Yemenis to devote khat-chewing time to sports or learning; most Yeminis dismiss suggestion; map; photos (M)
news.title: Khat-Chewing Yemen Told to Break Ancient Habit

news.abstract: PARIS—  Do you fancy digesting the millennium's arrival at the celebrated Tour d'Argent restaurant, gazing down on the living time-capsule Notre Dame cathedral, far from hoi polloi and ceremonial musak? The most intrusive sound will be the rich swish of caviar and vintage crus down elegant gullets. Sound good?
news.title: How to Celebrate the Millennium in Good Company : It's a Date, but Where's the Party?

news.abstract: Kosovo Liberation Army misses midnight deadline for its final disarmament and demobilization as its commanders wrangle with NATO officials over number of weapons its men will be allowed to retain in a civilian force; map (M)
news.title: As Talks Snag, NATO Puts Off Disarming Kosovo Rebels; Dispute Is Over Guns

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  Alarmed at the rise of xenophobic nationalism in Indonesia over its failure to control East Timor, Asian nations are rushing military personnel to Darwin, Australia, so that they can join the multinational force that is expected to start landing in the territory Monday.
news.title: Officials Say Deployment Seeks to Offset Dominant Role by Australia : Asians Move to Join UN Timor Force

news.abstract: Four Britons are identified as suspected Communist agents, bringing to eight the number of people recently acused of being cold war informers and prompting calls on Government to clarify why there have been no prosecutions and whether British security has been undermined; Robin Pearson, postgraduate studies director at Hull University, is identified as informer for East Germany; Vic Allen, retired economics professor at Leeds University, is said to have passed information about Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament to East Germany; Dr Gwyneth Edwards, German-language lecturer at Loughborough University, is accused of having collaborated with East German secret police, the Stasi; Richard Clements, former editor of leftist weekly Tribune and adviser to former Labor Party leader Neil Kinnock, is identified as agent for former Soviet Union; last week, accusations were brought against former Labor members of Parliament Tom Briberg and Raymond Fletcher, former Scotland Yard officer John Symonds, and a suburban London woman, Melita Norwood; unmasking of supposed spies is receiving enormous attention in British press (M)
news.title: New Spy Accusations Captivate British Press

news.abstract: First units of international peacekeeping force, a small contingent of Australians, land in East Timor; they are to be followed by 2,500 soldiers aboard nine warships from Australia, Great Britain and New Zealand gathered offshore; force is expected to grow to about 8,000; mission commander, Maj Gen Peter Cosgrove of Australia, says troops encountered cordial reception by Indonesian military; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Australian Forces Reach East Timor To Aid in Recovery

news.abstract: Indonesia's top military commander, Gen Wiranto, disputes reports of thousands of deaths in East Timor; claims fewer than 100 people have been killed there (S)
news.title: Timor Death Toll Disputed

news.abstract: Vanguard of international peacekeeping force stakes its claim to silent and broken town of Dili in East Timor under gaze of clusters of refugees, sullen Indonesian troops and small, angry groups of militiamen; more than 1,000 Australian soldiers spread out through burned, looted and evacuated city; there is no resistance, but three large fires are set hours after they arrive; photo (M)
news.title: U.N. PEACEKEEPERS STAKE TIMOR CLAIM

news.abstract: Pres Saddam Hussein of Iraq indicates he is unwilling to go along with even most generous of several proposals aimed at establishing new United Nations inspection system; this is fresh blow to prospect of any swift return of weapons inspectors to Iraq's soil; Hussein's tough stance complicates efforts of United Nations Security Council's five permanent members to agree on plan to entice Iraq to allow renewed inspections of its weapons programs (M)
news.title: Iraq Rejects Several Proposals For New Weapon Inspections

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    MEXICO: EXTRADITION BY SWISS -- Authorities in Switzerland have agreed to extradite to Mexico the former chief executive of the holding company that owns Aeromexico and Mexicana Airlines, Gerardo de Prevoisin. Mr. de Prevoisin fled into exile in 1994 as the airlines he bought from the Government in 1988 careered toward bankruptcy, and he was later charged with defrauding the companies of $57.8 million. He has said he donated part of the money to President Ernesto Zedillo's 1994 election campaign.   Sam Dillon (NYT)    COLOMBIA: BISHOP FREED -- A left-wing guerrilla group that kidnapped a Roman Catholic bishop more than a month ago has released the cleric, but is demanding that the Vatican transfer him and another bishop in the region to other dioceses. ''I will not go,'' was the response of the kidnapped bishop, Msgr. Jose de Jesus Quintero, said by the People's Liberation Army to favor right-wing paramilitary groups that have recently become active in the area.   Larry Rohter (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Clinton Administration officials say Federal investigation of money laundering at Bank of New York is examining transactions with bank by people close to Pres Boris N Yeltsin of Russia; Federal Bureau of Investigation has reportedly found transactions involving Pavel P Borodin, head of Yeltsin's property management team, and Leonid Dyachenko, influential political adviser to Yeltsin who is also Yeltsin's son-in-law; Yeltsin's spokesman has previously claimed that neither Yeltsin nor any members of immediate Yeltsin family has foreign bank account; spokesman now says disclaimer did not apply to Yeltsin's in-laws; Borodin has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing, and dismissed allegations against him as politically motivated (M)
news.title: Bank Affair and a Yeltsin Son-in-Law

news.abstract: NATO and United Nations officials release details about force that will replace rebel Kosovo Liberation Army, as guerrillas quietly congratulate themselves on winning deal they wanted; Kosovo Protection Corps will have 3,000 active and 2,000 reserve members; it has been portrayed as civilian by Western officials, but rebels consider it defense force (M)
news.title: Kosovo Rebel Leader Basking In Warmth of Deal's Reception

news.abstract: Over 1,700 people are reported dead and at least 4,400 injured in earthquake that devastated Taiwan on Sept 21; Interior Ministry says at least 30,000 homes have been destroyed; rescuers are trying to reach thousands of people still trapped inside toppled buildings; highways and bridges are impassable to traffic in worst-hit counties near epicenter, Taichung and Nantou; much of island, including sections of Taipei, are in darkness because of power failures; over 1,000 aftershocks are recorded, including one that registers potent 6.8; main quake measured 7.7 and was centered 90 miles south of Taipei; map; photos (M)
news.title: Rescuers Sift Rubble of Taiwan's Cities

news.abstract: NATO defense ministers, meeting in Toronto, Canada, for first time since end of Kosovo air war, agree that European members of alliance have to spend far more money on modern arms and equipment to carry their share of responsibility in war (M)
news.title: European Allies to Spend More on Weapons

news.abstract: United Nations officials say over 2,000 peackeeping troops have arrived in East Timor, most of them from Australia; say they will reach 3,000 by Sept 22, building toward final target of 8,000; map; photo (M)
news.title: East Timorese, First Wary, Then Jubilant, Greet U.N. Troops in Village Near Capital

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, in speech to General Assembly, urges other members of United Nations to strengthen their collective capacity for intervening to prevent kinds of mass killings and ethnic repression that ravaged Kosovo and East Timor, saying that there are limits to what individual nations can accomplish; photo (M)
news.title: Raise Intervention Abilities, Clinton Urges U.N. Members

news.abstract: Street protests intended to oust Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic appear to falter in Belgrade and other Serbian cities on second day, giving some comfort to Government deeply shaken by loss of Kosovo (M)
news.title: Fewer at Anti-Milosevic Rallies, but Leaders Vow to Continue

news.abstract: Concerns about security are delaying start of aid program to help hundreds of thousands of East Timorese refugees in urgent need of food, shelter and medical care; military officials say East Timor remains tense and unpredictable on fourth day of international peacekeeping mission to subdue terrorism; map; photo (M)
news.title: Aid to Timor Delayed by Dangers in Its Terrified Streets

news.abstract: Article on scene in Tali, Taiwan, following Sept 20 earthquake describes efforts to rescue 39 people trapped in rubble of 13-story apartment building; notes that no one knows if any are still alive (M)
news.title: Families of Taiwan's Missing See Little Hope in the Rubble

news.abstract: Growing political power and independence of lowest castes is being felt throughout India; surveys show they are voting in greater proportions than ever before, greater even than upper castes; democracy is leading to greater social equality for people who had been excluded from political power for first four decades of Indian independence; map; photo (M)
news.title: The Lowest Castes in India, Reaching for Power, Shake Up the System

news.abstract: Sec Gen Kofi Annan's call for more active intervention by United Nations when civilian populations are at risk is meeting resistance in General Assembly from China and small but vocal group of nations; China's Foreign Min Tang Jiaxuan says respect for national sovereignty and noninterference are 'basic principles governing international relations' (M)
news.title: China and Others Reject Pleas That U.N. Intervene in Civil Wars

news.abstract: Deputy State Sec Strobe Talbott, Pres Clinton's top Russia expert, testifies before Senate Foreign Relations Committee on corruption in Russia; gives unusually upbeat assessment of widening investigation into allegations of Russian laundering of billions of dollars through American banks and whether top Administration officials turned blind eye to corruption at highest levels of Russian Government; photo (M)
news.title: State Dept. Expert Upbeat About Russian Fund Case

news.abstract: Manhattan District Attorney's Office is looking into now-defunct London law firm, Talbott, Creggy & Company, for clues to genesis of Russian money movements through Bank of New York that are now under Federal investigation (M)
news.title: London Law Firm Is Target Of Russia Banking Inquiry

news.abstract: Russian warplanes bomb Grozny airport in Chechnya and set oil refinery ablaze on outskirts of city, as Kremlin takes its military campaign against Islamic rebels deep into Chechen territory; Russian bombing raids near Chechnya's capital represent a major stepping-up of fighting and signals change of strategy; maps (M)
news.title: Russia Bombs Chechnya Sites; Major Step-Up

news.abstract: Bishop Basil Rodzianko, retired Bishop of Orthodox Church in America who was known for broadcasts oni religious topics that he made from Britain and US to what is now Russia for over three decades, dies at age 84 (M)
news.title: Basil Rodzianko, 84, Bishop in Orthodox Church

news.abstract: Taiwan Government officials say that destruction from earthquake and its aftershocks will significantly reduce Taiwan's economic growth for 1999; warn that repairing the many damaged buildings, highways, power generators and other structures could take years; latest Government tally shows more than 2,100 people were killed and at least 7,800 injured; photo (M)
news.title: Taiwan Begins Looking at Timetable and Cost to Rebuild

news.abstract: Giulio Andreotti, seven-time Italian Prime Minister, is acquitted of conspiring with Mafia in 1979 murder of Carmine Pecorelli, a muckracking journalist, and also of killing him; so are four other co-defendants, some of whom have been convicted of mob-related crimes in other cases; verdict revives soul-searching about country's judicial system and prosecutors' reliance on testimony of turncoat informants (M)
news.title: Ex-Premier Andreotti Acquitted of Mafia Murder Conspiracy
