news.abstract: Hundreds of movements advocating qigong, invisible forces thought to fight disease, continue to operate in China, even as authorities pursue their harsh crackdown on one prominent offshoot, Falun Gong, and step up scrutiny of others; official acceptance of some qigong sects while others are crushed is part of two-decade, often tortuous effort by government to distinguish supposedly scientific, beneficial qigong from practices that are labeled superstitious and then curbed; Falun Gong, officially branded as superstitious 'evil cult,' was banned in July and four of its leaders have been given stiff prison sentences for allegedly telling ill followers that they could dispense with conventional medicine; Chinese officials are aware that mystical cults in past have erupted into huge, disruptive political forces, and that is what they fear; photo (M)
news.title: Health Sects in China Thrive, If Authorities See No Threat

news.abstract: Flights to Ivory Coast resume after first coup in country's 39 years of independence, and dusk-to-dawn curfew is lifted; businesses operate normally, but banks are forbidden to transfer money abroad; Gen Robert Guei, coup's leader, gathers country's political parties and invites them to nominate members for his cabinet, raising hopes that democracy might be restored; but Guei issues subtle warning to political parties to 'avoid troubles'; still in question is how spontaneous military's mutiny was; Gen Guei's junta is full of supporters of Alassane Ouattara, former prime minister who had hoped to run against ousted Pres Henri Konan Bedie, but was being excluded on ground that he was not really citizen of Ivory Coast; there have been no demonstrations demanding Bedie's restoration; map (M)
news.title: Ivory Coast's Leader Offers Signs of Democratic Revival

news.abstract: Russian forces make halting progress in another day of furious street fighting in Chechnya's capital city, Grozny; Russian troops are probing city's outer neighborhoods, dodging land mines and trading artillery fire with guerrillas holed up in trenches and basements; tens of thousands of civilians remain trapped in city, without heat or electricity and in fear for their lives; Chechen president, Aslan Maskhadov, vows that his rebel fighters will defend Grozny to the last man; photos; map (M)
news.title: Russians Attack Chechen Rebels in Mountain Strongholds

news.abstract: EUROPE    GERMANY: KOHL INVESTIGATION -- Prosecutors in Bonn plan a criminal investigation against former Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who has admitted that he kept secret bank accounts and received more than $1 million in undisclosed political contributions while in office. Dismissing demands from even his own party, the Christian Democratic Union, Mr. Kohl has refused to identify the donors. The prosecutor is expected to recommend an investigation on Wednesday; if there is no objection within two days from the head of Parliament, who has already urged an inquiry, work will begin immediately.   Edmund L. Andrews (NYT)    GERMANY: SENDING FOREIGN PRISONERS HOME -- Justice Minister Herta Daubler-Gmelin said foreigners convicted and jailed in Germany should be sent to their home countries to serve their sentences, provided lawful penal systems exist there. Foreigners and immigrants of German ancestry are among the ''marginal groups that often end up in prison'' and thus contribute to overcrowding, she said.   Victor Homola (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Hijacking of Indian Airlines jet is third attempt by militant associates of Masood Azhar, Pakistani cleric jailed in India since 1994 in fight over Indian control of Kashmir, to barter his release; photo (M)
news.title: 3rd Attempt to Free Pakistani Militant

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  Mayor Rudolph Giuliani of New York said Tuesday that the decision by Seattle to cancel New Year's Eve festivities — the first such cancellation in the United States — represented a victory for terrorists, and he vowed that a huge celebration in New York would go on as planned.
news.title: Seattle Cancels a Party On Fears of Terrorism

news.abstract: Russian military, facing heavy rebel resistance, concedes Chechnya fighting could drag on for at least several more months; has begun to prepare public for war that may be longer and messier than expected; map; photo (M)
news.title: Russians See No Quick End in Chechnya

news.abstract: Israel, in another gesture to Hezbollah after renewal of Israeli-Syrian talks, hands over bodies of two of group's guerrillas killed Dec 9 in fighting in southern Lebanon; military conflict continues, with Israeli jets and guerrillas striking targets in area; map (M)
news.title: Israel Hands Over the Remains Of 2 Guerrillas from Hezbollah

news.abstract: Neighbors in Cardenas, Cuba, cling to memory of Elian Gonzalez, 6-year-old boy at center of international tug of war between Cuba and United States immigration authorities; neighbors say they cannot understand why Elian's relatives in Miami are so intent on keeping boy against wishes of his father, Juan Miguel Gonzalez, who wants his son back; photos (M)
news.title: The Boy, 6, From Cuba: So Missed

news.abstract: Hijackers holding 154 hostages in Indian Airlines jet at airport in Afghanistan drop two of their demands, but continue to insist that India release jailed Pakistani Muslim cleric and 35 others whom Indian government considers terrorists opposed to Indian rule in Kashmir; hijackers drop demand that India hand over $200 million and body of slain militant after representatives of Afghanistan's ruling Taliban militia tell hijackers they have violated conditions of landing in Afghanistan by adding demands for money and body; Taliban is playing increasingly important role in efforts to end six-day-old crisis; Indian government, which does not have diplomatic relations with Taliban, nevertheless praised Taliban for its efforts to negotiate with hijackers; map (M)
news.title: Hijackers of Jet End 2 Demands Made to India

news.abstract: Web sites dedicated to the cult of complaint — allowing public- and private-sector employees to vent complaints against cruel, incompetent or even law-breaking bosses — appear to be proliferating on the Internet.
news.title: AMERICAN TOPICS : Complaint About a Boss?There's a Web Site for You

news.abstract: Russia's chief representative in Chechnya, Nikolai Koshman, is visibly troubled by what he sees in Alkhan-Yurt, village near Grozny that residents say was pillaged by Russian troops; tape recording of Koshman's visit to village strongly supports allegations that Russian troops went on rampage, terrorizing civilians, killing some and stealing their goods; at one point Koshman himself is threatened by Russian soldier, who backs down after being told Koshman is top Kremlin aide; Koshman promises to supply food and medicine to people of Alkhan-Yurt, and also promises thorough investigation; Maj Gen Vladimir A Shamanov, whose troops are in Alkhan-Yurt, denies that his soldiers committed any crimes; photo; map (M)
news.title: Russian Outraged at Tapes on Pillage in Chechnya

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    IRAN: LIBERAL TELLS OF ELECTION BAN  The head of the liberal Islamic opposition said all its candidates in the provinces had been barred from running in February's key parliamentary elections. ''It's the first stage in a long battle,'' Ibrahim Yazdi, secretary general of the Iran Freedom Movement, said after newspapers reported that 401 candidates of the 6,860 who applied to run had been rejected by the interior ministry. Mr. Yazdi said he had heard no word about the barring of Freedom Movement candidates in Tehran, where 30 seats are being contested.   (Agence France-Presse)    IRAQ: NEW FERRY LINK  A second ferry line linking Iraq to other nations in the Persian Gulf has opened with the arrival of a car ferry at the Iraqi port of Um Qasr from Bahrain. Iraq, barred from international air traffic under United Nations sanctions, was permitted to open the first ferry link in the gulf last year, from Dubai. The ferries take passengers, cars and some cargo, since each passenger is allowed about 220 pounds of baggage.   Barbara Crossette (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Prime Min Vladimir V Putin says Russian national pride is at stake in war to retake rebellious Chechnya; Russian general say war is intensifying in regional capital of Grozny and along mountain passes to the south, where rebels are dug in; Chechen commanders concede losing ground in Grozny and the mountains, but Pres Aslan Maskhadov vows that Russians will not be able to conquer Chechnya even if the war goes on for 10 years (M)
news.title: Putin Asserts National Pride Is at Stake in Chechnya War

news.abstract: Rabbi Schlomo Gestetner, director of Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies in Jerusalem, a modern Hasidic organization, seeks to exploit millennial excitement without commemorating Jesus by organizing a Y6K benefit concert on New Year's Day, 240 years short of the arrival of sixth millennium of Jewish calendar; Jerusalem will be shut down on New Year's Eve, the Sabbath, and the millennium will be a nonevent for most people there; photo (M)
news.title: On Millennium's Heels, One for Jews

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    ARGENTINA: DRUG CHIEF'S WIDOW INDICTED  A judge has indicted the widow of Pablo Escobar, once leader of Colombia's Medellin drug cartel, on charges of money laundering and froze $10 million of her assets. Prosecutors said Victoria Henao Vallejos has led a money laundering organization in Argentina since she arrived in Buenos Aires almost two years ago using an alias granted by Colombia through a witness protection program.   Clifford Krauss (NYT)    CHILE: EX-PINOCHET AIDES WARNED  The foreign ministry warned 36 former aides to Gen. Augusto Pinochet not to leave Chile, telling them that the Spanish judge who issued the warrant for the former dictator's arrest in London is now planning to prosecute them as well. Foreign Minister Juan Gabriel Valdes told the officials, mostly high-ranking retired military officers, that the government could not protect them from prosecution if they left the country.   Clifford Krauss (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Vatican transfers Bishop Raul Vera Lopez to diocese in Mexican state of Coahuila, taking him from state of Chiapas, where he shared diocese with Bishop Samuel Ruiz Garcia, who has been an ardent advocate of rights of Indians and who hoped Vera would succeed him when he is forced to step down at age 75 (M)
news.title: Mexican Indians Lose Another Church Ally as Bishop Is Moved

news.abstract: Man armed with large knife breaks into house of George Harrison, the former Beatle, in Hensley-on-Thames and stabs him in the chest; Harrison is treated for collapsed lung and various minor stab wounds; Harrison's wife, Olivia, is treated for cuts and bruises she suffered in struggle with intruder; police arrest a man, identified in news media at Michael Abram, and charge him on suspicion of attempted murder; evidence emerges that he may have harbored a dangerous obsession with Beatles; photos (M)
news.title: George Harrison Stabbed in Chest by an Intruder
